text.summary.young: Dachshunds are small dogs with long bodies and short legs that come from Germany. They were bred to chase badgers into underground tunnels — their name even means 'badger dog' in German!

text.summary.young: Rottweilers are strong working dogs from Germany that live all around the world. They were first used by Roman soldiers to herd cattle across Europe over 2,000 years ago — making them one of the oldest herding breeds still around today.
text.summary.tiny: Rottweilers are strong, clever dogs with shiny black coats and tan eyebrows. They love having jobs to do and are wonderfully loyal to their families.

text.summary.young: Siberian Huskies are sled dogs from the frozen lands of Siberia, Russia. They can run over 160 kilometres in a single day through snow and ice, staying warm even when it's colder than a freezer.

fun_facts.young: Goldendoodles are often used as therapy dogs in hospitals because they're so gentle and calm.
Their wavy or curly fur needs to be brushed almost every day to stay fluffy and tangle-free.
A Goldendoodle's nose is always wet, which helps them smell things better.
They love to play fetch and can run and jump for hours without getting tired.
They are great swimmers because both their parent breeds love the water.
Some Goldendoodles work as guide dogs, helping people who can't see.
fun_facts.tiny: Their wavy fur needs brushing almost every day to stay soft and tangle-free.
They're such good swimmers that they'll jump in any puddle they find.
Some Goldendoodles work as helper dogs, visiting hospitals to make people smile.
did_you_know.young: They are a mix of a Golden Retriever and a Poodle.
Their curly coats can be gold, cream, red, or even black.
Some Goldendoodles love water so much they'll jump in any puddle they see.
They're so smart they can learn a new trick in just a few tries.
They come in three sizes: mini, medium, and standard.
text.size_comparison.young: Standing beside you, they reach your belly — around 1 foot 10 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh a little more than you — around 55 pounds.
text.map_narration: Goldendoodles were first bred in North America by crossing Golden Retrievers and Poodles.
text.sound_description.young: They bark when they're excited, whine when they want attention, and sometimes growl playfully when they're playing.

text.summary.young: Persians are fluffy cats with long fur and flat faces that come from Iran. They have been kept as pets for over 500 years — making them one of the oldest cat breeds in the world.
text.summary.tiny: Persians are fluffy cats with flat faces and fur so long it can grow as long as your hand. They've been loved as pets for over five hundred years.
fun_facts.young: Persian cats have the longest fur of any cat breed — it can grow up to 5 inches long!
They almost never jump or climb — they'd rather stay on the ground where it's safe and comfy.
They are so quiet that some owners say they hardly ever hear them meow.
Their eyes are huge and round — almost like they're always surprised!
They love routine — they like eating, playing, and napping at the same time every day.
A Persian's fur is so thick that one cat can have over 100,000 hairs on its body.
fun_facts.tiny: Their fur is so thick that one Persian cat can have more hairs than a hundred thousand!
They almost never jump or climb — they'd rather stay on the ground where it's cosy.
Their eyes are huge and round — like they're always surprised to see you!
did_you_know.young: They need their long fur brushed every single day to keep it from getting tangled.
Their flat faces mean they can't cool down as easily as other cats — so they like to stay in cool places.
They are so calm that they're sometimes called 'furniture with fur' because they love to sit still and look beautiful.
Queen Victoria of England loved Persian cats and helped make them popular around the world.
They can have over 80 different fur colours and patterns — from solid white to striped tabby.
text.size_comparison.young: All that fluffy fur sits only above your knees — around 1 foot 3 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bowling ball — around 11 pounds.
text.map_narration: Persian cats originally come from Persia, which is now called Iran.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft, gentle meows and love to purr when they're being petted.

text.summary.young: Maine Coons are the largest pet cats in the world, originally from Maine in the United States. Some grow as long as a metre and can weigh as much as a small dog!
text.summary.tiny: Maine Coons are the biggest pet cats in the world. Some grow as long as a car door and weigh as much as a Jack Russell!
fun_facts.young: Maine Coons are sometimes called 'gentle giants' because they're so big but so friendly.
They love water and might try to join you in the bath!
They take 3 to 4 years to grow to full size — much longer than other cats.
Their ears have long tufts of fur on top, like a lynx.
They were originally bred to catch mice on farms and ships.
They have thick, shaggy coats that keep them warm in snowy winters.
fun_facts.tiny: They love water and might try to splash in your bath.
Their paws have extra fur between the toes, like built-in snow boots.
They can play fetch just like dogs do.
did_you_know.young: They have special water-resistant fur that helps them swim.
They can play fetch like dogs do!
Their big, fluffy tails help keep them warm in cold weather.
They often chirp and trill instead of meowing.
Their paws have extra fur between the toes — like built-in snowshoes!
text.size_comparison.young: One of the biggest house cats around — right at above your knees, around 1 foot 4 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bowling ball — around 18 pounds.
text.map_narration: Maine Coons come from the state of Maine in the United States.
text.sound_description.young: They chirp and trill more than they meow, making sweet little bird-like sounds.

text.summary.young: Siamese cats come from Thailand and are now loved all over the world. They are one of the most talkative cat breeds and will have loud, raspy conversations with their owners all day long.
text.summary.tiny: Siamese cats talk more than any other cat — they'll chat with you all day long! They come from Thailand and love people so much they follow you everywhere.
fun_facts.young: Siamese cats love to follow their owners around the house like a shadow.
They can learn tricks just like dogs — some even play fetch!
Siamese cats get cold more easily than other cats because their fur is short and thin.
They are very social and don't like being alone for long.
Siamese cats have long, thin bodies and big ears that make them look elegant.
Their loud voices can sound almost like a human baby crying.
fun_facts.tiny: They can learn tricks like dogs and some even play fetch.
Their kittens are born completely white and their dark patches appear as they grow.
They get cold more easily than other cats because their fur's so short and thin.
did_you_know.young: Siamese cats have bright blue eyes that almost seem to glow.
Their fur gets darker on their ears, face, paws, and tail — these are called 'points'.
Their kittens are born completely white and their dark points appear as they grow.
Siamese cats were once considered royal cats in Thailand and lived in palaces with kings and queens.
text.size_comparison.young: Sleek and slender, they stand your knees — around 10 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bag of sugar — around 9 pounds.
text.map_narration: Siamese cats come from Thailand, which used to be called Siam.
text.sound_description.young: Siamese cats make loud, raspy meows that sound almost like they're talking to you.

text.summary.young: Ragdolls are large, fluffy cats bred in California that now live in homes around the world. When you pick them up, they go completely limp and floppy like a cloth doll — that's how they got their name!
text.summary.tiny: Ragdolls are fluffy cats that go completely floppy when you pick them up. They got their name because they relax like a cloth doll in your arms!
fun_facts.young: Ragdolls have silky fur that doesn't mat easily — it feels like rabbit fur!
They often greet you at the door when you come home.
Some Ragdolls love to sleep on their backs with their paws in the air.
They're so calm and gentle that they make great therapy cats in hospitals.
They take up to four years to be fully grown — much longer than other cats!
They got their relaxed personality from careful breeding in the 1960s.
fun_facts.tiny: Their fur feels like stroking a rabbit.
They take four whole years to grow up — much longer than other cats!
Some love sleeping on their backs with their paws in the air.
did_you_know.young: They are one of the largest cat breeds — some males weigh as much as a small dog!
They have beautiful blue eyes that stay bright their whole lives.
They are born white and their colours appear as they grow up.
They love to follow their people from room to room like a shadow.
Many Ragdolls can be trained to play fetch like dogs!
text.size_comparison.young: Soft and floppy, they stand your knees — around 11 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bowling ball — around 15 pounds.
text.map_narration: Ragdoll cats were first bred in California in the United States.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft meows and loud, happy purrs when they're cuddled.

text.summary.young: Bengals are spotted cats with wild leopard ancestry that live in homes around the world. Unlike most cats, they love water and will jump in the shower or splash in their bowls for fun.
text.summary.tiny: Bengals are spotted cats that love splashing in water. They've got wild leopard relatives and shimmer like tiny jungle cats.
fun_facts.young: Bengals are one of the only cat breeds that actually enjoy swimming and playing in water.
Their soft fur feels like silk because it's shorter and smoother than most cats' fur.
They are so energetic they need lots of toys and playtime every single day.
They can jump up to six feet high — that's taller than most grown-ups!
Their kittens are born with fuzzy coats that get spots as they grow up.
These clever cats can figure out how to open doors and cabinets with their paws.
fun_facts.tiny: They can jump as high as your ceiling.
Their fur feels silky smooth, like your softest blanket.
They chirp and chatter like excited birds when they play.
did_you_know.young: Bengal cats have real leopard ancestors — they were bred by mixing wild Asian leopard cats with domestic cats!
Their spotted coat looks like a wild jungle cat, but Bengals are friendly house pets.
They can learn tricks like dogs — they can fetch toys and walk on a leash!
They love to climb so high that owners often find them on top of refrigerators and doors.
Bengal cats chirp and chatter when they see birds outside, making sounds other cats don't make.
text.size_comparison.young: Agile and athletic, they stand your knees — around 10 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bowling ball — around 13 pounds.
text.map_narration: Bengal cats were first bred in the United States by crossing house cats with wild Asian leopard cats.
text.sound_description.young: Bengal cats meow like other cats, but they also chirp and chatter in excited, chatty voices when they play.

text.summary.young: Sphynx cats are hairless cats that come from Canada and now live in homes around the world. They aren't completely bald — they have soft peach-fuzz fur and feel like warm suede when you pet them.
text.summary.tiny: Sphynx cats have no fur at all — they're naked! They feel warm and soft like a fuzzy peach when you touch them.
fun_facts.young: Sphynx cats love to be the center of attention and will show off with silly tricks.
They are amazing jumpers and climbers, leaping to high places like acrobats.
Sphynx cats follow their favorite people everywhere, even into the bathroom.
They sometimes stand on their back legs like little humans to get a better view.
These cats love warmth so much they'll snuggle right up to you or burrow under your blankets.
Sphynx cats are very playful and stay kitten-like their whole lives.
fun_facts.tiny: They follow you everywhere, even into the bathroom.
Sphynx cats get cold easily, so they love to snuggle under blankets.
They jump and climb like tiny acrobats.
did_you_know.young: Sphynx cats get cold easily because they have no fur coat, so they love to cuddle under blankets.
Their skin feels warm to the touch — warmer than most cats — because you can feel their body heat directly.
Sphynx cats need baths more often than furry cats because oils build up on their skin.
They are named after the Great Sphinx of Egypt because of their elegant, mysterious look.
Sphynx cats have huge ears and big lemon-shaped eyes that make them look like little aliens.
text.size_comparison.young: Hairless and sleek, they stand your knees — around 10 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bag of sugar — around 10 pounds.
text.map_narration: Sphynx cats first appeared in Canada when a kitten was born without any fur.
text.sound_description.young: Sphynx cats meow to talk to you, purr when they're happy, and make little chirping sounds when they're excited.

text.summary.young: British Shorthairs are calm, round-faced cats that came from England hundreds of years ago. Their big round eyes and chubby cheeks inspired the smiling Cheshire Cat in Alice in Wonderland.
text.summary.tiny: British Shorthairs have the roundest faces and chubbiest cheeks of any cat. They inspired the smiling Cheshire Cat in Alice in Wonderland!
fun_facts.young: British Shorthairs love to watch what you're doing but don't need to be held all the time.
Their round face and chubby cheeks make them look like they're always smiling.
These cats are excellent mousers and were kept on ships to catch rats.
They can come in over 100 different colors and patterns.
They take three to five years to fully grow up — longer than most cats.
They are called the teddy bears of the cat world because of their soft, thick fur.
fun_facts.tiny: They feel like teddy bears when you stroke them.
They take five whole years to grow up — that's longer than you've been alive!
They love watching you but don't always want cuddles.
did_you_know.young: They are one of the oldest cat breeds in the world.
Their thick, plush coat feels like a teddy bear when you pet them.
They came to England with Roman soldiers almost 2,000 years ago.
They can have orange eyes, blue eyes, or even two different colored eyes.
They often sit like a loaf of bread with their paws tucked underneath.
text.size_comparison.young: Round and sturdy, they stand above your knees — around 1 foot 2 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bowling ball — around 13 pounds.
text.map_narration: British Shorthairs come from Great Britain and are one of the oldest cat breeds.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft meows and quiet purrs, and sometimes chirp when they see birds outside.

text.summary.young: Scottish Folds are cats with unique folded ears that bend forward and down. A barn cat named Susie in Scotland was the first cat born with these special folded ears in 1961.
text.summary.tiny: Scottish Folds have ears that bend forward like little envelopes. The very first one was a barn cat called Susie who lived in Scotland.
fun_facts.young: Scottish Folds make soft, quiet voices and chirp more than they meow.
They love being near their favourite people and will follow them around the house.
They are very good at learning tricks and playing fetch.
Their folded ears come in different levels — some fold just a little, others fold completely flat.
These cats are calm and gentle, making them perfect indoor companions.
They get along well with children and other pets because of their sweet nature.
fun_facts.tiny: They chirp and trill more than they meow.
They sit in silly positions with their legs stretched out like little people.
Some are born with folded ears and some with straight ears.
did_you_know.young: Not all Scottish Fold kittens are born with folded ears — some have straight ears!
They love to sit in funny positions, like on their bottoms with their legs stretched out.
The fold in their ears is caused by a natural change in their genes.
They often sleep on their backs with their paws in the air.
These cats are known for their round faces and big, owl-like eyes.
text.size_comparison.young: With those cute folded ears, they stand your knees — around 10 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bag of sugar — around 10 pounds.
text.map_narration: Scottish Folds come from Scotland, where the very first one was a barn cat named Susie.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft meows and gentle chirping sounds, and they purr loudly when they're happy.

text.summary.young: Russian Blues are quiet, gentle cats with shimmery blue-grey fur that came from Russia long ago. Their double coat is so thick and plush that you can draw patterns in it with your finger — and the patterns stay there!
text.summary.tiny: Russian Blues have shimmery blue-grey fur so thick you can draw patterns in it with your finger. They're quiet, gentle cats who came from snowy Russia long ago.
fun_facts.young: Russian Blues love playing games but prefer calm, quiet playtime.
Their thick double coat kept them warm in freezing Russian winters.
They are very tidy cats and don't like messy spaces.
They can be shy with strangers but are very loyal to their family.
Their fur is naturally water-resistant because of its thick double layers.
These cats are excellent hunters and love chasing toy mice indoors.
fun_facts.tiny: Their thick fur kept them warm in freezing Russian winters.
They are very tidy cats who don't like messy spaces.
They're excellent hunters and love chasing toy mice indoors.
did_you_know.young: They have bright green eyes that glow like emeralds.
Their fur looks silver in the light because each hair has a silver tip.
They are very quiet and don't meow much — they use tiny soft voices.
They often choose one favourite person in the family and follow them everywhere.
They came from the snowy port city of Arkhangelsk in Russia.
text.size_comparison.young: Elegant and quiet, they stand your knees — around 10 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bag of sugar — around 10 pounds.
text.map_narration: Russian Blues come from the port city of Arkhangelsk in northern Russia.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft, quiet meows and gentle purring sounds.

text.summary.young: Abyssinians are active, playful cats from Ethiopia with short ticked coats. They are one of the oldest cat breeds and may have lived with ancient Egyptians thousands of years ago.
text.summary.tiny: Abyssinians are playful cats with shimmery golden fur. They might be related to cats who lived with ancient Egyptians thousands of years ago.
fun_facts.young: Abyssinians have large pointed ears that help them hear even tiny sounds.
They are one of the most athletic cat breeds and can jump very high.
They come from a country that used to be called Abyssinia — now it's called Ethiopia.
Their ancestors may have been the cats worshipped in ancient Egypt.
They love to play fetch just like dogs do.
They are always moving and exploring — they rarely sit still for long.
fun_facts.tiny: They're one of the jumpiest cats — they can leap higher than your bed.
Their fur has special stripes on every single hair.
They love to play fetch just like dogs do.
did_you_know.young: They love to climb to the highest spot in any room.
Their coat has a special pattern called 'ticking' where each hair has different colored bands.
They are sometimes called 'Aby cats' for short.
They are very curious and will investigate every corner of your home.
They often follow their owners from room to room like a shadow.
text.size_comparison.young: Active and curious, they stand your knees — around 10 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bag of sugar — around 9 pounds.
text.map_narration: Abyssinian cats are one of the oldest breeds, first brought to England from East Africa.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft meows and chirping sounds when they're curious about something.

text.summary.young: American Shorthairs are friendly cats that live in homes all around the world. They came to America on the Mayflower in 1620 to catch mice and protect the ship's food.
text.summary.tiny: American Shorthairs are friendly cats with soft fur and round paws. They sailed to America on ships long ago, catching mice to keep everyone's food safe.
fun_facts.young: American Shorthairs have very strong jaws for catching mice.
Their thick fur keeps them warm in cold winter weather.
These cats love to play but also enjoy quiet nap times.
They are great with kids and other pets.
They rarely meow unless they really need something.
Their paws are big and round like little snowshoes.
fun_facts.tiny: Their paws are big and round like little snowshoes.
They purr so loudly you can hear it across the room.
They can live as long as you'll be in school — twenty whole years!
did_you_know.young: They sailed on the Mayflower with the Pilgrims over 400 years ago.
They were working cats who caught mice on ships and farms.
They can live for 20 years — that's longer than most dogs!
They come in more than 80 different colors and patterns.
They are one of the most popular cat breeds in America.
text.size_comparison.young: Sturdy and easygoing, they stand your knees — around 10 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bowling ball — around 11 pounds.
text.map_narration: American Shorthairs came to North America on ships from Europe, catching mice along the way.
text.sound_description.young: They meow softly when they want attention and purr loudly when they're happy.

norwegian_forest_cat.name: Norwegian Forest Cat
norwegian_forest_cat.habitat: Originally from Norwegian forests, now found in homes worldwide

text.summary.young: Norwegian Forest Cats are fluffy cats from Norway with thick, waterproof fur that keeps them warm in snowy forests. In old Norse stories, giant cats like these pulled the goddess Freya's magical chariot across the sky.
text.summary.tiny: Norwegian Forest Cats have thick, waterproof fur that keeps them cosy in snowy forests. Long ago, people in Norway told stories about giant cats like these pulling a goddess's magical chariot across the sky.
fun_facts.young: Norwegian Forest Cats are sometimes called 'Wegies' for short.
Their thick fur forms a fluffy ruff around their neck, like a lion's mane.
These cats have long, bushy tails they can wrap around themselves like a blanket.
They take up to five years to grow into their full adult size and fluffiness.
They have tufts of fur between their toes that keep their paws warm in the snow.
They are excellent hunters and can catch mice, birds, and even fish.
fun_facts.tiny: They've got fluffy fur around their neck like a lion's mane.
Their big, furry paws work like snowshoes so they don't sink in deep snow.
They can climb down trees headfirst, just like squirrels.
did_you_know.young: They have two layers of fur — a fluffy undercoat and a waterproof top coat that sheds rain and snow.
Their big, furry paws work like snowshoes to help them walk on deep snow without sinking.
They are amazing climbers and can climb down trees headfirst, just like squirrels.
These cats didn't come to America until the 1970s, but they've lived in Norway for hundreds of years.
They love cold weather and often choose to sleep outside even when it snows.
text.size_comparison.young: Even this big fluffy cat only stands your knees — around 1 foot at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bowling ball — around 15 pounds.
text.map_narration: Norwegian Forest Cats come from the cold forests of Norway, where Vikings kept them on their ships.
text.sound_description.young: They meow softly, purr loudly when happy, and make little chirping sounds when they see birds.

text.summary.young: Birmans are gentle cats with silky fur and blue eyes that originally came from Burma. Their white paws look like they're wearing little socks — legend says this was a gift from a goddess to honour a temple cat.
text.summary.tiny: Birmans have white paws that look like tiny socks and blue eyes that sparkle like jewels. People say a goddess gave them those magical white feet long ago.
fun_facts.young: Birman kittens are born almost all white and their colour appears as they grow.
Their white paws are called 'gloves' on their front feet and 'laces' on their back feet.
They have soft voices and rarely meow loudly.
They love to sit on laps and be near their family.
They are called the 'Sacred Cat of Burma' because of temple legends.
Their fur feels like rabbit fur — super soft and smooth.
fun_facts.tiny: Their kittens are born nearly white and their colours appear as they grow.
Their fur feels as soft as a bunny's.
They follow you from room to room like a gentle shadow.
did_you_know.young: They always have four white paws that look like tiny socks.
Their blue eyes stay bright blue their whole life.
They were sacred temple cats in Burma hundreds of years ago.
Their fur is silky and doesn't tangle as much as other long-haired cats.
They love to follow their people from room to room.
text.size_comparison.young: Gentle and silky, they stand your knees — around 10 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bowling ball — around 11 pounds.
text.map_narration: Birman cats are said to have come from the temples of Burma, which is now called Myanmar.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft, gentle meows and love to purr when they're happy.

text.summary.young: Savannah Cats are a special breed created by mixing a pet cat with a wild African serval. They can jump over 2.5 metres straight up — that's taller than most grown-ups!
text.summary.tiny: Savannah Cats can jump higher than your grown-up's head in one leap! They're special cats made by mixing a pet cat with a wild cat from Africa.
fun_facts.young: A Savannah Cat can jump from the floor to the top of your refrigerator in one leap!
They follow their favourite people from room to room like a puppy.
Savannah Cats make chirping sounds instead of regular meows.
Their spotted coats look just like a wild leopard's fur.
Some Savannah Cats will play fetch and bring toys back to you.
They are so smart they can learn to open doors and cupboards.
fun_facts.tiny: They can leap from the floor right to the top of your fridge.
They make chirping sounds like little birds.
They follow you everywhere like a puppy does.
did_you_know.young: They can jump higher than any other pet cat — they can leap over 2.5 metres straight up!
Unlike most cats, Savannah Cats love water and will even play in the bathtub.
They can be walked on a leash just like dogs.
They have large, tall ears like their wild serval relatives.
They are one of the biggest pet cat breeds in the world.
text.size_comparison.young: Tall for a cat, they stand above your knees — around 1 foot 3 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a big watermelon — around 20 pounds.
text.map_narration: Savannah cats were first bred in the United States by crossing house cats with wild African servals.
text.sound_description.young: They make chirping sounds like birds and sometimes meow in a high voice.

text.summary.young: Devon Rex cats have short, curly fur and big ears that make them look like little elves. They love learning tricks and following their people around like playful puppies.
text.summary.tiny: Devon Rex cats have curly fur and huge ears like tiny elves. They follow you everywhere and love learning tricks.
fun_facts.young: Devon Rex cats wag their tails when they're happy — just like dogs!
They can learn to fetch, sit, and even walk on a leash.
Their fur feels soft like suede or velvet.
Devon Rex cats love warm places — you'll find them on radiators or under blankets.
They're very social and don't like being alone for long.
Their big ears help them hear everything happening in the house!
fun_facts.tiny: They wag their tails when they're happy — just like dogs!
Their fur feels soft like velvet.
They love warm spots and snuggle under blankets to stay cosy.
did_you_know.young: Devon Rex cats are sometimes called 'poodle cats' because of their curly fur.
Their whiskers are short and curly too — sometimes they break off!
Devon Rex cats get cold easily because their fur is so thin.
They love to perch on your shoulders like a parrot.
The first Devon Rex was discovered in England in 1960.
text.size_comparison.young: This little cat stands only your knees — around 1 foot at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bag of sugar — around 8 pounds.
text.map_narration: Devon Rex cats first appeared in Devon, England, where a curly-coated kitten was born on a farm.
text.sound_description.young: Devon Rex cats meow softly, purr loudly when happy, and make little chirping sounds when excited.

cornish_rex.name: Cornish Rex
cornish_rex.habitat: Homes worldwide, especially cozy spots near warmth

text.summary.young: Cornish Rex cats are playful, curly-coated cats from Cornwall, England. Their soft, wavy fur has no outer layer — it feels like warm velvet and makes them love snuggling for heat.
text.summary.tiny: Cornish Rex cats have soft, curly fur that feels like velvet. They love warmth and will snuggle up close to stay cosy.
fun_facts.young: Cornish Rex cats have huge ears that help them hear everything going on around them.
They love being up high and will perch on your shoulders like a parrot.
Their wavy coat comes in every color and pattern you can imagine.
They are one of the most mischievous cat breeds — they love getting into playful trouble.
They often use their paws like little hands to grab toys and open cabinets.
The first Cornish Rex was born on a farm in Cornwall in 1950 and surprised everyone with its curly coat.
fun_facts.tiny: Their enormous ears can hear the tiniest sounds across the room.
They jump and climb like acrobats and love perching on your shoulders.
They're playful their whole lives and never stop acting like kittens.
did_you_know.young: Cornish Rex cats love to play fetch like dogs do.
Their curly whiskers match their wavy fur all over their body.
They stay playful and kitten-like their whole lives.
Cornish Rex cats get cold easily because their special fur doesn't trap heat well.
They can jump incredibly high and love climbing to the tallest spots in the house.
text.size_comparison.young: With their wavy coat and long legs, they only reach your knees — around 9 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bag of sugar — around 8 pounds.
text.map_narration: Cornish Rex cats first appeared in Cornwall, England, when a curly-coated kitten was born in a litter.
text.sound_description.young: Cornish Rex cats meow softly to chat with you and purr loudly when they're happy and warm.

text.summary.young: Oriental Shorthairs are slender cats with huge ears and almond-shaped eyes that were bred in the United Kingdom. They come in over 300 different colour and pattern combinations — more than any other cat breed in the world.
text.summary.tiny: Oriental Shorthairs have ears as big as satellite dishes and they never stop talking. They come in more colours and patterns than any other cat in the world.
fun_facts.young: Oriental Shorthairs can come in solid colours, stripes, spots, and even swirly patterns.
They are incredibly curious and will investigate every corner of your home.
These cats love to play fetch just like dogs do.
They need lots of attention and don't like being left alone for long.
They are excellent climbers and love to perch on high places.
Their sleek, short coat feels like silk when you pet it.
fun_facts.tiny: They follow you everywhere like a shadow with whiskers.
Their fur feels as smooth as your favourite blanket.
They can leap higher than your bedroom doorway.
did_you_know.young: They are one of the most talkative cat breeds — they love to chat with their owners all day long.
Their enormous ears can be as wide as the base of their head.
They are incredibly athletic and can jump up to six times their own height.
They are sometimes called 'dogs in cat suits' because they follow their owners everywhere.
They have the same body shape as Siamese cats but come in hundreds of different colours.
text.size_comparison.young: Long and lean, they stand your knees — around 11 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bag of sugar — around 9 pounds.
text.map_narration: Oriental Shorthairs were bred in England by crossing Siamese cats with other breeds.
text.sound_description.young: They meow, chirp, and purr constantly to talk to their owners — they're famous for being very chatty cats.

turkish_angora.name: Turkish Angora
turkish_angora.habitat: Homes worldwide, originally from Ankara, Turkey

text.summary.young: Turkish Angoras are graceful long-haired cats that come from Turkey, where they are considered a national treasure. Unlike most cats, Turkish Angoras actually love water and are natural swimmers!
text.summary.tiny: Turkish Angoras are beautiful cats with long silky fur from Turkey. They love water and might jump in your bath!
fun_facts.young: Turkish Angoras love playing in water — they might even join you in the bathtub!
Their silky coat doesn't tangle easily, even though it's so long and fluffy.
They are very talkative and will have conversations with you.
They can learn tricks like sitting, high-fiving, and coming when called.
They were first brought to Europe in the 1500s as royal gifts.
These cats stay playful and kitten-like their whole lives.
fun_facts.tiny: Their fluffy coat never gets tangled.
They're chatty cats who'll meow back at you.
They stay playful like kittens their whole lives.
did_you_know.young: They are one of the oldest cat breeds in the world.
Many Turkish Angoras have one blue eye and one amber eye.
In Turkey, white Turkish Angoras with blue eyes are protected because they are so rare and special.
They can learn to play fetch just like dogs!
These cats are smart enough to figure out how to open doors and cabinets.
text.size_comparison.young: Graceful and slender, they stand above your knees — around 1 foot 2 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bag of sugar — around 9 pounds.
text.map_narration: Turkish Angoras come from Ankara, Turkey, and are one of the most ancient cat breeds.
text.sound_description.young: They are very vocal cats that meow, chirp, and purr to talk with their families.

rabbit.name: Rabbit
rabbit.habitat: Meadows, forests, gardens, and grasslands worldwide

text.summary.young: Rabbits are gentle, fluffy animals with long ears and powerful back legs. They can't vomit, so they have to be very careful about what they eat!
text.summary.tiny: Rabbits have long ears that can hear danger from far away and powerful back legs for hopping fast. They can't be sick like you can, so they're very careful what they munch!
fun_facts.young: Rabbits thump their back feet on the ground to warn other rabbits about danger.
A rabbit can run up to 45 miles per hour — that's faster than a car in your neighborhood!
They are most active at dawn and dusk, not in the middle of the day.
Wild rabbits live in underground tunnels called warrens with their families.
They groom themselves like cats do, licking their paws and cleaning their faces.
A rabbit's nose can wiggle 20 times per second when they're sniffing something interesting!
fun_facts.tiny: They thump their back feet on the ground to tell their friends danger's coming.
A rabbit can run faster than the cars on your street.
Wild rabbits live together in underground tunnels with lots of rooms.
did_you_know.young: When rabbits are really happy, they jump and twist in the air — it's called a 'binky'!
They have eyes on the sides of their heads so they can see almost all the way around without turning.
A rabbit's teeth never stop growing, so they need to chew hay and grass to keep them short.
They can sleep with their eyes open to watch for danger.
Baby rabbits are called kittens or kits — just like baby cats!
text.size_comparison.young: Tiny and fluffy, they only stand your knees — around 10 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bag of sugar — around 4 pounds.
text.map_narration: Wild rabbits live all over the world, but pet rabbits were first kept in France and Spain.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft purring sounds when they're happy and thump their back feet when they're worried.

text.summary.young: Hamsters are small rodents that originally came from Syria and the Middle East. Their cheek pouches can stretch to three times the size of their head to carry food back to their burrows.
text.summary.tiny: Hamsters have cheeks that stretch like magic bags to carry food. They can make their head look three times bigger by stuffing seeds inside!
fun_facts.young: Hamsters wash their faces with their tiny paws just like cats do.
A hamster can remember where it hid food weeks ago.
Baby hamsters are born without any fur and their eyes stay closed for two weeks.
They have terrible eyesight but an amazing sense of smell.
Wild hamsters travel several kilometres each night looking for food.
They have scent glands on their hips that they rub on things to mark their territory.
fun_facts.tiny: They wash their tiny faces with their paws just like cats do.
They can remember where they hid food weeks and weeks ago.
Baby hamsters are born pink with no fur and their eyes stay shut for two whole weeks.
did_you_know.young: They can run up to 8 kilometres every night on their wheel.
Wild hamsters dig tunnels underground with separate rooms for sleeping and storing food.
A hamster's teeth never stop growing, so they chew on things to keep them short.
They are nocturnal, which means they sleep during the day and wake up at night.
They can stuff so much food in their cheeks that their head looks three times bigger.
text.size_comparison.young: They are small enough to fit right in your cupped hands!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about the same as an apple — so light you can hold them easily.
text.map_narration: Hamsters originally come from the deserts of Syria and other parts of the Middle East.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft squeaking and chirping sounds to communicate.

guinea_pig.name: Guinea Pig
guinea_pig.habitat: Pet homes worldwide, originally from South American mountains

text.summary.young: Guinea pigs are small, gentle rodents originally from South America that now live as beloved pets around the world. They make over 11 different sounds to talk to each other — including a loud 'wheek wheek' when they hear food being opened!
text.summary.tiny: Guinea pigs jump straight up and twist when they're happy! They make over 11 different sounds to chat with their friends.
fun_facts.young: Guinea pigs 'popcorn' when they're happy — they jump straight up in the air and twist!
Their teeth never stop growing, so they need to chew on hay all day to keep them short.
They can't make their own vitamin C, so they need fresh vegetables every day.
They have four toes on their front feet but only three toes on their back feet.
They can recognize their owner's voice and come running when called.
They purr like cats when they're happy and content!
fun_facts.tiny: They've got four toes on their front feet but only three on their back feet.
Their teeth never stop growing — they chew hay all day to keep them short.
They can tell your voice from everyone else's and come running when you call.
did_you_know.young: They aren't pigs at all — they're rodents related to chinchillas and capybaras!
They aren't from Guinea either — they come from the mountains of South America.
They sleep with their eyes open so they can watch for danger.
A baby guinea pig is called a pup, and it can run around just hours after being born!
They live in groups called herds and get lonely if they live alone.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a school ruler — they fit perfectly on your lap.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a carton of milk — around 2 pounds.
text.map_narration: Guinea pigs originally come from the mountains of South America.
text.sound_description.young: They wheek loudly when excited, purr when happy, and make soft chirping squeaks to talk to their friends.

text.summary.young: Ferrets are long, bendy carnivores kept as pets all around the world. They make a happy chuckling sound called 'dooking' and do a wild bouncy 'war dance' when they play.
text.summary.tiny: Ferrets are long and bendy and love to play. They make a happy chuckling sound called dooking.
fun_facts.young: Ferrets love to steal and hide shiny things like keys and socks.
They can run backwards almost as fast as forwards.
They have a musky smell that some people love and some people don't.
Their spine is so bendy they can turn around inside a narrow tube.
They are related to otters, weasels, and badgers.
They can be trained to do tricks like dogs — some even walk on leashes!
fun_facts.tiny: They love to steal shiny things like keys and hide them.
They sleep more than cats — about as long as you sleep plus another whole day!
Their spine bends so much they can turn around inside a tube.
did_you_know.young: They sleep up to 18 hours a day — that's more than a cat!
A group of ferrets is called a business.
They can squeeze through any hole their head fits through.
People used ferrets to hunt rabbits hundreds of years ago.
Baby ferrets are called kits and are born deaf and blind.
text.size_comparison.young: Long and stretchy — about as long as your arm from shoulder to fingertips!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a carton of milk — around 2 pounds.
text.map_narration: Ferrets were first kept as pets in Europe over two thousand years ago.
text.sound_description.young: They make a happy chuckling sound called dooking when they're excited or playing.

chinchilla.name: Chinchilla
chinchilla.habitat: Rocky mountain slopes in South America

text.summary.young: Chinchillas are small, fluffy rodents from the cold mountains of South America. Their fur is the softest of any land animal — they have about 60 hairs growing from each tiny spot where humans have just one!
text.summary.tiny: Chinchillas have the softest fur in the world. About 60 hairs grow from each tiny spot where you have just one!
fun_facts.young: Chinchillas eat plants, bark, and seeds with their strong front teeth that never stop growing.
They use their long whiskers to feel their way around in the dark mountain caves where they live.
Baby chinchillas are called kits and are born with fur and open eyes.
They can release patches of fur if a predator grabs them, helping them escape.
They make happy chirping sounds when they're excited or playing with friends.
They groom themselves and each other by nibbling gently with their tiny teeth.
fun_facts.tiny: They take baths in dust instead of water to keep their fur fluffy.
They can jump higher than most grown-ups.
Baby chinchillas are born with their eyes already open.
did_you_know.young: They take baths in special volcanic dust instead of water to keep their fur clean and fluffy.
A chinchilla can jump over six feet high — that's taller than most grown-ups!
They can live for 20 years, which is very long for such a small animal.
Their fur is so thick that fleas and other bugs can't live in it.
They sleep during the day and wake up at night to play and eat.
text.size_comparison.young: About the size of a football — a fluffy, bouncy ball of fur!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a loaf of bread — around 1 pound.
text.map_narration: Chinchillas come from the rocky mountains of South America, high up in the Andes.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft chirping and squeaking sounds when they're happy, and quick barking sounds when they're scared.

text.summary.young: Gerbils are small, curious rodents originally from the deserts of Mongolia. They dig amazing underground tunnels with separate rooms for sleeping, storing food, and even going to the bathroom.
text.summary.tiny: Gerbils are tiny desert explorers with long tails that help them balance when they jump. They dig underground homes with different rooms for sleeping, eating and even a bathroom.
fun_facts.young: Gerbils groom each other to show friendship and keep their fur clean.
A gerbil can live its whole life without taking a bath — they clean themselves!
They love to chew because their teeth never stop growing.
Wild gerbils live in family groups of up to 20 gerbils in one burrow system.
They are most active at dawn and dusk, not during the day or night.
A gerbil can remember complex tunnel maps and find its way home underground.
fun_facts.tiny: A gerbil's teeth never stop growing, so they love to chew on things to keep them short.
They thump their back feet on the ground to tell their friends when danger's coming.
They can jump as high as a stack of books — that's amazing for such a small animal.
did_you_know.young: They can jump up to 12 inches high — that's like you jumping over a house!
A gerbil's tail helps it balance when it jumps and runs.
They hardly ever need to drink water because they get moisture from their food, just like in the desert.
They thump their back feet on the ground to warn their friends about danger.
text.size_comparison.young: Small enough to sit in the palm of one hand!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as an egg — so light you'd barely feel them.
text.map_narration: Gerbils originally come from the deserts and grasslands of Mongolia and China.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft squeaking and chirping sounds to talk to each other, and thump their back feet when they're excited or scared.

mouse.name: Mouse
mouse.habitat: Houses, fields, forests, and cities worldwide

text.summary.young: Mice are tiny rodents with long tails that live almost everywhere in the world. Male mice sing love songs to female mice, but the songs are too high-pitched for human ears to hear!
text.summary.tiny: Mice are tiny animals with long tails that live almost everywhere. They sing love songs too high for you to hear!
fun_facts.young: Mice are fantastic climbers and can run up walls and along wires.
A mouse's heart beats about 600 times every minute — that's ten times faster than yours!
Mice are very clean animals and groom themselves many times each day.
Mice have poor eyesight but amazing senses of smell, hearing, and touch.
Baby mice are called pinkies because they're born without fur and look pink.
Mice communicate with each other through squeaks, chirps, and those special ultrasonic songs.
fun_facts.tiny: A mouse's heart beats ten times faster than yours.
Mice can run up walls and along wires.
Baby mice are called pinkies because they're born pink and furless.
did_you_know.young: Mice can squeeze through holes as small as a pencil because their bodies are so bendy.
A mouse's teeth never stop growing, so they have to chew all the time to keep them short.
Mice are amazing jumpers — they can leap almost a foot high into the air!
Mice use their long whiskers to feel their way around in the dark.
A group of mice is called a mischief!
text.size_comparison.young: Tiny enough to curl up inside a teacup!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh less than a single cookie — you'd barely feel one in your hand.
text.map_narration: House mice have followed people all around the world for thousands of years.
text.sound_description.young: Mice make tiny squeaking and chirping sounds that we can hear, plus special ultrasonic songs that are too high for human ears.

rat.name: Rat
rat.habitat: Cities, farms, homes, and wild areas worldwide

text.summary.young: Rats are clever rodents with long tails that live almost everywhere in the world. They giggle at a frequency humans can't hear when they're tickled or playing with friends.
text.summary.tiny: Rats are clever animals with long tails that live almost everywhere in the world. They giggle when they're tickled but you can't hear it!
fun_facts.young: A rat's teeth never stop growing, so they have to chew on things to keep them short.
Rats are super clean animals and spend hours every day grooming themselves and their friends.
They can squeeze through holes as small as a quarter because their bodies are very bendy.
They have excellent memories and can remember paths through mazes for months.
Pet rats love to play games like hide-and-seek and chase with their human friends.
They use their long whiskers to feel their way in the dark and sense danger.
fun_facts.tiny: A rat's teeth never stop growing so they chew to keep them short.
They spend hours grooming themselves and their friends to stay clean.
They can squeeze through holes as small as your finger because their bodies are so bendy.
did_you_know.young: They laugh when you tickle them, but the sound is too high for human ears to hear.
They can learn their names and come when you call them, just like dogs.
They grind their teeth when they're happy — it's called bruxing and it sounds like chattering.
Some rats are trained to sniff out hidden landmines to keep people safe.
They are so smart they can learn tricks like fetching, spinning, and jumping through hoops.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a banana from nose to tail!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a can of beans — around 12 ounces.
text.map_narration: Rats originally come from Asia but now live on every continent except Antarctica.
text.sound_description.young: They make high-pitched squeaking and chirping sounds, and grind their teeth in a happy chattering called bruxing.

text.summary.young: Hedgehogs are small spiky mammals that live in gardens, forests, and grasslands across Europe, Africa, and Asia. They are immune to many snake venoms and can even eat poisonous snakes without getting hurt.
text.summary.tiny: Hedgehogs have thousands of sharp spines all over their backs. They curl up into a prickly ball when they're scared.
fun_facts.young: Hedgehogs snuffle and snort as they hunt for food at night.
Their spines are actually modified hairs made of keratin.
A hedgehog can run as fast as you can walk.
They sleep during the day and hunt at night.
They have been around for 15 million years.
Each spine can move independently to protect the hedgehog from any direction.
fun_facts.tiny: They snuffle and snort as they hunt for beetles at night.
They've been living on Earth for millions and millions of years.
A hedgehog can run as fast as you walk.
did_you_know.young: They have about 5,000 spines on their back.
When scared, a hedgehog rolls into a tight spiky ball.
Baby hedgehogs are called hoglets.
They can swim and climb surprisingly well.
They eat slugs, beetles, and other garden pests.
text.size_comparison.young: When they curl up into a ball, they fit right in both your cupped hands!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a loaf of bread — around 1 pound.
text.map_narration: Hedgehogs live across Europe, Africa, and Asia — they love gardens and woodlands.
text.sound_description.young: They snuffle, snort, and grunt as they search for food in the grass.

text.summary.young: Parakeets, also called budgies, are small colorful parrots from Australia that now live in homes around the world. They can learn to copy hundreds of human words — one budgie named Puck learned over 1,700 words, more than any other bird ever!
text.summary.tiny: Budgies are tiny parrots from Australia with bright feathers and chatty voices. They can learn hundreds of words — one budgie learned over 1,700!
fun_facts.young: Budgies grind their beaks when they're happy and relaxed, like a cat purring.
Male budgies have blue noses, and female budgies have brown or pink noses.
Budgies bob their heads up and down when they're excited or trying to get attention.
A budgie can fly up to 40 miles per hour when it's in a hurry!
Budgies love to chew and shred paper — it's their favorite hobby.
Each budgie has a special pattern of stripes on its head, like a fingerprint.
fun_facts.tiny: Budgies grind their beaks when they're happy, like a cat purring.
Boy budgies have blue noses and girl budgies have brown or pink noses.
Budgies bob their heads up and down when they're excited or want attention.
did_you_know.young: Wild budgies are always green and yellow, but pet budgies come in blue, white, and even purple!
Budgies can turn their heads almost all the way around to see behind them.
A budgie's heart beats over 300 times per minute — that's five times faster than yours!
Budgies love to look at themselves in mirrors and will chat with their own reflection.
In the wild, budgies fly in huge flocks of thousands of birds across the Australian desert.
text.size_comparison.young: Smaller than your hand — they perch happily on one finger!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh less than a cookie — light enough to barely feel on your finger.
text.map_narration: Budgies come from the grasslands and scrublands of Australia.
text.sound_description.young: Budgies chirp, chatter, and sing happy songs all day long, and some learn to whistle tunes and say words!

text.summary.young: Cockatiels are small parrots from Australia with bright orange cheek patches and a tall feather crest on their heads. Male cockatiels are amazing singers who can learn to whistle tunes and copy human words.
text.summary.tiny: Cockatiels are small parrots from Australia with bright orange cheek patches and tall feather crests on their heads. Male cockatiels can learn to whistle tunes and copy human words.
fun_facts.young: Cockatiels fly super fast — up to 40 miles per hour in the wild.
They love to sit on the highest perch they can find.
They eat mostly seeds and grass in the wild.
Baby cockatiels are born with their eyes closed and no feathers.
They use their feet like hands to hold food while they eat.
They bob their heads up and down when they're happy.
fun_facts.tiny: They use their feet like hands to hold food while they eat.
Baby cockatiels are born with their eyes closed and no feathers.
They bob their heads up and down when they're happy.
did_you_know.young: A cockatiel's crest shows how it feels — tall and pointy when excited, flat when scared or relaxed.
Male cockatiels are better singers than females and can learn whole songs.
They are the second most popular pet bird in the world.
Wild cockatiels travel in huge flocks across Australia looking for seeds and water.
They can live for over 20 years with good care.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a ruler, with a fancy crest on top!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about the same as an apple — light enough to sit on your shoulder.
text.map_narration: Cockatiels come from the dry grasslands of Australia.
text.sound_description.young: They chirp, whistle cheerful tunes, and the males sing loud songs to show off.

text.summary.young: Goldfish are small orange fish that live in freshwater tanks and ponds all around the world. They can remember things for at least three months and can even learn tricks like pushing levers to get food.
text.summary.tiny: Goldfish are small orange fish that remember your face and get excited when you visit them. They can live longer than most dogs if they have a big home.
fun_facts.young: Goldfish can see more colors than humans can — they can even see ultraviolet light.
A goldfish's memory lasts at least three months, not three seconds like people think.
They sleep with their eyes open because they don't have eyelids.
Some goldfish can live for over 40 years — the oldest goldfish ever lived to be 43.
They come in many colors including red, white, black, and even blue.
Baby goldfish are born gray or brown and turn orange as they grow up.
fun_facts.tiny: They can see more colours than you can — even invisible ones called ultraviolet.
Baby goldfish are born grey or brown and turn orange as they grow.
They sleep with their eyes open because they don't have eyelids.
did_you_know.young: They were first kept as pets in China over 1,000 years ago.
A goldfish can recognize its owner's face and get excited when they see them.
They can live for more than 10 years if they have a big tank and good care.
They keep growing their whole lives — the bigger their home, the bigger they can grow.
They have teeth in the back of their throat to help them chew their food.
text.size_comparison.young: Most goldfish are about as long as your finger, but some can grow as big as your forearm!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as an apple — but they live in water, so you'd never pick one up!
text.map_narration: Goldfish were first kept as pets in China over a thousand years ago.
text.sound_description.young: They don't make sounds with their voices, but you can hear bubbles popping and water splashing when they swim.

betta_fish.name: Betta Fish
betta_fish.habitat: shallow streams, rice paddies, and slow-moving waters in Southeast Asia

text.summary.young: Betta fish are small, colorful fish from Southeast Asia that live in rice paddies and shallow streams. They can breathe air directly from the surface using a special organ called a labyrinth, so they survive in water with very little oxygen.
text.summary.tiny: Betta fish are tiny, colorful fish that can breathe air like you do. They gulp air from the top of the water with a special part inside their body.
fun_facts.young: Betta fish flare their fins and gills to look bigger when they feel threatened.
They can live in tiny spaces like rice paddies because they breathe air from the surface.
Male bettas have long, flowing fins, while females have shorter fins.
They are carnivores and love to eat small insects and worms.
They can see you outside their tank and learn when it's feeding time.
Wild bettas come from Thailand, where they live in warm, shallow water.
fun_facts.tiny: Male betta fish spread their fins wide to look big and scary.
They can see you through the glass and know when it's time to eat.
Wild betta fish are brown, but people have made them bright red, blue, and purple.
did_you_know.young: Male betta fish are so territorial they will fight other males — that's why they're sometimes called Siamese fighting fish.
They can recognize their owners and will swim to the front of the tank when they see you.
In the wild, betta fish are usually brown or gray — the bright colors we see in pet bettas were bred by humans.
A male betta builds a bubble nest at the water's surface to protect his eggs.
They can jump out of the water, so their tanks need covers on top.
text.size_comparison.young: Only about as long as your little finger — tiny but fierce!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh less than a single coin — almost nothing at all.
text.map_narration: Betta fish come from the shallow rice paddies and ponds of Thailand.
text.sound_description.young: They don't make vocal sounds, but you can hear them splash when they jump to the surface for air.

turtle.name: Turtle
turtle.habitat: Oceans, rivers, ponds, forests, and deserts worldwide

text.summary.young: Turtles are reptiles with hard shells that live in oceans, rivers, and on land all over the world. They have been on Earth for over 200 million years — they even survived the asteroid that killed the dinosaurs!
text.summary.tiny: Turtles wear their bones on the outside — their shell is their skeleton! They've been swimming and walking on Earth since before the dinosaurs.
fun_facts.young: Turtles can't stick their heads out of their shells if the shell is too small — the shell grows with them!
A turtle's shell can feel touch — if you tap it gently, the turtle knows you're there.
Some turtles can breathe through their butts! They absorb oxygen from water while hibernating underwater.
The largest turtle ever recorded was a leatherback sea turtle that weighed over 900 kilograms — as heavy as a small car!
They have been to space! In 1968, two Russian tortoises flew around the moon.
Unlike tortoises, many turtles are excellent swimmers with webbed feet or flippers.
fun_facts.tiny: A turtle's shell can feel you touch it, just like your skin can.
Some turtles breathe through their bottoms when they sleep underwater.
Baby sea turtles follow the moonlight to find the ocean.
did_you_know.young: A turtle's shell is part of its skeleton — it's made of over 50 bones fused together!
Some sea turtles can hold their breath underwater for up to 7 hours while they sleep.
They don't have teeth — they use their sharp beaks to tear food instead.
Box turtles can live for over 100 years — some pet turtles outlive their owners!
Baby sea turtles use moonlight to find their way to the ocean after hatching on the beach.
text.size_comparison.young: Most pet turtles fit right in both your hands — shell and all!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a loaf of bread — around 1 pound.
text.map_narration: Turtles live on every continent except Antarctica — in rivers, ponds, and oceans.
text.sound_description.young: They usually don't make much noise, but they can hiss when scared or make quiet chirping sounds.

text.summary.young: Tortoises are slow-moving reptiles with hard shells that live on land in warm places like Africa, Asia, and the Americas. They are the longest-lived animals with backbones on Earth — some live for over 150 years!
text.summary.tiny: Tortoises carry their homes on their backs — hard shells made of bone that grow with them their whole lives. Some tortoises live longer than anyone you'll ever meet — over one hundred and fifty years!
fun_facts.young: Tortoises walk very slowly — only about 0.3 kilometers per hour!
Their shells are made of over 50 bones all joined together.
They eat plants, fruits, flowers, and cactus.
They can weigh as much as a baby elephant — up to 250 kilograms!
They dig burrows underground to stay cool on hot days.
A tortoise's shell is part of its skeleton — it grows along with the tortoise for its whole life.
fun_facts.tiny: They walk slower than you do — it takes them ages to cross a garden!
They don't have teeth so they tear their food with hard beaks.
Some tortoises can be heavier than you and your whole family put together!
did_you_know.young: A tortoise named Jonathan was born in 1832 and is still alive today — he's over 190 years old!
They can pull their heads and legs completely inside their shells when they're scared.
Baby tortoises are called hatchlings and they dig themselves out of their underground nests all alone.
They don't have teeth — they use their hard beaks to bite and chew their food.
Some tortoises can go a whole year without eating or drinking water.
text.size_comparison.young: Giant tortoises can be longer than a bathtub and taller than your knees!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as three or four grown-ups — around 550 pounds.
text.map_narration: Giant tortoises live on the Galapagos Islands and the Seychelles Islands.
text.sound_description.young: They sometimes make a quiet hissing sound when they pull their head into their shell.

text.summary.young: Leopard geckos are small lizards with spotted skin that live in the dry deserts of Asia. They can blink their eyes with real eyelids, which makes them different from almost every other gecko in the world.
text.summary.tiny: Leopard geckos are spotty lizards who can blink their eyes — something almost no other gecko can do! They live in desert burrows and hunt bugs at night.
fun_facts.young: Leopard geckos hunt at night when the desert cools down.
They wave their tail back and forth before pouncing on prey to get ready for the jump.
Their tail can break off if a predator grabs it, and a new one grows back.
They don't have ears you can see, but they can hear through small holes on the sides of their head.
They live in underground burrows to escape the hot desert sun.

text.summary.young: Pachycephalosaurus was a dinosaur that lived in North America 70 million years ago. It had a super thick skull dome on top of its head — up to 25 centimeters thick — that it may have used to headbutt rivals like bighorn sheep do today.
text.summary.tiny: Pachycephalosaurus had a super thick dome on top of its head made of solid bone. It might have headbutted other dinosaurs like sheep do today!
fun_facts.young: The dome on its head was as thick as your whole hand is long.
It had rows of spiky bumps and knobs around the back of its head like a crown.
This headbutting dinosaur was about as long as a small car.
It had a good sense of smell to find food and sniff out danger.
Its teeth were small and leaf-shaped — perfect for chomping plants.
No complete skeleton has ever been found — only skulls and skull pieces!
fun_facts.tiny: The dome on its head was thick as a big book.
It had spiky bumps around its head like a crown.
It walked on two legs and had tiny arms.
did_you_know.young: The name means 'thick-headed lizard' — a reference to their dome-shaped skull.
Its skull dome was made of solid bone — thicker than a bowling ball!
Scientists think it headbutted other Pachycephalosaurus to show who was strongest.
It walked on two legs and had tiny arms like T. rex.
It ate both plants and small animals — berries, leaves, and maybe bugs!
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a car, with a thick dome of bone on their head — around 15 feet long!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weighed about as much as five or six grown-ups — around 990 pounds.
text.map_narration: Pachycephalosaurus fossils have been found in Montana, South Dakota, and Wyoming.
text.sound_description.young: They probably made deep growls and loud snorting sounds.

therizinosaurus.name: Therizinosaurus
therizinosaurus.habitat: Forests and river valleys in ancient Asia

text.summary.young: Therizinosaurus was a giant dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period. It had the longest claws of any animal ever — up to 1 metre long — but it used them to pull down branches to eat leaves, not to hunt.
text.summary.tiny: Therizinosaurus had the longest claws that ever existed — each one as long as your whole arm. But it didn't hunt with them — it used them like giant hooks to pull leafy branches down to eat.
fun_facts.young: Each claw was as long as a grown-up's arm
This strange dinosaur walked on two legs like a bird
It had a long neck to reach leaves high in trees
Its claws were so long they might have dragged on the ground
They had a pot belly to help digest all the plants it ate
Scientists first thought its giant claws belonged to a turtle
fun_facts.tiny: Each claw was longer than a cricket bat.
It walked on two legs and had a round belly full of leaves.
Scientists first thought these enormous claws belonged to a giant turtle!
did_you_know.young: Therizinosaurus's claws were longer than a baseball bat
Despite its scary claws, Therizinosaurus only ate plants
It could reach up to pull down the highest tree branches
They were as heavy as an elephant
Its name means 'scythe lizard' because its claws looked like giant farming tools
text.size_comparison.young: As tall as a giraffe, with claws longer than your arm — around 33 feet long!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weighed about as much as a school bus — around 11,000 pounds.
text.map_narration: Therizinosaurus fossils have been found in Mongolia.
text.sound_description.young: They probably made deep rumbling calls and low growls to communicate with other dinosaurs.

utahraptor.name: Utahraptor
utahraptor.habitat: Forests and plains of North America

text.summary.young: Utahraptor was a giant raptor dinosaur that lived in North America 130 million years ago. It had a huge sickle-shaped claw on each foot — as long as a ruler — that it used like a knife to catch prey.
text.summary.tiny: Utahraptor was a giant hunting dinosaur with a huge curved claw on each foot — as long as a ruler. It lived in North America millions of years before the smaller raptors you might know.
fun_facts.young: Utahraptor was the largest raptor dinosaur ever discovered.
It lived millions of years before the smaller Velociraptor.
Each hand had three fingers with sharp curved claws for grabbing.
They probably hunted plant-eating dinosaurs much bigger than themselves.
Its brain was big for a dinosaur, which made it a clever hunter.
The sickle claw could swing down like a hook to hold onto struggling prey.
fun_facts.tiny: They were the biggest raptor dinosaurs ever found.
It had feathers all over its body, just like birds today.
Each hand had three fingers with curved claws for grabbing.
did_you_know.young: They were as big as a polar bear and weighed as much as a grand piano.
Its deadly toe claw was 24 centimeters long — that's longer than a pencil.
They had feathers covering their body, just like modern birds.
It could run fast on two strong legs and had sharp teeth for eating meat.
Scientists found the first Utahraptor bones in Utah, which is how it got its name.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a large car, with a massive curved claw on each foot — around 20 feet long!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weighed about as much as five or six grown-ups — around 1,100 pounds.
text.map_narration: Fossils of this fierce raptor have been found in Utah — which is how they got their name!
text.sound_description.young: They probably made loud roars and screeches to communicate with other raptors.

text.summary.young: Microraptor was a tiny dinosaur that lived in the forests of ancient China. It had four wings — two on its arms and two on its legs — and glided through the trees like a flying squirrel.
text.summary.tiny: Microraptor was a tiny dinosaur with four wings — two on its arms and two on its legs. It glided through the treetops like a furry flying squirrel.
fun_facts.young: Microraptor had sharp curved claws on all four feet for climbing trees.
It probably lived in trees and hunted like a small hawk.
Its name means 'tiny thief' because it was so small.
They had teeth like tiny knives for catching prey.
It could glide up to 40 meters between trees — that's longer than three school buses!
Scientists think Microraptor hunted at dawn and dusk when it was shadowy.
fun_facts.tiny: They had shiny black feathers that sparkled like a crow's.
It was about as big as a chicken.
Scientists found fish bones inside one — it caught fish from the water!
did_you_know.young: They had shiny black feathers that sparkled like a crow's.
It was one of the smallest dinosaurs ever — about the size of a chicken.
They couldn't flap their wings to fly, but they could glide from tree to tree.
Scientists found fish bones in a Microraptor's stomach, so it ate fish!
Its long tail feathers helped it steer while gliding through the air.
text.size_comparison.young: Tiny for a dinosaur — only about as long as a school ruler, with four feathered wings!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weighed about as much as a carton of milk — around 2 pounds. Light enough to glide!
text.map_narration: Microraptor fossils have been found in northeastern China.
text.sound_description.young: They probably made high-pitched screeches and chirping calls like modern birds.

deinonychus.name: Deinonychus
deinonychus.habitat: forests and plains of North America

text.summary.young: Deinonychus was a fierce dinosaur that lived in North America during the Early Cretaceous period. It had a huge curved claw on each foot that it used like a slashing knife to hunt its prey.
text.summary.tiny: Deinonychus had a giant curved claw on each foot — as long as your hand! It could run as fast as a galloping horse.
fun_facts.young: Deinonychus could run as fast as a horse
It had sharp teeth shaped like steak knives for tearing meat
Its stiff tail helped it balance when running and turning quickly
They were about as tall as a grown-up person
It had big eyes for spotting prey from far away
Scientists think Deinonychus was warm-blooded like birds are today
fun_facts.tiny: Its tail was stiff like a broom handle to help it balance when it ran.
It had sharp teeth shaped like little knives.
They were probably covered in feathers to keep warm.
did_you_know.young: The name means 'terrible claw' — a reference to their giant toe claws
Its sickle claw was as long as a grown-up's hand
Scientists think Deinonychus may have hunted in packs like wolves do today
The Velociraptors in Jurassic Park were actually based on Deinonychus
They were probably covered in feathers to keep warm
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a small car — around 10 feet from nose to tail, with a big killer claw on each foot.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weighed about as much as a grown-up — around 165 pounds.
text.map_narration: Deinonychus fossils have been found in Montana, Wyoming, and Oklahoma.
text.sound_description.young: They probably made loud roars and screeches to talk to their pack.

text.summary.young: African elephants are the largest land animals on Earth and live in grasslands and forests across Africa. They can communicate by making ultra-low rumbles that travel through the ground — other elephants feel the vibrations through their feet from kilometres away.
text.summary.tiny: African elephants are the biggest animals that walk on land — bigger than a car! They talk to each other with rumbles so low you can't hear them, but other elephants feel them through the ground.
fun_facts.young: An elephant's tusks are actually giant teeth that never stop growing.
Elephants love taking mud baths to protect their skin from sunburn and bug bites.
A baby elephant can stand up and walk just 20 minutes after being born.
Elephants spend up to 16 hours a day eating grass, leaves, bark, and fruit.
An adult elephant drinks about 200 litres of water every day — that's enough to fill a bathtub.
Elephants remember their friends and family for their whole lives and show love by wrapping trunks together.
fun_facts.tiny: An elephant's tusks are really giant teeth that never stop growing.
Baby elephants can stand up and walk just twenty minutes after they're born.
Elephants remember their friends and family forever — they say hello by wrapping trunks together.
did_you_know.young: They are the largest land animals in the world.
An elephant's trunk has over 40,000 muscles and can lift heavy logs or pick up a single blade of grass.
Elephants use their huge ears like fans to cool down in the hot African sun.
Baby elephants suck their trunks for comfort, just like human babies suck their thumbs.
Elephants can recognize themselves in a mirror — only a few animals are smart enough to do this.
text.size_comparison.young: The biggest land animal alive — they tower over every grown-up at over 10 feet at the shoulder!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a school bus full of kids — around 11,000 pounds.
text.map_narration: African elephants roam across the grasslands and forests of Africa.
text.sound_description.young: They make loud trumpet calls and deep rumbling sounds that can travel for many kilometres.

text.summary.young: Lions are big cats that live in Africa and parts of Asia. They are the only cats that live together in family groups called prides.
text.summary.tiny: Lions are the only cats that live together in families. A male lion's fluffy mane gets darker and darker as he grows older — like a crown.
fun_facts.young: With their powerful paws, lions can knock prey to the ground in a single swipe.
A lion's tongue is so rough it can lick meat right off a bone.
The males can weigh as much as three adult humans put together.
They're the second biggest cats in the world — only tigers are bigger.
A pride can have up to 40 lions living together like one big family.
They spend most of their time resting in the shade during hot days.
fun_facts.tiny: Their tongue is so rough it can lick meat right off a bone!
They sleep for twenty hours every day — longer than you sleep at night!
Baby lions have spotty fur that slowly disappears as they grow up.
did_you_know.young: The females do almost all the hunting while the males guard the pride.
Their roar can be heard from 8 kilometres away — that's as far as 80 football fields!
They sleep up to 20 hours a day to save energy for hunting.
The males have big manes that get darker as they get older.
The cubs have spots on their fur that fade away as they grow up.
text.size_comparison.young: Standing on all fours, they're already taller than you at the shoulder — about 4 feet. With their head held high, they tower over you.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as ten kids put together — around 420 pounds.
text.map_narration: Lions live in parts of Africa and a small region of western India.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep, thundering roars that can be heard from very far away.

text.summary.young: Cheetahs are spotted wild cats that live in grasslands across Africa and parts of Asia. They are the fastest land animals on Earth, reaching speeds of 100 km/h in just 3 seconds.
text.summary.tiny: Cheetahs are the fastest runners on land — faster than any car on your street. They have spots, long tails, and black stripes down their faces like tears.
fun_facts.young: Cheetahs hunt during the day when other big cats are resting.
Their claws don't retract all the way, which gives them extra grip while running.
A cheetah's spine bends like a spring with every stride, making their legs stretch farther.
They drink water every three to four days.
Mother cheetahs teach their cubs to hunt by bringing them live prey to practice on.
They can't climb trees as well as leopards because their claws aren't sharp enough.
fun_facts.tiny: A cheetah can run as fast as a car on the motorway.
Their claws stick out all the time, like a dog's — most cats tuck theirs away.
Their babies have fluffy silver hair on their backs to help them hide in the grass.
did_you_know.young: They can only run at top speed for about 30 seconds before their bodies get too hot.
A cheetah's long tail helps it balance and steer when running at high speeds.
They have black tear marks on their faces that help reduce glare from the sun.
Unlike other big cats, cheetahs cannot roar — they chirp and purr instead.
Their cubs have a silvery mane on their backs that helps them hide in tall grass.
text.size_comparison.young: Tall and slender, they reach right up to your chin — around 3 feet 1 inch at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a grown-up — around 121 pounds.
text.map_narration: Cheetahs live in the grasslands and open plains of Africa and a tiny part of Iran.
text.sound_description.young: They chirp like birds, purr like house cats, and make hissing or growling sounds when upset.

leopard.name: Leopard
leopard.habitat: Forests, grasslands, and mountains in Africa and Asia

text.summary.young: Leopards are spotted wild cats that live in Africa and Asia. They are so strong they can drag prey twice their weight up into trees to keep it safe from other animals.
