text.summary.tiny: Leopards have rose-shaped spots on golden fur — and they're strong enough to drag animals heavier than themselves straight up a tree. They can leap as far as a car and climb better than any other big cat.
fun_facts.young: Leopards are the strongest climbers of all the big cats.
They can leap more than 6 metres forward and 3 metres high — that's as tall as a giraffe!
They are silent hunters who sneak up on their prey without making a sound.
They eat everything from antelopes and monkeys to birds and beetles.
A leopard can carry animals heavier than itself straight up a tree trunk.
Black panthers are actually leopards with dark fur — you can still see their spots in bright light!
fun_facts.tiny: Black panthers are actually leopards with dark fur — you can still see their spots in bright sunlight.
Every leopard has different spots, like a fingerprint — no two patterns are ever the same.
They hunt at night and see in the dark seven times better than you can.
did_you_know.young: They can run as fast as a car on a city street — up to 58 kilometres per hour!
A leopard's spots are called rosettes because they look like little roses.
They are excellent swimmers and sometimes catch fish to eat.
Each leopard has a unique pattern of spots — no two leopards look exactly the same.
They hunt at night and can see seven times better in the dark than humans can.
text.size_comparison.young: On all fours, they reach your shoulders — around 2 feet 7 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a grown-up — around 132 pounds.
text.map_narration: Leopards live across Africa and Asia — from forests to mountains to grasslands.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep growls and rasping roars, and they purr like giant cats when they're happy.

text.summary.young: Giraffes are the tallest animals on Earth, living in Africa's grasslands and open woodlands. Their dark bluish-purple tongue is 45 centimetres long and the special colour protects it from sunburn while they eat thorny acacia leaves all day.
text.summary.tiny: Giraffes are the tallest animals in the whole world — as tall as a house with an upstairs! They live in Africa and use their long purple tongue to pluck leaves from the prickliest trees.
fun_facts.young: Giraffes are so tall they can look into second-floor windows.
Each giraffe has a unique pattern of spots, just like human fingerprints.
They can run as fast as 56 kilometres per hour when they need to escape danger.
A giraffe's kick is so powerful it can seriously hurt a lion.
They drink water by spreading their front legs wide apart so they can reach down to the ground.
Male giraffes sometimes gently bump their long necks together when they play or compete.
fun_facts.tiny: Every giraffe has its own special pattern of spots, like your own fingerprints.
A giraffe's kick is so powerful it can knock down a lion.
Baby giraffes can stand up and walk around less than an hour after they're born.
did_you_know.young: A giraffe's tongue is as long as a ruler and dark purple to protect it from the hot sun.
They only sleep about 30 minutes each day — usually just a few minutes at a time.
Baby giraffes can stand up and walk within an hour of being born.
They have the same number of neck bones as humans — just seven — but each bone is super long.
A giraffe's heart weighs 11 kilograms and pumps blood all the way up its long neck to its brain.
text.size_comparison.young: The tallest animal on Earth — their legs alone are taller than most grown-ups, and their head is nearly 20 feet up!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a small car — around 2,600 pounds.
text.map_narration: Giraffes live across the grasslands and open woodlands of Africa.
text.sound_description.young: They are mostly quiet, but they can make low grunts, snorts, and bellowing sounds to talk to each other.

text.summary.young: Zebras are striped horses that live on the grasslands of Africa. Every zebra has a completely unique stripe pattern — like a fingerprint — and foals recognise their mother by her stripes.
text.summary.tiny: Zebras are striped horses that live on the grasslands of Africa. Every single zebra has its own special stripe pattern — no two are the same.
fun_facts.young: Zebra stripes may help keep biting flies away — the pattern confuses the bugs
They are very social and live in family groups led by a stallion
When zebras run together their stripes blend and make it hard for predators to pick out one zebra
They can run up to 65 kilometres per hour to escape lions and hyenas
They spend most of their day eating grass — up to 18 hours
They roll in dust to protect their skin and keep bugs away
fun_facts.tiny: They live in families and they look after each other.
When zebras run together, their stripes swirl and blend — it's hard to see where one zebra ends and another begins.
Baby zebras can stand up and walk just twenty minutes after they're born.
did_you_know.young: No two zebras have the same stripe pattern — each one is as unique as your fingerprint
Baby zebras can stand up and walk just 20 minutes after being born
They sleep standing up so they can run away quickly if danger comes
A group of zebras is called a dazzle because their stripes dazzle and confuse predators
They have excellent hearing and can turn their ears in almost any direction
text.size_comparison.young: Taller than you at the shoulder — about 4 feet 3 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as five or six grown-ups — around 772 pounds.
text.map_narration: Zebras live in the grasslands and savannas of eastern and southern Africa.
text.sound_description.young: They bray like donkeys and also bark to warn the group of danger.

text.summary.young: Hippos are huge animals that live in rivers and lakes across Africa. Their skin makes a special red oil that works like sunscreen and keeps cuts from getting infected.
text.summary.tiny: Hippos make special red oil on their skin that works like sunscreen and medicine. They live in rivers and lakes, spending their days in the water and their nights eating grass on land.
fun_facts.young: Hippos spend most of their day in the water to keep their skin cool and moist.
At night, hippos leave the water to eat grass — they can eat 80 pounds in one night!
A hippo's eyes, ears, and nose are all on top of its head so it can see and breathe while mostly underwater.
Hippos are excellent swimmers and can even walk along the bottom of rivers.
The red oil hippos make is sometimes called 'blood sweat' but it's not blood or sweat at all.
Hippos use their tail like a propeller to spread their poop and mark their territory.
fun_facts.tiny: A hippo's mouth can open wider than you are tall — almost as wide as your front door!
Hippos can hold their breath underwater for five whole minutes.
Baby hippos are born right in the water and have to swim up for their very first breath.
did_you_know.young: Hippos can hold their breath underwater for up to five minutes.
A hippo's mouth can open almost four feet wide — that's wider than a door!
Baby hippos are born underwater and must swim to the surface for their first breath.
Hippos can run faster than humans on land, reaching speeds of 30 miles per hour.
Even though hippos look chubby, they have almost no body fat — it's mostly muscle!
text.size_comparison.young: Even on all fours, they're already taller than you at the shoulder — about 4 feet 11 inches.
text.weight_comparison.young: About 4400 pounds — as heavy as a small car!
text.map_narration: Hippopotamuses live in the rivers and lakes of sub-Saharan Africa.
text.sound_description.young: Hippos make deep grunting and bellowing sounds that can be heard both above and below the water.

rhinoceros.name: Rhinoceros
rhinoceros.habitat: Grasslands and forests in Africa and Asia

text.summary.young: Rhinoceroses are huge, plant-eating animals with thick gray skin that live in Africa and Asia. Their horn is made of the same stuff as your fingernails and keeps growing their whole life!
text.summary.tiny: Rhinos are gigantic animals with one or two horns on their nose that keep growing forever. They're gentle plant-eaters — but they can run faster than your car drives down your street!
fun_facts.young: Rhinos can run as fast as 50 kilometers per hour — that's faster than most cars drive in a neighborhood!
A rhino's skin is 5 centimeters thick, but it's still sensitive enough to feel a fly landing on it.
Rhinos communicate by making snorts, growls, and trumpet sounds.
A group of rhinos is called a 'crash' — perfect for such powerful animals!
Rhinos can weigh as much as 30 adult humans put together.
Oxpecker birds sit on rhinos' backs and eat ticks and bugs off their skin — it's like a cleaning service!
fun_facts.tiny: A rhino's skin is thick as a cushion, but it can still feel a tiny fly land on its back.
Little birds sit on rhinos all day, eating bugs off their skin like a cleaning crew.
Baby rhinos can stand up and walk just one hour after they're born.
did_you_know.young: A rhino's horn isn't bone — it's made of keratin, just like your fingernails and hair!
Rhinos have terrible eyesight but amazing hearing and smell.
A baby rhino can stand up and walk just one hour after being born.
Rhinos love to roll in mud to protect their skin from the sun and bugs.
White rhinos aren't actually white — they're gray! Their name comes from the Afrikaans word 'wijd' meaning 'wide' for their wide mouth.
text.size_comparison.young: Taller than any grown-up at the shoulder — a wall of muscle and horn, around 5 feet 7 inches.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a small car — around 5,000 pounds.
text.map_narration: Rhinoceroses live in the grasslands and forests of Africa and southern Asia.
text.sound_description.young: Rhinos make loud snorting sounds, deep growls, and trumpet calls to talk to each other.

text.summary.young: African Buffalo are large, powerful animals that live in African grasslands and forests. When the herd can't decide which way to go, the females vote by standing up, looking in their preferred direction, and sitting back down — whichever way most females face wins!
text.summary.tiny: African Buffalo are huge, strong animals with massive curved horns. When the herd needs to choose a path, the females vote — they stand, face the way they want to go, then sit back down!
fun_facts.young: Buffalo live in herds that can have over 1,000 members
They spend most of their day eating grass — up to 10 hours every day!
Buffalo love to roll in mud to cool down and protect their skin from bugs and sunburn
Baby buffalo are called calves and can run with the herd just hours after being born
Buffalo stick together — if one is attacked, the whole herd will come to help defend it
They can weigh as much as a small car — about 700 kilograms!
fun_facts.tiny: Buffalo can weigh as much as a small car.
They love rolling in mud — it cools them down and keeps bugs away.
If one buffalo is in trouble, the whole herd rushes over to help.
did_you_know.young: They hold democratic votes — females stand up, look the way they want to go, then sit down, and the herd follows the direction most chose
Their curved horns can grow so wide they meet in the middle of their head, forming a hard helmet called a 'boss'
Buffalo have excellent memories and can recognize other herd members even after years apart
They never forget an enemy — if a lion attacks them, they remember that lion and will chase it away if they see it again
They are one of the most dangerous animals in Africa and have never been successfully domesticated
text.size_comparison.young: Standing on all fours, they're already taller than you at the shoulder — about 4 feet 11 inches.
text.weight_comparison.young: About 1550 pounds — as heavy as a horse!
text.map_narration: African buffalo roam the grasslands and forests of sub-Saharan Africa.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep snorting and grunting sounds, and loud bellowing calls to communicate with their herd.

text.summary.young: Hyenas are wild hunters that live in Africa and parts of Asia. They have one of the strongest bites of any mammal and can crush bones that other animals can't even break.
text.summary.tiny: Hyenas have one of the strongest bites in the whole animal world — strong enough to crack bones like twigs. They live in big families in Africa and Asia, and they hunt together like a team.
fun_facts.young: Hyenas make a sound that sounds like laughing, but they're not actually happy — they make this sound when they're excited or nervous
A hyena clan can have up to 80 members
They have excellent night vision and can see in almost total darkness
Their front legs are longer than their back legs, which gives them their unique sloped shape
They can run up to 60 kilometers per hour when chasing prey
They store extra food underwater in rivers and lakes to keep it fresh
fun_facts.tiny: They make a sound that's just like laughing — but they're not telling jokes!
Their front legs are longer than their back legs, so they walk with a slope.
Baby hyenas are born with their eyes already open and all their teeth ready to go.
did_you_know.young: Spotted hyenas hunt most of their own food — lions actually steal from hyenas more often than hyenas steal from lions
A hyena's bite is so strong it can crush a giraffe's leg bone
Their groups are led by females, and the females are bigger and stronger than the males
They can digest things other animals can't, like bones, horns, and hooves
Baby hyenas are born with their eyes open and their teeth already grown in
text.size_comparison.young: Sturdy and strong, they reach your shoulders — around 2 feet 7 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a grown-up — around 132 pounds.
text.map_narration: Hyenas live across the savannas, grasslands, and forests of Africa.
text.sound_description.young: They make a famous laughing sound called a giggle, plus whoops and growls to talk to their clan.

text.summary.young: Warthogs are wild pigs that live in the grasslands of Africa. They kneel down on their front legs to eat grass because their necks are too short to reach the ground.
text.summary.tiny: Warthogs kneel down to eat because their necks are too short to reach the grass. They run backwards into their underground homes so their tusks point out to keep them safe.
fun_facts.young: Warthogs have special pads on their knees from kneeling so much.
They sleep underground in burrows that other animals have dug.
They use their flat snouts like shovels to dig for roots.
Their name comes from the bumps on their face that look like warts.
Oxpecker birds sit on warthogs and eat bugs off their skin.
Male warthogs fight by pushing each other with their tusks.
fun_facts.tiny: They have special tough pads on their knees from kneeling down so much.
Little birds sit right on a warthog's back and eat the bugs off its skin.
They use their flat nose like a shovel to dig up tasty roots.
did_you_know.young: They run backward into their burrows so their tusks face outward to protect them.
They can run as fast as a car in the city — up to 50 kilometers per hour!
They have four tusks that keep growing their whole life.
They take mud baths to cool down and protect their skin from the hot sun.
Baby warthogs follow their mother in a single-file line with their tails sticking straight up.
text.size_comparison.young: On all fours, they reach your belly — around 2 feet 2 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a grown-up — around 176 pounds.
text.map_narration: Warthogs live in the grasslands and savannas of sub-Saharan Africa.
text.sound_description.young: They make grunting and snorting sounds, and squeal loudly when they're scared or excited.

text.summary.young: Meerkats are small mammals that live in the deserts of southern Africa. They are immune to scorpion venom and teach their babies how to hunt stinging scorpions safely.
text.summary.tiny: Meerkats stand up tall on their back legs like tiny guards watching for danger. They live together in big families in the African desert.
fun_facts.young: Meerkats take turns being the lookout while others hunt for food.
They stand on their back legs to watch for danger from eagles and jackals.
They love to eat scorpions, spiders, and beetles.
They use over 20 different sounds to talk to each other.
They sunbathe every morning to warm up after cold desert nights.
Their burrows can have 15 different entrances and exits for quick escapes.
fun_facts.tiny: They take turns standing guard while everyone else digs for breakfast.
They can close their ears when they dig so sand doesn't get inside.
They sunbathe together every morning to warm up after the cold night.
did_you_know.young: They can close their ears to keep sand out when they dig underground tunnels.
A meerkat family can have up to 40 members living together in one burrow.
They have dark patches around their eyes that work like sunglasses to block the bright desert sun.
Baby meerkats practice their lookout skills by standing on their parents' backs.
They can dig through sand as heavy as their own body weight in just seconds.
text.size_comparison.young: Standing on their hind legs, they only reach your knees — around 1 foot tall!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh less than a carton of milk — around 2 pounds.
text.map_narration: Meerkats live in the dry deserts and grasslands of southern Africa.
text.sound_description.young: They chirp, bark, and squeak to warn each other about danger and talk to their family.

text.summary.young: Ostriches are the tallest and heaviest birds in the world, living in the grasslands and deserts of Africa. They can run faster than any other bird on Earth — up to 70 kilometres per hour, which is faster than a car in the city!
text.summary.tiny: Ostriches are the tallest birds in the whole world — taller than your dad! They can't fly, but they run faster than a car drives down your street.
fun_facts.young: Ostrich eggs are the largest eggs of any bird — one egg is as big as 24 chicken eggs!
They don't bury their heads in the sand — but they do lie flat on the ground to hide from danger.
They have only two toes on each foot, which helps them run super fast.
They can go without water for days by getting moisture from the plants they eat.
An ostrich's kick is so strong it can break bones.
Their feathers are soft and fluffy, and people once used them to make fancy hats and fans.
fun_facts.tiny: One ostrich egg is as big as twenty-four chicken eggs stacked together.
An ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain.
They have only two toes on each foot — just like you have two legs!
did_you_know.young: An ostrich's eye is bigger than its entire brain!
They can't fly, but their powerful legs can kill a lion with one kick.
They swallow pebbles and stones to help grind up food in their stomachs.
They live in groups called herds to help protect each other from predators.
A male ostrich does a special dance, flapping his wings and shaking his feathers, to impress females.
text.size_comparison.young: The tallest bird alive — they stand nearly 9 feet tall, way taller than any grown-up!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as two grown-ups — around 265 pounds.
text.map_narration: Ostriches live in the open grasslands and deserts of Africa.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep booming sounds that rumble like thunder, and they hiss when they're angry or scared.

baboon.name: Baboon
baboon.habitat: African savannas, woodlands, and rocky hills

text.summary.young: Baboons are large monkeys that live in Africa and Arabia. Female baboons inherit their mother's social rank at birth, which affects their friendships and power their entire life.
text.summary.tiny: Baboons are clever monkeys with colourful bottoms who live in huge families. They talk to each other with barks and grunts — and they even hold hands.
fun_facts.young: Baboons groom each other's fur to find bugs and make friends.
They use over 30 different sounds to talk to each other.
They eat almost anything — fruit, seeds, insects, eggs, and even small animals.
A baby baboon clings to its mother's belly for the first few weeks of life.
They have bare, colorful bottoms that help them sit comfortably on rocks.
They drink water by dipping their hands in and licking them, or by sucking it up directly.
fun_facts.tiny: They have special pouches in their cheeks where they store food to eat later.
Baby baboons cling tight to their mum's tummy and ride everywhere she goes.
They clean each other's fur with their fingers — looking for tiny bugs and making friends.
did_you_know.young: They sleep in trees or on cliff faces to stay safe from predators at night.
A baboon troop can have over 100 members, all working together.
They have cheek pouches where they store food to eat later.
Male baboons have fangs as long as a lion's teeth.
They can run as fast as a car in a neighborhood — up to 45 kilometers per hour!
text.size_comparison.young: On all fours, they reach your chest — around 2 feet 6 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh a little more than you — around 55 pounds.
text.map_narration: Baboons live across Africa, from savannas and forests to rocky hillsides.
text.sound_description.young: They bark like dogs, grunt to say hello, and scream loudly when they're excited or scared.

gorilla.name: Gorilla
gorilla.habitat: Rainforests and mountains of central Africa

text.summary.young: Gorillas are the largest primates in the world and live in the forests of Africa. Every single night, they build a brand new sleeping nest from branches and leaves — sometimes on the ground, sometimes high up in trees.
text.summary.tiny: Gorillas are the biggest apes in the whole world — bigger than your dad, bigger than any person you know. Every night, they build a brand new nest from branches and leaves to sleep in.
fun_facts.young: Male gorillas are called silverbacks because of the silver hair that grows on their backs when they turn 12 years old.
Gorillas are gentle giants — they mostly eat plants like leaves, stems, bamboo, and fruit.
A gorilla family is led by one big silverback dad who protects everyone.
They beat their chests to show they're strong — not because they're angry!
They use sticks as tools to test how deep water is before crossing.
When gorillas are happy, they sing and hum while they eat!
fun_facts.tiny: When a boy gorilla grows up, silver hair grows on his back — that's why he's called a silverback!
They sing and hum while they eat when they're happy.
Baby gorillas ride on their mum's back until they're about three years old.
did_you_know.young: They share 98% of their DNA with humans — that's more than almost any other animal!
A silverback gorilla can lift up to 815 kilograms — that's as heavy as 10 adult humans!
They have unique fingerprints just like people do.
Baby gorillas ride on their mother's back until they're about 3 years old.
They can learn sign language and communicate with humans!
text.size_comparison.young: Standing up straight, they are taller than most grown-ups — around 5 feet 7 inches!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as two or three grown-ups — around 400 pounds.
text.map_narration: Gorillas live in the tropical forests of central Africa.
text.sound_description.young: They grunt softly to talk to their family, hoot when they're happy, and roar loudly to warn others to stay away.

text.summary.young: Chimpanzees are clever apes that live in the forests of Africa. They make tools from sticks and rocks to get food — just like humans do!
text.summary.tiny: Chimpanzees use sticks and rocks like tools — they're one of the cleverest animals in the world! They live in African forests and sleep in nests they build fresh every night.
fun_facts.young: Chimpanzees use sticks to fish termites out of tiny holes in the ground.
They crack nuts open by smashing them with rocks like little hammers.
They make sponges from chewed leaves to soak up water and drink.
They sleep in cozy nests they build fresh every night high up in the trees.
They can learn sign language and talk to humans with their hands!
They remember where hundreds of different fruit trees are in the forest.
fun_facts.tiny: They fish termites out of tiny holes using sticks, then lick them off like a lolly.
They crack nuts by smashing them with rocks — bang bang bang!
They give each other hugs and kisses to say sorry or show they care.
did_you_know.young: They share 98% of their DNA with humans — we're more alike than different!
They can recognize themselves in mirrors, which shows they understand who they are.
They give each other hugs, kisses, and pats on the back to show they care.
They have unique fingerprints, just like you do!
Baby chimpanzees ride on their mother's back like a piggyback ride for years.
text.size_comparison.young: Standing up, they are about your height — around 4 feet tall.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a big suitcase — around 110 pounds.
text.map_narration: Chimpanzees live in the forests and woodlands of central and western Africa.
text.sound_description.young: They hoot and scream loudly to talk to each other, and they pant-laugh when they play and have fun.

text.summary.young: African wild dogs live in the grasslands and forests of Africa. They are some of the best hunters in the world — they catch their prey 8 out of every 10 times they hunt!
text.summary.tiny: African wild dogs sneeze to vote on what to do next! They live in big families and hunt together in the grasslands of Africa.
fun_facts.young: African wild dogs can run up to 60 kilometres per hour when chasing prey!
A pack of African wild dogs can have up to 40 members working together.
Their big, round ears help them hear prey from far away and cool down in the hot African sun.
They are also called painted wolves because of their colourful spotted coats.
Baby African wild dogs are born in underground dens to keep them safe from other predators.
When African wild dogs greet each other, they make excited squeaking and twittering sounds — almost like birds!
fun_facts.tiny: Every wild dog has its own spotty coat — no two patterns are ever the same.
They have four toes on each foot, not five like most dogs.
Wild dogs squeak and twitter when they're excited — it sounds a bit like birds!
did_you_know.young: They work together as a team when they hunt — they take turns chasing their prey until it gets tired.
Every African wild dog has a unique coat pattern — just like your fingerprints, no two are exactly the same!
They sneeze to vote! When the pack needs to decide whether to go hunting, they sneeze — and the dog who sneezes the most gets to choose.
These dogs have only four toes on each foot, not five like most dogs — this helps them run faster!
They packs take care of sick and old pack members by bringing them food and protecting them.
text.size_comparison.young: Standing beside you, they reach your chest — around 2 feet 4 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh a little more than you — around 55 pounds.
text.map_narration: African wild dogs roam the grasslands and woodlands of sub-Saharan Africa.
text.sound_description.young: They make squeaking and twittering sounds when they're excited, and they also bark and howl to talk to their pack.

text.summary.young: Servals are wild cats that live in the grasslands of Africa. They have the longest legs of any cat and can leap 3 metres straight up to catch birds flying in the air.
text.summary.tiny: Servals are wild cats with the longest legs of any cat — they can leap as high as your ceiling to catch birds flying by! They live in the grasslands of Africa.
fun_facts.young: Servals have the biggest ears of any cat compared to their head size.
They can jump higher than a basketball hoop to snatch birds out of the sky.
They are usually silent hunters — they sneak through grass without making a sound.
Their long legs help them see over tall grass like periscopes.
A serval can run up to 80 kilometres per hour in short bursts.
They sometimes play with their food before eating it, like house cats do.
fun_facts.tiny: They have the biggest ears of any cat, and they can swivel them like little satellite dishes.
They sometimes play with their food before eating it, just like pet cats do.
Their long legs help them peek over tall grass to spot their next meal.
did_you_know.young: They can hear a mouse moving underground from metres away.
Their huge ears can turn like satellite dishes to pinpoint sounds.
They catch their prey on the first try more than half the time — better than most cats.
They hunt at dawn and dusk when the grass is cool.
A serval's spots and stripes help it hide in tall grass.
text.size_comparison.young: Tall and leggy for a wild cat, they reach your belly — around 2 feet at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about the same as you — around 31 pounds.
text.map_narration: Servals live in the tall grasslands and wetlands of sub-Saharan Africa.
text.sound_description.young: They meow and chirp like house cats, but also make a high-pitched cry to call to each other.

great_white_shark.name: Great White Shark
great_white_shark.habitat: Coastal and open ocean waters worldwide

text.summary.young: Great white sharks are powerful ocean hunters found in seas all around the world. They can smell a single drop of blood from far away — like finding one red marble in a swimming pool full of clear ones.
text.summary.tiny: Great white sharks are mighty ocean swimmers with rows and rows of triangle teeth. They can smell one tiny drop of blood from really far away — like finding one red sweet in a whole bathtub of water.
fun_facts.young: Great white sharks can grow as long as a minibus!
Their teeth are shaped like triangles with zigzag edges — perfect for cutting.
They can swim up to 56 kilometres per hour when they're chasing prey.
They have special sensors in their nose that can detect the electricity made by other animals' heartbeats.
They can live for 70 years or more — that's as old as your great-grandparents!
Their grey-blue backs help them hide when seen from above, and their white bellies make them hard to see from below.
fun_facts.tiny: They grow as long as a big bus!
When one tooth falls out, another slides forward to take its place.
They can leap right out of the water when they're hunting seals!
did_you_know.young: They have been swimming in the oceans for 400 million years — that's way longer than trees have been growing on land!
A great white shark has about 300 teeth arranged in rows, and when one falls out, another moves forward to take its place.
They can jump completely out of the water when hunting seals — it's called breaching!
Baby great white sharks are called pups and they're born knowing how to hunt — no one teaches them.
They don't chew their food — they bite off big chunks and swallow them whole.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a large car — around 16 feet from nose to tail!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a small car — around 4,200 pounds.
text.map_narration: Great white sharks swim in cool oceans all around the world.
text.sound_description.young: They are mostly silent, but you might hear a powerful whoosh and splash when they breach out of the water.

text.summary.young: Hammerhead sharks are ocean hunters with hammer-shaped heads that live in warm waters all around the world. Their eyes sit on the ends of their wide heads, giving them 360-degree vision so they can see everything around them at once.
text.summary.tiny: Hammerhead sharks have heads shaped like hammers with eyes on each end. They can see all around them at once — above, below, and behind!
fun_facts.young: Baby hammerheads are born with soft, bendy heads that harden as they grow
Hammerheads love to eat stingrays, even though stingrays have poisonous barbs
Their favourite food is stingrays, squid, and fish
A hammerhead's head works like a metal detector to find prey
They can grow as long as a small car
Hammerheads sometimes get a tan from swimming in shallow, sunny water
fun_facts.tiny: Baby hammerheads are born with soft, bendy heads that harden as they grow.
Their heads work like treasure detectors to find fish hiding under the sand.
Some hammerheads swim in groups of more than a hundred during the day.
did_you_know.young: A hammerhead can see above and below at the same time with no blind spots
Their wide heads help them make sharp turns while swimming
Hammerheads use special sensors in their heads to find fish hiding in the sand
Some hammerheads swim in groups of over 100 sharks during the day
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a car, with a head shaped like a hammer — around 13 feet long!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as five or six grown-ups — around 990 pounds.
text.map_narration: Hammerhead sharks swim in warm tropical oceans all around the world.
text.sound_description.young: They are silent swimmers, but you might hear a splash when they jump out of the water.

text.summary.young: Whale sharks are the biggest fish in the ocean, living in warm tropical waters around the world. They can grow as long as a school bus but only eat tiny plankton and fish eggs by filtering ocean water through their mouths.
text.summary.tiny: Whale sharks are the biggest fish in the whole ocean — as long as a school bus! They swim with their giant mouths wide open, gulping water to catch the tiniest food.
fun_facts.young: Whale sharks have about 3,000 tiny teeth, but they don't use them to eat.
A whale shark's mouth can be 1.5 metres wide — big enough for a person to stand in.
They are gentle giants that sometimes let divers swim beside them.
They can live for over 100 years, making them one of the longest-living fish.
Their spotted pattern helps them blend in with sunlight filtering through the water.
Scientists use the spot patterns to identify individual whale sharks, just like we use names.
fun_facts.tiny: A whale shark's mouth is so big you could stand inside it.
They've got thousands of teeny tiny teeth but never use them to eat.
Every whale shark has its own special pattern of spots that no other whale shark has.
did_you_know.young: A whale shark can filter over 6,000 litres of water every hour to catch tiny food.
Each whale shark has a unique pattern of spots, like a fingerprint that never matches another whale shark.
They swim with their mouths wide open to scoop up plankton and small fish.
Baby whale sharks are born about 40–60 centimetres long, and scientists still don't know where they are born.
They can dive deeper than 1,800 metres into the ocean.
text.size_comparison.young: The biggest fish in the entire ocean — longer than a school bus, around 40 feet long!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as three school buses — around 40,000 pounds.
text.map_narration: Whale sharks swim in warm tropical oceans all around the world.
text.sound_description.young: They are quiet and don't make sounds that humans can hear.

text.summary.young: Orcas are large black and white dolphins that live in oceans all around the world. Each orca family has its own special language of clicks and whistles that no other family uses.
text.summary.tiny: Orcas are enormous black and white dolphins — they're the biggest dolphins in the whole ocean! Every orca family speaks its own special language that no other family uses.
fun_facts.young: Orcas teach their babies how to hunt — young orcas learn by watching their mothers for years.
Different orca families eat different foods — some only eat fish, while others hunt seals or even sharks!
They can swim as fast as a car drives through a neighbourhood — up to 35 miles per hour!
Baby orcas drink their mother's milk for up to two years.
They sleep by resting half their brain at a time — one side sleeps while the other watches for danger!
With incredible teamwork, orcas hunt together in family groups using clever strategies to catch their prey.
fun_facts.tiny: They teach their babies how to hunt — the little ones watch their mothers for years.
Some orca families only eat fish, while others hunt seals or even sharks!
Baby orcas drink their mother's milk for up to two years.
did_you_know.young: They are actually dolphins, not whales — they're the biggest dolphins in the ocean!
These dolphins have different accents! Each family pod makes unique sounds that scientists can recognize.
They hunt in teams and work together to catch food, just like wolf packs do on land.
An orca's white eye patch is actually above its real eye — it tricks other animals about where the orca is looking!
They can live as long as humans — some grandma orcas are over 80 years old!
text.size_comparison.young: They're about as long as two cars parked end to end — roughly 23 feet from nose to tail.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as 300 kids put together — around 12,000 pounds.
text.map_narration: Orcas live in every ocean on Earth, from the Arctic to the Antarctic.
text.sound_description.young: They make clicking sounds to find food and whistles to talk to their family.

text.summary.young: Blue whales are the largest animals that have ever lived on Earth, swimming in oceans all around the world. A blue whale's heart is as big as a small car, and its call can be heard over 1,600 kilometres away underwater.
text.summary.tiny: Blue whales are the biggest animals that have ever lived — bigger than any dinosaur. A blue whale's heart is as big as a small car.
fun_facts.young: Blue whales are not actually blue — they look blue-grey underwater but grey on the surface.
A blue whale's heart beats only 2 times per minute when it dives deep.
They have no teeth — they use baleen plates like a giant comb to filter tiny krill from the water.
They are louder than a jet engine — their calls reach 188 decibels.
A newborn blue whale is already 7 metres long and weighs 3 tonnes.
They swim slowly most of the time, cruising at about 8 kilometres per hour.
fun_facts.tiny: A blue whale's tongue weighs as much as an elephant.
Baby blue whales drink so much milk they get heavier than you every single day.
They have no teeth — they catch tiny creatures through a giant comb in their mouth.
did_you_know.young: A blue whale's tongue weighs as much as an elephant.
They eat up to 4 tonnes of tiny krill every day.
A blue whale's blood vessels are so wide that a small child could swim through them.
They can hold their breath for up to 90 minutes underwater.
A baby blue whale drinks 200 litres of milk every day and gains 90 kilograms each day.
text.size_comparison.young: The biggest animal that has ever lived — longer than three school buses parked end to end, around 100 feet!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh more than twenty elephants all together — around 330,000 pounds.
text.map_narration: Blue whales swim in every ocean on Earth.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep singing and rumbling sounds that travel for thousands of kilometres through the ocean.

text.summary.young: Dolphins are playful ocean mammals that live in seas and oceans around the world. They sleep with one eye open, switching off half their brain at a time so they can keep breathing and stay safe.
text.summary.tiny: Dolphins sleep with one eye open! They switch off half their brain at a time so they can breathe and stay safe.
fun_facts.young: Dolphins leap out of the water to save energy when swimming fast.
They work together to catch fish by swimming in circles around them.
Baby dolphins stay close to their mothers for up to three years.
They have excellent eyesight both above and below water.
They can recognize themselves in a mirror.
They help injured friends by pushing them to the surface to breathe.
fun_facts.tiny: They leap out of the water to save energy when they're swimming fast.
They help injured friends by pushing them up to breathe.
Baby dolphins stay with their mothers for up to three years.
did_you_know.young: They sleep with one eye open and half their brain awake.
They can swim up to 30 kilometers per hour.
They use clicking sounds to find fish in dark water.
Each dolphin has its own special whistle that works like a name.
They can hold their breath for up to 15 minutes.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a grown-up lying down — around 8 feet from nose to tail.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as two or three grown-ups — around 440 pounds.
text.map_narration: Dolphins live in oceans all around the world, and some even live in rivers.
text.sound_description.young: They make clicking sounds to find food and whistling sounds to talk to each other.

sea_turtle.name: Sea Turtle
sea_turtle.habitat: Warm tropical oceans and sandy beaches worldwide

text.summary.young: Sea turtles are ancient reptiles with flippers that glide through warm oceans all around the world. They swim thousands of kilometres back to the exact beach where they hatched to lay their own eggs — using Earth's magnetic field like a built-in compass.
text.summary.tiny: Sea turtles glide through warm oceans with flippers like wings. They swim back to the exact beach where they were born to lay their own eggs.
fun_facts.young: Baby sea turtles hatch at night and race to the ocean guided by moonlight on the waves.
Leatherback sea turtles can dive deeper than 1,200 metres — that's as deep as four Eiffel Towers stacked on top of each other.
Sea turtles can't pull their heads and flippers into their shells like land turtles can.
The temperature of the sand decides if baby sea turtles will be boys or girls — warmer sand makes more girls.
They have special glands near their eyes that help them drink ocean water without getting sick from the salt.
Hawksbill sea turtles eat sponges that would be poisonous to most other animals.
fun_facts.tiny: Baby sea turtles hatch at night and race to the waves following the moonlight.
The sand's warmth decides if babies will be boys or girls — warmer sand makes more girls.
They have been swimming in the ocean since dinosaurs roamed the Earth.
did_you_know.young: They can hold their breath underwater for up to 7 hours while resting.
A sea turtle's shell is part of its skeleton — it can't crawl out of it.
Female sea turtles cry salty tears on the beach to get rid of extra salt from seawater.
They have been swimming in the ocean since the time of dinosaurs — over 100 million years ago.
Green sea turtles turn green because they eat so much sea grass and algae.
text.size_comparison.young: Their shell is about as wide as a bathtub — around 3 feet across.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as two grown-ups — around 286 pounds.
text.map_narration: Sea turtles swim in warm and tropical oceans all around the world.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft chirping and grunting sounds, especially when they're baby hatchlings or when they come up to breathe.

text.summary.young: Octopuses are soft-bodied sea animals with eight long arms covered in suckers. They have three hearts, blue blood, and nine brains — one main brain plus a mini-brain in each arm that can think on its own!
text.summary.tiny: An octopus has eight bendy arms covered in sticky suckers. It's got three hearts and nine brains!
fun_facts.young: Octopuses have three hearts — two pump blood to their gills and one pumps blood to the rest of their body.
When an octopus swims fast, its main heart stops beating!
An octopus can regrow a lost arm in just a few months.
They have no bones at all — their whole body is squishy and bendy.
An octopus tastes with its suckers because they have taste sensors all over them.
Some octopuses build little gardens of shells and rocks around their dens.
fun_facts.tiny: An octopus can squeeze through any gap bigger than its mouth.
It tastes everything with its arms.
When it swims really fast, one of its hearts stops beating!
did_you_know.young: An octopus can squeeze through any opening bigger than its hard beak — even a tiny crack!
They can change color in less than a second to match rocks, sand, or coral.
Each octopus arm has its own mini-brain, so the arms can taste and explore on their own.
An octopus has blue blood instead of red blood because it uses copper instead of iron.
They are so smart they can open jars, solve puzzles, and even recognize human faces.
text.size_comparison.young: With arms stretched out, they can be as wide as a grown-up is tall — about 5 feet across!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a house cat — around 22 pounds.
text.map_narration: Octopuses live in oceans all around the world, from shallow reefs to the deep sea.
text.sound_description.young: They are usually silent, but you might hear splashing and gurgling as they move through the water.

text.summary.young: Giant squids are huge sea creatures that live deep in oceans all around the world. They have the biggest eyes of any animal on Earth — as big as a dinner plate — to see in the dark deep sea.
text.summary.tiny: Giant squids have eyes as big as dinner plates — the biggest eyes of any animal on Earth! They live deep in the ocean where it's completely dark.
fun_facts.young: Giant squids live so deep in the ocean that scientists rarely see them alive.
They use jet propulsion by shooting water out of their bodies to zoom backward through the ocean.
Their tentacles have rows of powerful suction cups lined with tiny teeth.
They can change color by controlling special cells in their skin.
Baby giant squids are only as big as your thumb when they hatch.
They hunt fish and smaller squids in the deep dark ocean where no sunlight reaches.
fun_facts.tiny: They can grow as long as a bus.
They zoom backward by shooting water out of their bodies.
Baby giant squids are only as big as your thumb.
did_you_know.young: A giant squid's eye is as big as a dinner plate!
They have eight long arms and two even longer feeding tentacles.
They can grow longer than a school bus.
They have three hearts to pump blood through their huge bodies.
Their beaks are as sharp as a parrot's and strong enough to cut through fish.
text.size_comparison.young: Longer than a school bus — around 43 feet from tentacle tip to tentacle tip!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as three or four grown-ups — around 606 pounds.
text.map_narration: Giant squids live deep in every ocean on Earth — so deep that humans have rarely seen one alive.
text.sound_description.young: They are silent hunters, but they make splashing sounds when they move through water.

text.summary.young: Jellyfish are soft sea animals with no bones that float through oceans all around the world. The immortal jellyfish can turn itself back into a baby when it gets old or stressed, so it might never die.
text.summary.tiny: Jellyfish are soft sea animals with no bones that float through oceans everywhere. One kind can turn itself back into a baby and might never die.
fun_facts.young: Jellyfish are about 95% water, so they look almost see-through.
They catch food using special stinging cells on their tentacles.
They move by squeezing their bell-shaped body like a pump.
Some jellyfish are tiny as your fingernail, others are bigger than a person.
Moon jellyfish can make copies of themselves without needing a partner.
Box jellyfish have 24 eyes even though they don't have a brain to see with.
fun_facts.tiny: They're see-through because they're mostly water.
They catch food with stinging arms called tentacles.
Some are tiny as your fingernail and others are bigger than your dad.
did_you_know.young: They have been floating in Earth's oceans for over 500 million years — that's before dinosaurs existed!
Some jellyfish glow in the dark and light up the ocean at night.
They don't have brains, hearts, or bones — they're mostly made of water.
A group of jellyfish floating together is called a bloom or a smack.
text.size_comparison.young: Some are as small as your thumbnail, others have tentacles longer than a blue whale!
text.weight_comparison.young: Most jellyfish weigh about as much as a bag of sugar — around 4 pounds. They're almost all water!
text.map_narration: Jellyfish float in every ocean on Earth, from the surface to the deep sea.
text.sound_description.young: They are silent and don't make any sounds at all.

starfish.name: Starfish
starfish.habitat: Ocean floors and coral reefs worldwide

text.summary.young: Starfish are ocean animals with five arms that live in seas all around the world. They have no brain and no blood — instead, they pump seawater through their bodies to move and breathe.
text.summary.tiny: Starfish have five arms and no brain or blood — they pump seawater through their bodies instead. They live on the ocean floor all around the world.
fun_facts.young: Starfish aren't actually fish — they're more closely related to sea urchins.
They move using hundreds of tiny tube feet on the bottom of their arms.
Some starfish can live for 35 years in the ocean.
They eat clams and mussels by pulling their shells open with their strong arms.
If a starfish is flipped upside down, it can flip itself back over using its arms.
Baby starfish are so tiny they float in the ocean like specks of dust.
fun_facts.tiny: They walk using hundreds of tiny suckers underneath their arms.
If a starfish loses an arm, it can grow a brand new one.
A starfish's mouth is right in the middle of its tummy.
did_you_know.young: They can regrow a lost arm in about a year.
Some starfish have more than five arms — sun stars can have up to 40!
They don't have eyes like we do, but they have light sensors on the tip of each arm.
A starfish's mouth is on the bottom of its body, right in the center.
They can push their stomachs outside their bodies to eat their food.
text.size_comparison.young: Most starfish are about as wide as your hand — around 10 inches across.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a loaf of bread — around 1 pound.
text.map_narration: Starfish live in every ocean on Earth, from warm tropical reefs to cold polar waters.
text.sound_description.young: They don't make sounds that we can hear.

seahorse.name: Seahorse
seahorse.habitat: Shallow coastal waters with seagrass and coral

text.summary.young: Seahorses are tiny fish that live in warm ocean waters around the world. Male seahorses carry babies in a special pouch on their belly and give birth to up to 2,000 tiny seahorses at once.
text.summary.tiny: Seahorses are tiny fish that swim standing up and hold onto plants with their curly tail. Daddy seahorses carry the babies in a special pouch and give birth to hundreds of tiny seahorses.
fun_facts.young: Seahorses swim upright, not flat like other fish.
A seahorse can eat up to 3,000 tiny shrimp in one day.
Baby seahorses are called fry and are smaller than a grain of rice when they're born.
They use their curly tail like an anchor to hold onto plants so waves don't wash them away.
A seahorse's head looks like a tiny horse, which is how they got their name.
They have bony armor instead of scales to protect their bodies.
fun_facts.tiny: A seahorse can eat three thousand tiny shrimp in one day.
Baby seahorses are smaller than a grain of rice when they're born.
A seahorse's eyes can look in two different directions at once.
did_you_know.young: They are the only animals where dads get pregnant and give birth to babies.
A seahorse's tail can grab onto seaweed like a monkey's tail grabs branches.
They have no teeth and no stomach — they suck up food through their snout like a vacuum.
Each of a seahorse's eyes can look in different directions at the same time.
They mate for life and dance together every morning to say hello.
text.size_comparison.young: Most seahorses are about as long as your finger — tiny and curly!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as an egg — almost nothing at all.
text.map_narration: Seahorses live in shallow warm waters around the world, hiding in seagrass and coral.
text.sound_description.young: They make tiny clicking sounds by snapping their head while they eat.

text.summary.young: Manta rays are huge, gentle fish that glide through warm oceans around the world. They have the biggest brain of any fish and can recognise themselves in a mirror — just like dolphins and elephants!
text.summary.tiny: Manta rays are huge, gentle fish that glide through warm oceans like underwater birds. They have the biggest brain of any fish!
fun_facts.young: Manta rays can grow as wide as a small car.
They eat tiny floating animals called plankton by filtering water through their mouths.
They do somersaults underwater to catch more food.
They are very friendly and sometimes swim up to scuba divers.
Baby manta rays are called pups and are born knowing how to swim.
They have no stinger — unlike their stingray cousins!
fun_facts.tiny: They can grow as wide as a small car.
They do somersaults underwater to catch more food.
Baby manta rays are called pups and they're born knowing how to swim.
did_you_know.young: They have the largest brain of any fish in the ocean.
They can recognise themselves in a mirror — only a few animals can do this!
They never stop swimming, even when they sleep.
Each manta ray has unique spots on its belly, like a fingerprint.
They can live for 40 to 50 years in the wild.
text.size_comparison.young: With their wings spread wide, they can be as wide as a car is long — around 18 feet across!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a small car — around 3,100 pounds.
text.map_narration: Manta rays glide through warm tropical and subtropical oceans around the world.
text.sound_description.young: They are silent swimmers — they don't make sounds we can hear.

clownfish.name: Clownfish
clownfish.habitat: Coral reefs in warm ocean waters

text.summary.young: Clownfish are small, bright orange fish that live in warm ocean waters near coral reefs. All clownfish are born male, and the biggest one can change into a female when needed.
text.summary.tiny: Clownfish are bright orange fish with white stripes who live inside sea flowers called anemones. They're born boys, and the biggest one becomes a girl.
fun_facts.young: Clownfish cover themselves in special mucus so anemone tentacles won't sting them
A clownfish dad protects hundreds of eggs until they hatch
They do a special wiggle dance when they meet their anemone for the first time
Baby clownfish are so tiny they're almost see-through when they're born
They can recognize their family members by sight
The female clownfish is always the largest and strongest fish in the group
fun_facts.tiny: Their dads guard hundreds of tiny eggs and fan them with their fins to keep them clean.
They cover themselves in slimy mucus so the anemone's stinging arms won't hurt them.
Baby clownfish are so small and clear you can almost see right through them.
did_you_know.young: They sleep in the tentacles of sea anemones at night
A clownfish's stripes are like fingerprints — each pattern is unique
They make clicking and popping sounds to talk to each other
The father clownfish guards the eggs and fans them with his fins to keep them clean
They can live their entire lives without leaving their anemone home
text.size_comparison.young: Only about as long as your finger — tiny and bright orange!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh less than a single cookie — almost nothing at all.
text.map_narration: Clownfish live among the colourful anemones of warm tropical oceans in the Pacific and Indian Ocean.
text.sound_description.young: They make little clicking and popping sounds to communicate with their family.

moray_eel.name: Moray Eel
moray_eel.habitat: Coral reefs and rocky ocean floors

text.summary.young: Moray eels are long, snake-like fish that live in coral reefs and rocky crevices in warm ocean waters around the world. They have a second set of jaws hidden in their throat that shoot forward to grab prey and pull it down into their stomach.
text.summary.tiny: Moray eels hide in rocky holes with their mouths wide open — they're just breathing! They have special jaws hidden in their throat that shoot forward like a monster in a movie.
fun_facts.young: Moray eels sleep during the day with their mouths open to breathe
They have terrible eyesight and hunt mostly by smell
Some moray eels can grow as long as a car
Their second throat jaws are called pharyngeal jaws
They sometimes team up with grouper fish to hunt together
They can live in the same hiding spot for years
fun_facts.tiny: They hunt by smell because they can't see very well.
Some grow as long as your family's car.
They can tie themselves in a knot to pull food apart.
did_you_know.young: They have a second set of jaws in their throat that shoot forward to grab food
They breathe by opening and closing their mouths, which makes them look scary but they're just breathing
They have no scales — their skin is covered in slimy mucus that protects them
They can tie their body in a knot to help them rip apart food or escape danger
text.size_comparison.young: Long and snaky — about as long as a grown-up is tall, around 5 feet.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a big bag of dog food — around 66 pounds.
text.map_narration: Moray eels live in warm tropical and subtropical oceans, hiding in rocky crevices and coral reefs.
text.sound_description.young: They make snapping sounds with their jaws and sometimes hiss when they feel threatened.

text.summary.young: Narwhals are whales with a long spiral tusk that live in the icy Arctic Ocean. Their tusk is actually a giant tooth that grows through their lip and can sense changes in the water around them.
text.summary.tiny: Narwhals are whales with a long twisty tusk growing right through their lip. That tusk is really a giant tooth that can feel tiny changes in the water.
fun_facts.young: Narwhals travel in groups called pods with 10 to 100 friends.
They eat fish, squid, and shrimp from the deep, cold ocean.
They can hold their breath underwater for up to 25 minutes.
Their skin changes color as they grow — babies are blue-gray, and adults get spotty.
Scientists think narwhals rub their tusks together to clean them or say hello.
They have no dorsal fin on their back, which helps them swim under thick ice.
fun_facts.tiny: They swim in groups called pods with up to a hundred friends.
They can hold their breath underwater for as long as you'd watch a whole TV show.
Baby narwhals are blue-grey, and grown-ups get spotty.
did_you_know.young: A narwhal's tusk can grow up to 10 feet long — that's taller than most ceilings!
Only male narwhals usually grow tusks, though some females do too.
They can dive almost a mile deep into the ocean to find food.
Their tusk is packed with millions of tiny nerve endings that help them sense the water.
They are sometimes called the unicorns of the sea because of their magical-looking tusk.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a large car — with a spiral tusk that can be 10 feet long all by itself!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a small car — around 3,300 pounds.
text.map_narration: Narwhals live in the freezing Arctic waters near Canada, Greenland, and Russia.
text.sound_description.young: They click, whistle, and squeal to talk to each other underwater.

text.summary.young: Beluga whales are white whales that live in the cold Arctic Ocean. They're called the canaries of the sea because they make so many chirps, whistles, and clicks that you can hear them right through a boat!
text.summary.tiny: Beluga whales are white whales that sing so loudly underwater you can hear them through a boat. People call them the canaries of the sea!
fun_facts.young: Beluga whales don't have a dorsal fin on their back — this helps them swim under ice.
They use echolocation to find fish hiding under thick sea ice.
Belugas shed their skin every summer by rubbing against gravel on the ocean floor.
They can make their lips into different shapes to create unique sounds.
They often travel in groups called pods with 10 or more whales.
They can dive down 700 meters deep and hold their breath for 25 minutes!
fun_facts.tiny: Baby belugas are born grey and turn white as they grow.
They can swim backwards and turn their heads side to side.
Belugas squeeze their forehead to make different sounds.
did_you_know.young: They can swim backward — most whales can't do that!
Their neck bones aren't fused together, so they can turn their heads from side to side.
Belugas can change the shape of their forehead to make different sounds.
A beluga's white color helps it hide in icy Arctic waters.
Baby belugas are born dark gray and slowly turn white as they grow up.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a large car — round and white like a swimming snowball, around 15 feet long.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a small car — around 3,100 pounds.
text.map_narration: Beluga whales live in the cold Arctic and sub-Arctic oceans.
text.sound_description.young: They click, whistle, chirp, and clang — they're so loud you can hear them through the bottom of a boat!

sea_lion.name: Sea Lion
sea_lion.habitat: Rocky coastlines and beaches of the Pacific and Southern Oceans

text.summary.young: Sea lions are playful ocean animals with flippers and whiskers that live along coastlines of the Pacific and Southern Oceans. They are the only seal family that can walk on land using all four flippers like legs — true seals can only wriggle on their bellies.
text.summary.tiny: Sea lions are the ocean's acrobats with whiskers and flippers that work like legs. They're the only seals that can walk on land using all four flippers.
fun_facts.young: Sea lions can rotate their back flippers forward to walk on land like a four-legged animal.
They have ear flaps on the outside of their heads — seals have ears but no flaps you can see.
A sea lion's whiskers are so sensitive they can feel a fish swimming by in complete darkness.
They love to play and often surf on ocean waves just for fun.
Mother sea lions can recognize their pup's bark out of thousands of other sea lion voices.
They are very smart and can be trained to do tricks and even help scientists.
fun_facts.tiny: They surf on waves just for fun.
Their whiskers can feel a fish swimming past in total darkness.
A mother sea lion knows her pup's bark out of thousands of other voices.
did_you_know.young: They can hold their breath underwater for up to 20 minutes while hunting for fish.
They have special whiskers that help them find fish in dark, murky water.
They can swim as fast as 25 miles per hour — that's faster than most boats!
Baby sea lions are called pups and they can swim when they're just two weeks old.
They bark loudly to talk to each other, just like dogs do.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a grown-up lying down — around 8 feet from nose to flippers.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as three or four grown-ups — around 660 pounds.
text.map_narration: Sea lions live along the coasts of the Pacific Ocean, from Alaska down to Australia.
text.sound_description.young: They bark loudly like dogs, especially when they're talking to each other or protecting their space.

text.summary.young: Jaguars are big spotted cats that live in the rainforests of South America and Central America. They have the strongest bite of any big cat and can bite straight through a turtle's shell or even a skull!
text.summary.tiny: Jaguars are big spotted cats with the strongest bite of any cat in the world. They can crunch straight through a turtle's shell!
fun_facts.young: A jaguar's bite is so powerful it can crack open a turtle's hard shell like a nut.
Jaguars sometimes catch fish by slapping them out of the water with their paws.
Their name comes from a Native American word meaning 'he who kills with one leap.'
Black jaguars aren't a different species — they just have extra dark fur, and you can still see their spots in bright light.
They can see six times better in the dark than humans can.
They're the third largest cats in the world, after tigers and lions.
fun_facts.tiny: They love swimming and catch fish by slapping them out of the water.
Black jaguars still have spots — you can see them shining in bright sunlight.
They can see six times better in the dark than you can.
did_you_know.young: They love swimming and are excellent hunters in water.
Their spotted coat helps them hide in the shadows of the jungle.
They hunt alone and are most active at night.
They can climb trees and sometimes drag their prey up into branches.
Unlike most cats, jaguars don't avoid water — they actually seek it out!
text.size_comparison.young: Powerful and stocky, they reach your shoulders — around 2 feet 6 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as two grown-ups — around 220 pounds.
text.map_narration: Jaguars prowl through the dense rainforests and wetlands of Central and South America.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep roars and growls, and also make friendly chuffing sounds to say hello to other jaguars.

text.summary.young: Sloths are slow-moving animals that live high in the rainforest trees of Central and South America. They move so slowly that green algae grows in their fur, which helps them blend in with the leaves around them.
text.summary.tiny: Sloths hang upside down in rainforest trees and move so slowly that green algae grows in their fur. They're brilliant swimmers and can hold their breath underwater longer than you can hold yours!
fun_facts.young: Sloths hang upside down from tree branches using their long, curved claws.
A sloth can turn its head almost all the way around — like an owl!
They eat leaves, shoots, and fruit from the trees where they live.
Baby sloths cling to their mother's belly for the first few months of life.
They move so slowly that it can take them a whole minute just to climb one meter.
Some moths and beetles live in a sloth's fur and nowhere else on Earth!
fun_facts.tiny: A sloth only comes down from its tree once a week to poo.
They can turn their heads almost all the way around, just like owls.
Baby sloths cling to their mum's tummy for months and months.
did_you_know.young: They sleep up to 20 hours every single day.
A sloth only poops once a week — and they climb all the way down from their tree to do it!
They are such good swimmers that they can hold their breath underwater for up to 40 minutes.
A sloth's fur grows in the opposite direction from most animals — from their belly toward their back — so rain runs off easily.
They have been around for millions of years — even before the dinosaurs disappeared!
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as your arm — they curl up into a fuzzy ball about the size of a big pillow.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a couple bags of sugar — around 11 pounds.
text.map_narration: Sloths live high up in the trees of Central and South American rainforests.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft squeaking and chirping sounds, and sometimes hiss when they feel scared.

text.summary.young: Toucans are colorful tropical birds that live in the rainforests of Central and South America. Their enormous, brightly colored beaks are hollow and lightweight, helping them stay cool in the hot jungle.
text.summary.tiny: Toucans have the most enormous beaks you've ever seen — as long as your whole arm! Their beaks are bright rainbow colours but light as a feather because they're hollow inside.
fun_facts.young: Toucans live in small flocks and love to play by tossing fruit to each other.
Their beaks are made of lightweight hollow bone covered in a hard shell.
They eat mostly fruit, but sometimes snack on insects, eggs, or lizards.
They make their nests in tree holes high up in the rainforest canopy.
They can live up to 20 years in the wild.
Each species of toucan has a different pattern of bright colors on its beak.
fun_facts.tiny: They toss fruit to each other like they're playing catch.
They sleep by tucking their beaks under their wings and folding their tails right over their heads.
Baby toucans are born with tiny beaks that grow bigger and bigger as they get older.
did_you_know.young: A toucan's beak can be longer than its entire body!
They sleep by tucking their beaks under their wings and folding their tails over their heads.
Baby toucans are born with tiny beaks that grow bigger as they get older.
They use their beaks to reach fruit on branches too thin to land on.
A toucan's beak has special blood vessels that release heat like a radiator to keep the bird cool.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a school ruler — and a third of that is their enormous colourful beak!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a loaf of bread — around 1 pound.
text.map_narration: Toucans live in the tropical forests of Central and South America.
text.sound_description.young: They make loud croaking and rattling calls that sound like frogs in the treetops.

text.summary.young: Macaws are big, colorful parrots that live in the rainforests of South and Central America. They eat clay from riverbanks to help their bodies handle poison from unripe seeds.
text.summary.tiny: Macaws are huge, colorful parrots with feathers like rainbows. They eat clay from riverbanks to stop poison from seeds making them sick.
fun_facts.young: Macaw feathers come in almost every color of the rainbow — red, blue, green, yellow, and orange.
They use their beaks like an extra foot to climb trees.
A macaw's tongue has a bone inside it that helps it grip and taste food.
They are so smart they can learn to say over 100 words.
Wild macaws travel in flocks and can be heard squawking from a mile away.
They sleep standing up on one foot with their heads tucked under their wings.
fun_facts.tiny: A macaw's beak is strong enough to crack nuts you'd need a hammer for.
They talk to each other with squawks so loud you'd hear them from streets and streets away.
They sleep standing on one foot with their head tucked under a wing.
did_you_know.young: They can crack open Brazil nuts with their beaks — nuts so hard that humans need a hammer!
A macaw's beak is so strong it can snap a broomstick in half.
They mate for life and stay with the same partner for 50 years or more.
Baby macaws are born completely naked without any feathers.
They can fly up to 35 miles per hour through the jungle.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as your arm — with a long, colourful tail that makes up half their length!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a carton of milk — around 3 pounds.
text.map_narration: Macaws live in the tropical rainforests of Central and South America.
text.sound_description.young: They make loud squawking and screeching sounds that echo through the jungle.

poison_dart_frog.name: Poison Dart Frog
poison_dart_frog.habitat: Rainforest floors in Central and South America

text.summary.young: Poison dart frogs are tiny, colorful frogs that live in the rainforests of Central and South America. Their bright colors warn other animals that their skin contains poison from the insects they eat.
text.summary.tiny: Poison dart frogs are tiny rainforest frogs with the brightest colours you've ever seen. Their skin is poisonous, and those amazing colours tell other animals to stay away.
fun_facts.young: The golden poison dart frog is the most poisonous — it's bright yellow and smaller than a bottle cap.
Indigenous people in Colombia used the frogs' poison on their hunting arrows.
Poison dart frogs can be red, blue, yellow, green, or even spotted like strawberries.
They're active during the day, unlike most frogs that come out at night.
Each female frog lays only 3 to 5 eggs at a time.
Mother frogs feed their tadpoles unfertilized eggs until they grow legs.
fun_facts.tiny: They're smaller than your hand but some are poisonous enough to make a jaguar very sick.
Dad frogs carry their babies on their backs and take them swimming in tiny pools high up in the trees.
They can be bright blue, fiery red, sunshine yellow, or spotty like strawberries.
did_you_know.young: They get their poison from eating toxic ants and mites in the wild.
Their bright colors are a warning sign that says 'Don't eat me — I'm poisonous!'
Some poison dart frogs are so toxic that one frog has enough poison to harm ten grown people.
Male poison dart frogs carry their tadpoles on their backs to water pools in tree branches.
Frogs raised in zoos are not poisonous because they eat different insects.
text.size_comparison.young: Smaller than your thumb — tiny enough to sit on a coin!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh less than a single coin — you'd need hundreds to fill a teaspoon.
text.map_narration: Poison dart frogs live on the rainforest floors of Central and South America.
text.sound_description.young: They make high-pitched chirping and trilling sounds to call to each other.

anaconda.name: Anaconda
anaconda.habitat: Rivers and swamps in South America

text.summary.young: Anacondas are giant snakes that live in rivers and swamps in South America. They are the heaviest snakes in the world and can swallow animals as big as a deer whole!
text.summary.tiny: Anacondas are the heaviest snakes in the whole world. They live in rivers and swamps and can swallow animals as big as a deer!
fun_facts.young: Anacondas don't chew their food — they swallow it whole!
Their jaws can open super wide to fit big animals inside
They squeeze their prey tight before swallowing it
They are excellent swimmers and spend most of their time in water
Female anacondas are much bigger than males
They shed their skin as they grow, just like other snakes
fun_facts.tiny: They don't chew — they swallow everything whole.
Their jaws open super wide to fit big animals inside.
They're brilliant swimmers and love being in water.
did_you_know.young: An anaconda can go months without eating after a big meal
They give birth to live babies instead of laying eggs
They can hold their breath underwater for 10 minutes
Their eyes and nose are on top of their head so they can breathe while hiding in water
A baby anaconda is about as long as a ruler when it's born
text.size_comparison.young: One of the longest snakes in the world — about as long as a large car, around 20 feet!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a grown-up and a half — around 220 pounds.
text.map_narration: Green anacondas live in the swamps and rivers of South America, especially the Amazon.
text.sound_description.young: They make a loud hissing sound when they feel threatened or want to be left alone.

capybara.name: Capybara
capybara.habitat: Rivers, lakes, and wetlands in South America

text.summary.young: Capybaras are the world's largest rodents and live near rivers and lakes in South America. They're so calm and friendly that birds, monkeys, and even cats sit on their backs like living chairs!
text.summary.tiny: Capybaras are the biggest rodents in the whole world. They're so calm and friendly that birds and monkeys sit on their backs like comfy chairs!
fun_facts.young: Capybaras eat their own poop to get extra vitamins from their food.
Their teeth never stop growing, so they chew tough grasses to keep them short.
They love to take mud baths to cool off on hot days.
They're related to guinea pigs, but they're about 100 times bigger!
They make friends with almost every animal they meet.
Their eyes, ears, and nose are all on top of their head so they can see and breathe while swimming.
fun_facts.tiny: Their teeth never stop growing, so they chew grass all day to keep them short.
They can hold their breath underwater while they hide.
Baby capybaras can run and swim on the day they're born!
did_you_know.young: They have webbed feet like ducks to help them swim.
They can hold their breath underwater for up to 5 minutes.
They sleep in the water with just their noses sticking out.
A group of capybaras is called a herd, and they live together in groups of 10 to 20.
Baby capybaras can run and swim within hours of being born.
text.size_comparison.young: The world's biggest rodent reaches your belly — around 2 feet at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a grown-up — around 132 pounds.
text.map_narration: Capybaras live near rivers, lakes, and wetlands across South America.
text.sound_description.young: They squeak, bark, purr, and whistle to talk to each other.

text.summary.young: Howler monkeys live high in the rainforest trees of Central and South America. They are the loudest land animals on Earth — their calls can be heard from 5 kilometres away!
text.summary.tiny: Howler monkeys are the loudest animals on land. Their roaring calls can be heard as far away as your house is from the shops — if you drove for five minutes!
fun_facts.young: Howler monkeys eat leaves, fruits, and flowers.
They live in groups of 10 to 20 monkeys.
Their howls help them avoid fights with other monkey groups.
They rarely come down from the trees.
They have a special stomach that helps them digest tough leaves.
Male howler monkeys have the loudest calls in the group.
fun_facts.tiny: They spend most of their day resting in the treetops.
Their tail is so strong it can hold them up like an extra arm.
They eat leaves, fruit and flowers high in the trees.
did_you_know.young: They have a special bone in their throat that makes their voice super loud.
They howl the most at sunrise and sunset to tell other monkey groups where they are.
They spend most of their day resting and digesting leaves.
Their tail is so strong it can hold their whole body weight like an extra hand.
Baby howler monkeys cling to their mother's belly for the first few weeks of life.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as your arm — but their howl can be heard 3 miles away!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a small watermelon — around 18 pounds.
text.map_narration: Howler monkeys live in the forests of Central and South America.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep, loud roaring howls that sound like a strong wind blowing through the trees.

text.summary.young: Spider monkeys live high in the rainforest trees of Central and South America. Their tail works like a fifth hand — it's so strong they can hang upside down by just their tail while they eat!
text.summary.tiny: Spider monkeys live high in the rainforest trees. Their tail works like a fifth hand!
fun_facts.young: Spider monkeys don't have thumbs — their four long fingers work like hooks for swinging.
They eat mostly fruit, but also munch on leaves, flowers, and sometimes insects.
They help plant new trees by pooping out seeds as they travel through the forest.
They live in groups of 15 to 25 monkeys and make lots of noise to talk to each other.
They can recognize themselves in a mirror — not many animals can do that!
Their arms are longer than their legs, which makes them super fast swingers.
fun_facts.tiny: They don't have thumbs — their four long fingers work like hooks for swinging.
Their arms are longer than their legs, which makes them super fast swingers.
They can recognize themselves in a mirror — not many animals can do that!
did_you_know.young: A spider monkey's tail has special skin on the tip that works like fingerprints — it helps them grip branches.
They almost never come down to the ground — they spend their whole lives swinging through the treetops!
When spider monkeys hang by their arms and tail, they look like giant spiders — that's how they got their name.
