They can swing up to 40 feet from tree to tree — that's longer than a school bus!
Baby spider monkeys cling to their mother's belly for the first few months, riding along as she swings through the trees.
text.size_comparison.young: Their body is about the size of a big teddy bear — but with extra-long arms and a tail that grips like a hand!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a small watermelon — around 18 pounds.
text.map_narration: Spider monkeys swing through the tropical forests of Central and South America.
text.sound_description.young: They make loud screeches, barks, and chattering sounds to talk to their friends in the trees.

orangutan.name: Orangutan
orangutan.habitat: Rainforest trees in Borneo and Sumatra

text.summary.young: Orangutans are great apes with long orange fur that live high in the rainforest trees of Borneo and Sumatra. Every single night, they build a brand new sleeping nest out of branches and leaves — like making a cozy treehouse bed before bedtime.
text.summary.tiny: Orangutans have long orange fur and spend their whole lives high in the rainforest trees. Every single night, they build a brand new sleeping nest out of branches.
fun_facts.young: Orangutans spend almost their whole lives up in the trees — they rarely come down to the ground.
They have super strong hands and feet that grip branches like built-in hooks.
They are incredibly smart and can use sticks as tools to get bugs out of tree holes.
They eat over 300 different kinds of fruit in the rainforest.
Male orangutans have big puffy cheeks that make their faces look round and wide.
They can swing from tree to tree using their super long arms — this is called brachiating.
fun_facts.tiny: Their arms are so long they can touch their ankles without bending over.
Male orangutans have big puffy cheeks that make their faces look round and wide.
Baby orangutans stay with their mothers for up to eight years — longer than almost any other animal.
did_you_know.young: They are the largest animals that live in trees.
Their arms are so long they can touch their ankles without bending over.
Baby orangutans stay with their mothers for up to eight years — longer than almost any other animal.
Some smart orangutans use big leaves as umbrellas when it rains.
The word 'orangutan' means 'person of the forest' in the Malay language.
text.size_comparison.young: Their arms can stretch wider than a grown-up is tall — about 7 feet across!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a grown-up — around 176 pounds.
text.map_narration: Orangutans live in the tropical rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra in Southeast Asia.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep hooting calls, soft grunts, and long grumbling sounds to talk to each other in the trees.

text.summary.young: Tapirs are large forest animals with a short trunk-like snout, found in the rainforests of South America and Asia. They've barely changed for 35 million years — making them living fossils older than elephants!
text.summary.tiny: Tapirs have a bendy trunk-nose that works like a finger to grab leaves. They've looked almost the same for millions and millions of years — even before elephants!
fun_facts.young: Tapirs are related to horses and rhinos, not pigs or elephants.
They can run fast through thick jungle even though they look heavy.
They walk on four toes on their front feet and three on their back feet.
Their thick skin protects them from thorns and branches.
They mostly eat at night when the forest is cooler.
One tapir can eat 40 kilograms of plants in a single day.
fun_facts.tiny: Baby tapirs have stripes and spots like watermelons to help them hide.
They're brilliant swimmers and love splashing in rivers and ponds.
They help forests grow by pooping out seeds everywhere they wander.
did_you_know.young: Baby tapirs have stripes and spots like watermelons to hide in the forest.
They can hold their breath underwater for several minutes while hiding from predators.
Their flexible snout works like a finger to grab leaves and fruit.
They are excellent swimmers and love spending time in water.
They poop seeds all over the forest, helping new trees grow.
text.size_comparison.young: On all fours, they reach almost up to about your height — around 3 feet 3 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as three or four grown-ups — around 551 pounds.
text.map_narration: Tapirs live in the forests of Central and South America and Southeast Asia.
text.sound_description.young: They make high-pitched squeaks and whistles to talk to each other, and snort loudly when alarmed.

text.summary.young: Leafcutter ants live in big underground nests in Central and South America. They cut leaves and carry them home to grow special mushrooms that feed their whole family.
text.summary.tiny: Leafcutter ants cut pieces of leaf and carry them home like tiny green umbrellas. They're growing food underground — special mushrooms that feed their whole family.
fun_facts.young: Leafcutter ants make underground highways to march back and forth carrying leaves.
They chew leaves into tiny pieces and mix them with their spit to help the fungus grow.
Different ants have different jobs — some cut leaves, some carry them, and some guard the nest.
Their fungus gardens smell like fresh mushrooms.
A big leafcutter ant nest can be as wide as a house and go as deep as 20 feet underground!
They never sleep — they work day and night taking care of their garden.
fun_facts.tiny: They can carry leaf pieces heavier than your toy car.
Tiny baby ants ride on top of the leaves like passengers.
Their mushroom gardens smell fresh and earthy.
did_you_know.young: They can carry pieces of leaf 50 times heavier than their own body!
A leafcutter ant colony can have 8 million ants all working together.
The queen ant can live for 14 years and lay millions of eggs.
They have been farming mushrooms for 50 million years — long before humans learned to farm!
Tiny baby ants ride on top of the leaves to protect their bigger sisters from flies.
text.size_comparison.young: Smaller than your smallest fingernail — but they can carry leaf pieces bigger than their whole body!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh almost nothing — you'd need thousands just to equal one coin.
text.map_narration: Leafcutter ants live in the forests of Central and South America.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft rustling sounds as they march in long lines carrying leaves.

text.summary.young: Harpy eagles are huge, powerful birds that live in the rainforests of Central and South America. Their talons are as long as a grizzly bear's claws and strong enough to crush bones.
text.summary.tiny: Harpy eagles are the most powerful birds in the rainforest. Their claws are as long as a grizzly bear's.
fun_facts.young: Harpy eagles have feathers on their head that stand up like a crown when they're alert.
They can fly through thick rainforest branches without touching a single leaf.
Their eyesight is so sharp they can spot a sloth from 200 meters away.
They mate for life and raise only one chick every two or three years.
Their wings are short and broad — perfect for flying between rainforest trees.
They are named after harpies from Greek myths — creatures that were half woman and half bird.
fun_facts.tiny: They have crown feathers on their head that stand up when they're listening.
They can carry a monkey through the trees without dropping it.
Their eyes are so sharp they can spot a sloth hanging far away in the treetops.
did_you_know.young: A harpy eagle's talons can be 13 centimeters long — that's longer than your hand!
They can carry prey that weighs as much as half their own body weight through the trees.
They hunt monkeys and sloths high up in the rainforest canopy.
They build huge nests in the tallest trees that can be used for many years.
Baby harpy eagles stay with their parents for over a year learning to hunt.
text.size_comparison.young: One of the biggest eagles in the world — about 3 feet tall with claws as big as a grizzly bear's!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a small watermelon — around 18 pounds.
text.map_narration: Harpy eagles live in the tropical rainforests of Central and South America.
text.sound_description.young: They make loud screeching calls and high whistles to talk to each other in the rainforest.

text.summary.young: Okapis live in the rainforests of central Africa and are the only living relatives of giraffes. They have zebra stripes on their legs but a body like a small giraffe with a dark reddish-brown coat.
text.summary.tiny: Okapis are the only cousins of giraffes in the whole world. They've got stripy legs like zebras and a long blue tongue that can lick their own ears clean!
fun_facts.young: Okapis walk by moving both legs on one side at the same time — just like giraffes do.
Their tongue is blue-grey and can be 45 centimetres long.
They have huge ears that can move in different directions to listen for danger.
They eat leaves, fruits, ferns, and even clay from riverbanks to get important minerals.
Male okapis have short horns covered in skin called ossicones.
They make quiet coughing sounds to talk to each other in the thick forest.
fun_facts.tiny: They walk by moving both legs on one side together — just like giraffes do.
Their huge ears can swivel around to listen for danger in every direction.
They make soft coughing sounds to talk to each other through the thick forest.
did_you_know.young: They were completely unknown to scientists until 1901 — people thought they were made-up creatures like unicorns!
An okapi's tongue is so long it can lick its own eyes and ears clean.
Baby okapis don't poop for their first month of life so predators can't smell them.
They have special oil on their fur that makes rainwater slide right off.
Local people called okapis 'African unicorns' because they were so rare and mysterious.
text.size_comparison.young: Already taller than you on all fours — about 4 feet 11 inches at the shoulder. With their long neck, their head is way above yours!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as three or four grown-ups — around 551 pounds.
text.map_narration: Okapis live only in the dense rainforests of the Democratic Republic of Congo in Africa.
text.sound_description.young: They make quiet coughing and bleating sounds to communicate with each other in the forest.

tree_frog.name: Tree Frog
tree_frog.habitat: Forests, rainforests, and trees near water

text.summary.young: Tree frogs are small frogs that live in forests around the world, especially in warm places like South America and Central America. They have special sticky toe pads with millions of tiny cells that work like suction cups, letting them climb up trees and even walk upside down on leaves.
text.summary.tiny: Tree frogs have sticky toe pads that let them climb straight up trees and even walk upside down on leaves. They live in forests all over the world and sing loudly at night.
fun_facts.young: Tree frogs have tiny suction cups on their toes that help them stick to smooth surfaces.
They eat insects like flies, mosquitoes, and moths.
Some tree frogs are bright green, while others are brown or gray.
They lay their eggs in water or on leaves above water.
Male tree frogs puff up their throats like balloons when they sing.
They can live in rainforests, swamps, and even in your backyard.
fun_facts.tiny: They have special sticky toes that work like tiny suction cups.
They can climb up glass windows without falling off.
Male tree frogs puff up their throats like little balloons when they sing.
did_you_know.young: They can climb straight up glass windows without falling.
Some tree frogs can change color to match the leaves around them.
They don't drink water through their mouths — they absorb it through their skin.
A tree frog's sticky toes work even when they're wet.
They sing loudest at night to find friends.
text.size_comparison.young: Small enough to sit on a coin — with sticky toe pads that grip like suction cups!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh less than a single coin — lighter than a paper clip.
text.map_narration: Tree frogs live in tropical forests all around the world, from the Americas to Asia.
text.sound_description.young: They make high-pitched croaking, chirping, and singing sounds, especially at night when they're looking for friends.

text.summary.young: Glass frogs are tiny frogs that live in the rainforests of Central and South America. Their belly skin is completely see-through — you can watch their heart beating and see their bones and organs inside!
text.summary.tiny: Glass frogs have see-through bellies. You can watch their tiny hearts beating inside!
fun_facts.young: Glass frogs are about as long as your thumb.
Their bones look green through their clear skin.
They hunt insects at night in the trees.
You can count all the eggs inside a pregnant female glass frog.
Their sticky toe pads help them climb on wet leaves.
They can live for more than ten years in the wild.
fun_facts.tiny: They're as long as your thumb.
Dad frogs sit on the eggs to keep them safe.
Their sticky toes help them climb on wet leaves.
did_you_know.young: You can see a glass frog's heart pumping blood through its body.
They sleep on the bottom of leaves so predators can't see them from below.
Male glass frogs guard their eggs on leaves until they hatch.
When glass frog tadpoles hatch, they drop into streams below.
They have green backs but clear bellies — the perfect camouflage!
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a paper clip — so small and so see-through you can see their heart beating!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh less than a single coin — almost nothing.
text.map_narration: Glass frogs live in the cloud forests and rainforests of Central and South America.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft chirping and croaking sounds to call to each other at night.

text.summary.young: Panther chameleons are colorful lizards that live in the trees of Madagascar. They change color to show how they're feeling — bright colors mean they're excited or want to impress someone!
text.summary.tiny: Panther chameleons change color like a mood ring! They turn bright red and orange when they're showing off.
fun_facts.young: A panther chameleon's tongue can be twice as long as its whole body!
They grip branches with special feet that work like mittens with two sides.
Panther chameleons turn bright red and orange when they want to show off.
They almost never come down from the trees — they eat, sleep, and live way up high.
When panther chameleons are calm and happy, they turn soft green colors.
Baby panther chameleons are born knowing how to climb and hunt right away!
fun_facts.tiny: Their tongue shoots out twice as long as their whole body.
Each eye can look in a different direction at the same time.
They grip branches with feet that work like mittens.
did_you_know.young: They can move each eye in a different direction at the same time!
Their tongue shoots out faster than you can blink to catch bugs.
Male panther chameleons are much more colorful than females.
They can see things that are tiny and far away at the same time.
Each panther chameleon has its own special pattern of colors.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a ruler — with a curly tail and eyes that look in two directions at once!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as an egg — around 3 ounces.
text.map_narration: Panther chameleons live on the island of Madagascar, off the coast of Africa.
text.sound_description.young: They make a soft hissing sound when they feel scared or want to be left alone.

text.summary.young: Boa constrictors are large snakes that live in the rainforests and grasslands of Central and South America. They squeeze their prey just tight enough to stop blood flow, and can sense a heartbeat to know exactly when to let go.
text.summary.tiny: Boa constrictors are huge snakes that wrap around their dinner like a hug that won't let go. They live in rainforests and can sense a heartbeat through their skin.
fun_facts.young: A boa constrictor can open its mouth wide enough to swallow prey bigger than its own head.
They have tiny leftover leg bones inside their bodies from ancient snake ancestors.
Boa constrictors are excellent swimmers and climbers.
Their teeth curve backward to help them hold onto slippery prey.
They shed their skin several times a year as they grow.
They can live for 30 years in the wild.
fun_facts.tiny: A boa constrictor can open its mouth wide enough to swallow something bigger than its own head.
They've got tiny leg bones hidden inside their bodies from when snakes used to have legs.
They don't crush — they squeeze just tight enough to stop the heart.
did_you_know.young: They don't crush their prey — they squeeze just tight enough to stop the heart.
They can sense a heartbeat through their body to know when to let go.
Baby boas are born live, not hatched from eggs.
They can go weeks or even months without eating after a big meal.
They have heat-sensing pits on their faces to find warm-blooded prey in the dark.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a small car — around 10 feet from head to tail.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a big bag of dog food — around 60 pounds.
text.map_narration: Boa constrictors live in the forests and grasslands of Central and South America.
text.sound_description.young: They make a loud hissing sound when they feel threatened or want to be left alone.

text.summary.young: Cows are large farm animals found all over the world. They have best friends and feel happier when they spend time with their favourite cow companions.
text.summary.tiny: Cows are gentle giants who live on farms and make milk for us to drink. They're as tall as your front door and have best friends they love to spend time with.
fun_facts.young: Cows can remember faces for years — both human and cow faces.
A cow stands up and sits down about 14 times every day.
They can sleep standing up but prefer to lie down for deep sleep.
Baby cows are called calves and can stand up within an hour of being born.
They make different sounds to talk to each other — they have special moos for their calves.
A cow's tongue is so long it can lick its own nose.
fun_facts.tiny: A cow's tongue is so long it can lick its own nose.
They remember faces for years — your face and other cow faces too.
Baby cows can stand up within an hour of being born.
did_you_know.young: They have best friends and get sad when separated from them.
A cow's stomach has four parts to help digest grass.
They can see almost all the way around without turning their heads.
They spend up to 8 hours a day chewing their cud.
A cow can drink a bathtub full of water every day.
text.size_comparison.young: Standing beside one, they're already taller than you at the shoulder — about 4 feet 7 inches.
text.weight_comparison.young: About 1300 pounds — as heavy as a horse!
text.map_narration: Cows were first kept by farmers in the Middle East about ten thousand years ago.
text.sound_description.young: They make a deep mooing sound to talk to their herd and call their calves.

text.summary.young: Horses are large, strong animals that live all over the world and have worked alongside humans for thousands of years. They can sleep standing up by locking their knees, but they still need to lie down for deep sleep.
text.summary.tiny: Horses are strong animals with soft noses and long manes that flow when they run. They can sleep standing up without falling over.
fun_facts.young: Horses sleep standing up by locking their knees so they don't fall over.
They use their ears, eyes, and nostrils to show how they're feeling.
A baby horse can stand up and walk just one hour after being born.
They love to roll in the dirt to scratch their backs and stay cool.
They have excellent memories and can recognize people they haven't seen in years.
Wild horses live in groups called herds and take turns watching for danger.
fun_facts.tiny: A baby horse can stand up and walk just one hour after it's born.
They remember people they haven't seen in years.
They roll in the dirt to scratch their backs and cool down.
did_you_know.young: They can run within hours of being born.
A horse's teeth never stop growing throughout its entire life.
They have the biggest eyes of any land mammal.
They can remember people and places for many years.
A horse's hoof is like a giant toenail — it's made of the same stuff as your fingernails.
text.size_comparison.young: Way taller than you — their back is at a grown-up's chest, around 5 feet 2 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a horse — around 1,100 pounds. Well, they ARE a horse!
text.map_narration: Horses were first tamed on the grasslands of Central Asia about six thousand years ago.
text.sound_description.young: They neigh and whinny to call to each other, and snort when they're excited or nervous.

text.summary.young: Sheep are fluffy farm animals that live all around the world. They can remember the faces of 50 other sheep for more than 2 years!
text.summary.tiny: Sheep are fluffy friends with wool that never stops growing. They remember faces better than you might think!
fun_facts.young: Sheep don't have top front teeth — they use their bottom teeth and a hard pad on top to tear grass.
One sheep can produce enough wool each year to make 4 or 5 sweaters.
They like to stay close together in groups called flocks — it makes them feel safe.
They have best friends! They spend most of their time with their favorite sheep.
Lambs can recognize their mother's call out of hundreds of other sheep voices.
They are very good at solving puzzles and can learn their names just like dogs.
fun_facts.tiny: They have best friends and spend most of their time together.
A lamb can recognize its mum's voice out of hundreds of other sheep.
One sheep makes enough wool each year for four cosy jumpers.
did_you_know.young: They have rectangular pupils that let them see almost all the way around without turning their heads.
A sheep's wool never stops growing — they need haircuts every year!
They recognize their friends' faces and get sad when their friends are taken away.
Baby sheep are called lambs, and they can walk just minutes after being born.
They have excellent memories and can remember paths and places for years.
text.size_comparison.young: On all fours, they reach your chest — around 2 feet 6 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a grown-up — around 154 pounds.
text.map_narration: Sheep were first kept by farmers in the Middle East and are now found all over the world.
text.sound_description.young: They say 'baa' or 'bleat' to talk to each other and call their lambs.

text.summary.young: Goats are playful farm animals found all over the world. They have rectangular pupils that let them see almost all the way around without turning their heads!
text.summary.tiny: Goats can see almost all the way around without turning their heads! Their eyes have special rectangle-shaped pupils that work like magic windows.
fun_facts.young: Baby goats are called kids, and they love to jump and play together.
Goats can jump over 5 feet high from a standing position.
Each goat has a unique voice, and mothers can recognize their babies by their bleats.
They have four stomachs to help them digest tough plants and grass.
They are excellent swimmers and love to explore new places.
A group of goats is called a herd or a tribe.
fun_facts.tiny: Baby goats are called kids, and they can jump and play just hours after they're born.
They are fantastic climbers and can balance on cliffs steeper than your stairs.
Every goat has its own special voice, and mums know their baby's bleat straight away.
did_you_know.young: They have rectangular pupils that give them a 320-degree view — they can see almost everything around them without moving their head!
They were one of the first animals ever domesticated by humans, over 10,000 years ago.
They are incredible climbers and can scale steep cliffs and even trees to find food.
A goat's pupils are shaped like rectangles instead of circles like ours.
They are very picky eaters and will taste everything before they eat it.
text.size_comparison.young: Standing beside you, they reach your shoulders — around 2 feet 7 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a grown-up — around 121 pounds.
text.map_narration: Goats were first kept in the mountains of western Asia about ten thousand years ago.
text.sound_description.young: They make a bleating sound that sounds like 'maa' or 'baa' — they bleat to talk to each other and call their babies.

text.summary.young: Pigs are smart farm animals found all over the world. They are smarter than dogs and can even learn to play video games with joysticks!
text.summary.tiny: Pigs are clever animals who live on farms everywhere. They're smarter than dogs and can learn to play video games!
fun_facts.young: Pigs are cleaner than you think — they never go to the bathroom where they sleep or eat.
A group of pigs is called a drift or a drove.
They love to play and will run around and play with toys.
Baby pigs are called piglets and they weigh only about 3 pounds when born.
They can learn tricks just like dogs — they can sit, spin, and fetch!
They have excellent memories and can remember things for years.
fun_facts.tiny: They never go to the bathroom where they sleep or eat.
Baby pigs weigh about as much as a bag of sugar when they're born.
They remember things for years and years.
did_you_know.young: They don't sweat — they roll in mud to cool down!
A pig's snout is super strong and can dig up roots and truffles underground.
They can recognize their own names and come when called.
Mother pigs sing to their babies while nursing them.
They have an amazing sense of smell — even better than dogs!
text.size_comparison.young: On all fours, they reach your shoulders — around 2 feet 7 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a grown-up — around 176 pounds.
text.map_narration: Pigs were first kept as farm animals in China and the Middle East thousands of years ago.
text.sound_description.young: They oink and grunt to talk to each other and squeal when they're excited or scared.

text.summary.young: Chickens are farm birds that live all around the world. They are the closest living relatives to Tyrannosaurus rex — scientists found this out by studying dinosaur bones!
text.summary.tiny: Chickens are farm birds that live all around the world. They're the closest living relatives to Tyrannosaurus rex!
fun_facts.young: Chickens can run up to 9 miles per hour — that's faster than most people can walk!
Baby chicks can do maths — they understand that 1 + 1 = 2 when they're just days old.
They have their own language with over 30 different sounds for different messages.
A hen can lay more than 300 eggs in one year.
They dream when they sleep, just like people do.
The red flap of skin under a chicken's beak is called a wattle — it helps them stay cool.
fun_facts.tiny: They can run faster than most people can walk.
Baby chicks can do maths when they're just days old.
A hen can lay more than 300 eggs in one year.
did_you_know.young: They can remember over 100 different faces — including people and other chickens.
A mother hen talks to her chicks while they're still inside their eggs, and they chirp back!
They have better colour vision than humans — they can even see colours we can't see.
There are more chickens on Earth than any other bird — over 25 billion!
They take dust baths to clean their feathers and get rid of bugs.
text.size_comparison.young: Only about as tall as a football standing up — around 1 foot 4 inches.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bag of sugar — around 6 pounds.
text.map_narration: Chickens were first kept in Southeast Asia and are now the most common bird on Earth.
text.sound_description.young: They cluck softly to talk to each other and squawk loudly when they're excited or scared.

text.summary.young: Ducks are waterbirds with webbed feet that live near ponds, lakes, and rivers all over the world. Their feathers are completely waterproof because they spread special oil all over them to keep dry.
text.summary.tiny: Ducks are birds with feet like paddles that live on ponds and rivers. They spread special oil on their feathers so water slides right off.
fun_facts.young: Ducks have webbed feet that work like paddles to push them through water.
A group of ducks swimming together is called a raft.
They don't get cold feet in icy water because their feet have no nerves or blood vessels.
Male ducks are called drakes and have brighter, more colorful feathers than females.
They eat plants, insects, small fish, and seeds.
When ducks dive underwater, they can hold their breath for about a minute.
fun_facts.tiny: They have webbed feet that work like paddles to push them through water.
Baby ducks can swim and find food just hours after they hatch.
They sleep with one eye open to watch for danger.
did_you_know.young: They have three eyelids — one see-through eyelid lets them see underwater while keeping their eyes safe.
A duck's quack doesn't echo, and scientists still aren't sure why.
Baby ducks can swim and find their own food just hours after hatching.
They sleep with one eye open to watch for danger while they rest.
Some ducks can fly over 300 miles in a single day during migration.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a school ruler — they waddle along close to the ground.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a carton of milk — around 3 pounds.
text.map_narration: Ducks live near ponds, lakes, and rivers all over the world.
text.sound_description.young: They make a loud quacking sound, and some ducks also chirp or whistle softly.

text.summary.young: Turkeys are large birds originally from North America that now live on farms all over the world. Wild turkeys can fly up to 88 km/h, but farm turkeys have been bred so big and heavy that most can't fly at all!
text.summary.tiny: Turkeys are big birds with wobbly red skin hanging from their necks. Wild turkeys can zoom through the sky, but farm turkeys are too heavy to fly!
fun_facts.young: The wobbly red skin that hangs from a turkey's neck is called a wattle.
Turkeys have around 5,000 feathers covering their bodies.
Baby turkeys are called poults and can leave the nest within 24 hours of hatching.
They have three stomachs to help them digest all the seeds, insects, and plants they eat.
Wild turkeys roost in trees but spend most of their day walking around looking for food.
Benjamin Franklin wanted the turkey to be America's national bird instead of the bald eagle!
fun_facts.tiny: They have about five thousand feathers all over their bodies.
Baby turkeys can walk around just one day after they hatch.
Boy turkeys fan out their tail feathers like a beautiful rainbow when they want to show off.
did_you_know.young: Wild turkeys can run as fast as 40 km/h on the ground — faster than most people can sprint!
They have excellent eyesight and can see in colour, which helps them spot danger from far away.
A group of turkeys is called a rafter or a flock.
Male turkeys are called toms and have colourful feathers that fan out like a rainbow when they want to show off.
They sleep in trees at night to stay safe from predators like foxes and coyotes.
text.size_comparison.young: About as tall as your belly — around 3 feet tall, with a big fan-shaped tail.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a house cat — around 22 pounds.
text.map_narration: Turkeys originally come from North America and were first kept by the Aztec people in Mexico.
text.sound_description.young: They gobble loudly, cluck softly to each other, and make gentle purring sounds when they're happy.

text.summary.young: Donkeys are strong, patient animals related to horses that live on farms around the world. They have incredible memories and can remember other donkeys and places for over 25 years.
text.summary.tiny: Donkeys are strong, gentle animals with big soft ears and fluffy coats. They can remember friends and places for their whole lives — even longer than you've been alive!
fun_facts.young: A baby donkey is called a foal.
Donkeys love rolling in dust to keep their skin clean and cool.
Their hooves are small and tough — perfect for rocky mountain paths.
They talk to each other with loud brays that sound like 'hee-haw'.
They can live for 40 years — longer than most horses.
They are very smart and can learn their names and tricks.
fun_facts.tiny: They roll in the dust to keep their skin clean and cool.
Their big ears can hear other donkeys calling from very far away.
A baby donkey is called a foal.
did_you_know.young: They can carry heavy loads — up to 20% of their body weight all day long.
Their big ears help them hear other donkeys calling from far away — up to 3 kilometres.
They are very careful walkers and won't step somewhere dangerous, which is why people think they're stubborn.
They can live in very hot deserts because their bodies are good at saving water.
They protect sheep and goats from predators like coyotes and foxes.
text.size_comparison.young: At the shoulder, they're already taller than you at the shoulder — about 3 feet 7 inches.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as three or four grown-ups — around 397 pounds.
text.map_narration: Donkeys were first tamed in Africa about five thousand years ago.
text.sound_description.young: They make a loud 'hee-haw' bray that can be heard from far away.

text.summary.young: Llamas are fluffy animals from the mountains of South America. They spit green goo when they're angry or annoyed!
text.summary.tiny: Llamas are fluffy animals from the mountains of South America. They spit green goo when they're angry!
fun_facts.young: Llamas have soft, padded feet that don't damage the ground like horse hooves do.
A llama's woolly coat keeps them warm in freezing mountain weather.
They are cousins of camels but they don't have humps!
They are excellent guards and will protect sheep and chickens from foxes and coyotes.
Each llama has its own personality — some are bossy and some are shy.
They love taking dust baths to keep their coats clean and fluffy.
fun_facts.tiny: They hum to talk to each other.
They can carry heavy loads up steep mountains without getting tired.
Baby llamas can walk just half an hour after they're born!
did_you_know.young: They hum to talk to each other — they make soft humming sounds when they're happy or curious.
A llama's spit is actually green because it comes from their stomach!
They can carry heavy packs up steep mountains without getting tired.
Baby llamas are called crias and can walk just 30 minutes after being born.
They have three stomach chambers to help them digest tough grass.
text.size_comparison.young: At the shoulder, they're already taller than you at the shoulder — about 3 feet 9 inches. With their long neck, their head is way above yours!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as two grown-ups — around 331 pounds.
text.map_narration: Llamas come from the high mountains of South America, especially Peru and Bolivia.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft humming sounds to talk, and loud alarm calls when they sense danger.

alpaca.name: Alpaca
alpaca.habitat: Mountain grasslands in South America and farms worldwide

text.summary.young: Alpacas are fluffy animals from the Andes mountains in South America that are raised for their soft wool. Their wool is warmer than sheep wool and doesn't make people itchy, so it's perfect for cozy sweaters and blankets.
text.summary.tiny: Alpacas are fluffy friends from high mountains who hum like they're singing a gentle song. Their wool is so soft and warm it makes the cosiest jumpers.
fun_facts.young: Alpacas are cousins of camels, but they don't have humps.
A group of alpacas is called a herd.
They can live high in the mountains where the air is very thin.
Baby alpacas are called crias and can walk just one hour after being born.
They come in 22 different colors, from white to black to brown.
They have big eyes on the sides of their heads so they can see danger coming from almost every direction.
fun_facts.tiny: Baby alpacas can walk just one hour after they're born.
They have big eyes on the sides of their heads so they can see almost everything around them.
They always use the same spot as their toilet — they're very tidy.
did_you_know.young: They hum to talk to each other — mothers hum to their babies and babies hum back!
They have soft padded feet instead of hooves, so they don't hurt the ground when they walk.
When alpacas are annoyed, they spit at each other — but they rarely spit at people!
They always go to the bathroom in the same spot, making them very tidy animals.
An alpaca's wool keeps growing, so they need haircuts once a year to stay cool.
text.size_comparison.young: At the shoulder, they reach right up past your chin — around 2 feet 11 inches at the shoulder. With their long neck, their head reaches above yours!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a grown-up — around 143 pounds.
text.map_narration: Alpacas come from the high Andes Mountains of Peru, Bolivia, and Chile.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft humming sounds to talk to each other, and sometimes snort or cluck when they're curious or alert.

text.summary.young: Geese are large water birds found on farms and lakes around the world. They are such good guards that ancient Roman soldiers used them as alarm systems to warn of enemy attacks.
text.summary.tiny: Geese are big birds with honking voices that guard farms like feathery watchdogs. They fly in giant V shapes across the sky and swim with feet like flippers.
fun_facts.young: Geese honk loudly at strangers, making them natural guard animals
A group of geese on water is called a gaggle, but in the air it's called a skein
Geese eat grass all day long like tiny lawnmowers
When geese fly together, they take turns being the leader in front
Geese can fly over 3,000 miles during migration without stopping to rest
Mother geese teach their babies to fly by running and flapping alongside them
fun_facts.tiny: Geese mate for life and stay with the same partner forever.
A baby goose can swim the day after it hatches.
When geese fly together, they take turns being the leader at the front.
did_you_know.young: Geese fly in a V-shape to save energy — each bird drafts behind the one in front
A goose can live for 25 years, longer than most dogs
Geese mate for life and stay with the same partner forever
Baby geese can swim just one day after they hatch
Geese have tiny teeth on their tongues and beaks to grip grass
text.size_comparison.young: About as tall as your belly when they stretch their long neck up — around 2 feet 7 inches.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a couple bags of sugar — around 11 pounds.
text.map_narration: Geese live near lakes, ponds, and fields across Europe, Asia, and North America.
text.sound_description.young: Geese make loud honking sounds to talk to each other and warn away strangers.

text.summary.young: Water buffaloes are large, powerful animals that live in Asia, Europe, and Australia. They love wallowing in mud and water to stay cool and protect their skin from biting insects.
text.summary.tiny: Water buffaloes love being wet! They spend hours soaking in rivers and rolling in cool, squishy mud.
fun_facts.young: Water buffaloes spend up to half their day soaking in water or rolling in mud.
Their thick, grey skin is almost hairless, which is why they need mud to protect them from sunburn and bugs.
They are excellent swimmers and love diving underwater to eat water plants.
Baby water buffaloes are called calves and can walk within minutes of being born.
They live in herds and look after each other — the whole group helps protect the calves.
Despite their size, water buffaloes are gentle and form close bonds with the farmers who care for them.
fun_facts.tiny: Their huge, curved horns can be as wide as your mum lying down with her arms stretched out.
Baby water buffaloes can walk just minutes after they're born.
They're brilliant swimmers and dive underwater to nibble plants from the riverbed.
did_you_know.young: They can hold their breath underwater for several minutes while they graze on plants at the bottom of rivers and ponds.
Their wide, splayed hooves work like snowshoes in mud — they don't sink as easily as other animals.
They milk is richer and creamier than cow's milk and is used to make mozzarella cheese.
A water buffalo's curved horns can grow up to 2 metres long from tip to tip — that's taller than most adults.
They have been helping farmers plough rice fields for thousands of years because they're so strong and calm.
text.size_comparison.young: On all fours, they're already taller than you at the shoulder — about 4 feet 11 inches.
text.weight_comparison.young: About 2000 pounds — as heavy as a horse!
text.map_narration: Water buffalo were first kept by farmers in southern Asia and are still working on farms today.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep bellowing sounds and snorts to communicate with their herd.

yak.name: Yak
yak.habitat: High mountain plateaus and valleys in Tibet and Central Asia

text.summary.young: Yaks are large, shaggy cattle that live high in the mountains of Tibet and Central Asia. Their blood has three times more red blood cells than regular cows, so they can breathe easily where the air is very thin.
text.summary.tiny: Yaks are big, shaggy cows that live high up in the mountains where the air is thin. They've got special blood that helps them breathe where you'd feel dizzy!
fun_facts.young: Yaks have almost no sweat glands, so they stay cool by panting like a dog.
A yak's tail is so bushy it's used as a flyswatter in some countries!
They can carry heavy loads up steep mountain trails without slipping.
Their thick coat has two layers — a woolly undercoat and long guard hairs that almost touch the ground.
They grunt instead of moo — that's why their scientific name means 'grunting ox'!
Baby yaks are born with a soft, curly coat that gets longer and shaggier as they grow.
fun_facts.tiny: A yak's coat is so long it nearly sweeps the ground.
They grunt instead of moo — that's how they got their name!
Their bushy tails make brilliant flyswatters.
did_you_know.young: They can survive higher than almost any other large mammal — even above where most birds fly!
A yak's heart and lungs are much bigger than a cow's to help them breathe in thin mountain air.
They don't sweat — their thick coat keeps them so warm they can freeze if they get too hot!
People in Tibet use yak milk, wool, and even yak poop for fuel to keep warm.
Wild yaks can weigh twice as much as farm yaks — up to 1,000 kilograms!
text.size_comparison.young: Taller than any grown-up at the shoulder — a shaggy wall of muscle, around 5 feet 7 inches.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a horse — around 1,300 pounds.
text.map_narration: Yaks live in the high mountains of Central Asia, especially Tibet and Nepal.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep grunting and snorting sounds instead of mooing like cows.

highland_cow.name: Highland Cow
highland_cow.habitat: Cold mountains and grassy hills in Scotland

text.summary.young: Highland Cows are shaggy cattle from the cold mountains of Scotland. Their long fringe, called a 'dossan', keeps flies out of their eyes like a natural curtain.
text.summary.tiny: Highland Cows have the shaggiest coats of any cow — like they're wearing a fuzzy blanket all the time. Their long fringe keeps flies away from their eyes.
fun_facts.young: A Highland Cow's fringe is so long it covers their whole face.
They eat grass, leaves, and flowers — munching for up to eight hours a day.
Highland Cows are very calm and gentle, even though they look wild and woolly.
Their thick coat means they don't need barns — they sleep outside in all weather.
Baby Highland Cows are called calves and are born with fluffy coats.
They have been living in Scotland for over 1,000 years.
fun_facts.tiny: They munch grass for hours and hours — sometimes all morning long.
They sleep outside in rain and snow because their coat keeps them cosy.
Baby Highland Cows are born with fluffy coats that make them look like teddy bears.
did_you_know.young: They have two layers of hair — a soft woolly undercoat and a long outer coat that keeps rain off like a raincoat.
Their horns can grow over three feet long and curve outward like handlebars.
They can survive in snow and wind because their thick coat is like wearing a winter jacket all year.
They use their horns to dig through snow to find grass underneath.
They come in many colors including red, black, yellow, and even white.
text.size_comparison.young: Already taller than you at the shoulder — about 3 feet 11 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as five or six grown-ups — around 1100 pounds.
text.map_narration: Highland cows come from the Scottish Highlands, where their shaggy coats keep them warm.
text.sound_description.young: They say 'moo' in a deep, rumbling voice that echoes across the hills.

text.summary.young: Mules are special animals created when a horse and a donkey have a baby together. They are stronger than horses and better at climbing rocky mountains without slipping.
text.summary.tiny: Mules are special animals with a horse mum and a donkey dad. They're brilliant at carrying heavy things up mountains without slipping.
fun_facts.young: Mules are famous for being stubborn, but they're actually just very smart and careful.
A mule's mother is always a horse and its father is always a donkey.
They helped build roads through mountains by carrying tools and supplies.
Some mules can carry loads that weigh as much as a full-grown lion!
They eat grass, hay, and grain just like horses do.
They have been helping farmers and travelers for over 3,000 years.
fun_facts.tiny: They can carry loads as heavy as a lion.
They've been helping people for over three thousand years.
Some mules live to be fifty years old.
did_you_know.young: They can carry heavy loads up steep mountains where horses would slip and fall.
A mule's ears are longer than a horse's ears but shorter than a donkey's ears.
They almost never have babies of their own, even though they are healthy and strong.
They can live longer than horses — some mules live to be 50 years old!
They have harder hooves than horses, so they don't need horseshoes as often.
text.size_comparison.young: On all fours, they're already taller than you at the shoulder — about 4 feet 7 inches.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as five or six grown-ups — around 772 pounds.
text.map_narration: Mules have been helping people carry heavy loads for thousands of years, all over the world.
text.sound_description.young: They make a sound called a bray that starts like a horse's neigh but ends like a donkey's hee-haw.

text.summary.young: Oxen are strong cattle trained to pull heavy loads and plough fields. They helped build the pyramids and the Great Wall of China — they were the tractors of the ancient world for over 6,000 years.
text.summary.tiny: Oxen are strong cattle who've been helping people farm and build for thousands of years. They pulled the stones to build the pyramids — like tractors with hooves.
fun_facts.young: Oxen usually work in pairs wearing a wooden yoke across their shoulders.
An ox can pull a plough through hard soil all day without getting tired.
They are calm and patient — they listen carefully to their farmer's commands.
Baby oxen learn to work by watching older oxen and copying what they do.
They have been helping humans farm and build for over 6,000 years.
They are vegetarians and eat grass, hay, and grain to stay strong.
fun_facts.tiny: Two oxen working together can pull loads heavier than a car.
They're so calm and patient they'll plough fields all day without complaining.
Baby oxen learn their job by copying what older oxen do.
did_you_know.young: They helped build the pyramids in Egypt thousands of years ago.
Two oxen working together can pull twice as much as one ox alone.
They are just regular cattle that have been trained to work with people.
Farmers used oxen to plough fields long before tractors were invented.
They are so strong they can pull loads that weigh more than a car.
text.size_comparison.young: At about 4 feet 7 inches at the shoulder, they're taller than you!
text.weight_comparison.young: About 1550 pounds — as heavy as a horse!
text.map_narration: Oxen have been working alongside farmers for thousands of years, pulling ploughs and heavy carts.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep mooing sounds and low bellows to communicate with each other and their farmers.

barn_owl.name: Barn Owl
barn_owl.habitat: Barns, old buildings, and open grasslands worldwide

text.summary.young: Barn owls are pale, heart-faced hunters found on every continent except Antarctica. They can catch mice in complete darkness using only their ears — their face acts like a dish that collects even the tiniest sounds.
text.summary.tiny: Barn owls have pale heart-shaped faces and hunt in complete darkness. They can hear a mouse moving under snow and catch it without making a sound.
fun_facts.young: Barn owls don't hoot — they make a scary screeching sound instead
They can turn their head almost all the way around to look behind them
Baby barn owls are covered in fluffy white down that makes them look like cotton balls
They mate for life and often return to the same nest year after year
Their eyes are so big they can't move them — that's why they turn their whole head
One ear is slightly higher than the other to help them pinpoint sounds perfectly
fun_facts.tiny: They don't hoot — they screech and hiss instead.
Their heart-shaped face works like a dish that catches tiny sounds.
They swallow mice whole and cough up the bones later in a fuzzy pellet.
did_you_know.young: A barn owl can hear a mouse moving under snow from far away
Their feathers are specially shaped to make no sound when they fly
They swallow mice whole and cough up the bones later in a pellet
One barn owl can eat over 1,000 mice in a single year
Their heart-shaped face works like a radar dish to collect sounds
text.size_comparison.young: Only about as tall as a school ruler — with a heart-shaped white face.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a loaf of bread — around 1 pound.
text.map_narration: Barn owls live on every continent except Antarctica — often in old barns and church towers.
text.sound_description.young: They make a harsh screeching or hissing sound, not a hoot like other owls.

bald_eagle.name: Bald Eagle
bald_eagle.habitat: Near rivers, lakes, and coasts in North America

text.summary.young: Bald eagles are large birds of prey that live near rivers and lakes in North America. They aren't actually bald — their white head feathers don't grow in until they're five years old.
text.summary.tiny: Bald eagles aren't bald at all — they've got bright white feathers on their heads. They live near water and catch fish with their super-strong feet.
fun_facts.young: A bald eagle's grip is ten times stronger than a human's hand.
They don't get their white head feathers until they're five years old.
Bald eagles can swim using their wings like paddles if they land in water.
Their sharp talons lock in place when they grab fish — so they don't let go.
They build the biggest nests of any bird in North America.
They steal fish from other birds by chasing them until they drop their catch.
fun_facts.tiny: They can see fish swimming from way up in the clouds.
Their nests can be as heavy as a small car.
Baby eagles are covered in fluffy grey feathers, not white ones.
did_you_know.young: They can see fish swimming underwater from high up in the sky.
Their nests can weigh as much as a car — up to 2,000 pounds!
They mate for life and return to the same nest every year.
They can fly as fast as 100 miles per hour when diving to catch fish.
Baby bald eagles are covered in gray fluffy feathers, not white ones.
text.size_comparison.young: With wings spread wide, they are wider than a grown-up is tall — about 7 feet across!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a couple bags of sugar — around 13 pounds.
text.map_narration: Bald eagles live near lakes, rivers, and coasts across North America.
text.sound_description.young: They make high-pitched screeching and chirping calls that sound like squeaky whistles.

peregrine_falcon.name: Peregrine Falcon
peregrine_falcon.habitat: Mountains, cliffs, cities, and coastlines worldwide

text.summary.young: Peregrine falcons are powerful hunting birds found on every continent except Antarctica. They are the fastest animals on Earth, diving through the sky at over 320 kilometres per hour to catch other birds in mid-air.
text.summary.tiny: Peregrine falcons are the fastest animals in the whole world. They dive through the sky faster than a racing car to catch birds.
fun_facts.young: Peregrine means 'wanderer' because these falcons travel long distances.
They have special bones in their nose that slow down air so they can breathe during fast dives.
Peregrine falcons were used by kings and queens for hunting over 3000 years ago.
Their eyes have two centres of focus so they can see clearly while diving at high speed.
Baby peregrine falcons are covered in fluffy white feathers.
They can live in deserts, mountains, forests, and cities.
fun_facts.tiny: They can spot a flying bird from further away than you can see to the end of your street.
Baby peregrines are covered in fluffy white feathers like little clouds.
They live everywhere — mountains, deserts, forests, and even on tall city buildings.
did_you_know.young: They can spot a pigeon from over 3 kilometres away.
Their dive is called a 'stoop' and they tuck their wings into a teardrop shape to go faster.
They strike prey with their feet so hard it can knock birds unconscious instantly.
They often nest on tall city buildings and bridges.
A peregrine falcon's heart beats 600 times per minute during a dive.
text.size_comparison.young: Only about as long as a ruler — but the fastest animal on Earth when they dive!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a carton of milk — around 2 pounds.
text.map_narration: Peregrine falcons live on every continent except Antarctica — even in big cities!
text.sound_description.young: They make loud screeching calls, especially near their nests.

text.summary.young: Great horned owls are large hunting birds with feather tufts on their heads that live across North and South America. They can turn their heads almost all the way around — 270 degrees — because they have twice as many neck bones as humans.
text.summary.tiny: Great horned owls have feathery tufts on their heads that look like pointy ears. They can spin their heads almost all the way around to look behind them.
fun_facts.young: The 'horns' on their heads are actually just feathers called ear tufts
They can hear a mouse moving under snow from far away
Great horned owls swallow small animals whole, then spit out balls of fur and bones later
Their feathers are so soft they fly silently through the air
They don't build their own nests — they take over nests from hawks and eagles
They mate for life and stay together year after year
fun_facts.tiny: Their feathers are so soft they fly without making any sound at all.
They swallow mice whole, then cough up little balls of fur and bones.
They steal nests from other birds instead of building their own.
did_you_know.young: They have 14 bones in their neck, while humans only have 7
They can turn their heads almost all the way around to look behind them
Their big yellow eyes stay completely still in their heads — they can't move their eyes at all
They hunt at night and can see prey in almost total darkness
They are strong enough to catch skunks and porcupines
text.size_comparison.young: About as tall as a school ruler and a half — around 22 inches, with big ear tufts on top.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a carton of milk — around 3 pounds.
text.map_narration: Great horned owls live across North and South America, from forests to deserts.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep hooting calls that sound like 'hoo-hoo-hoo, hoo-hoo' echoing through the night.

snowy_owl.name: Snowy Owl
snowy_owl.habitat: Arctic tundra and open snowy fields

text.summary.young: Snowy owls are large white owls that live in the cold Arctic, where snow covers the ground most of the year. Unlike most owls that hunt at night, snowy owls hunt during the day because the Arctic summer has sunlight all day and night.
text.summary.tiny: Snowy owls are big white owls with feathers so thick they cover their toes. They hunt in bright daylight across snowy land where the sun never sets in summer.
fun_facts.young: A snowy owl can eat more than 1,600 lemmings in one year.
Their feet are covered in thick feathers to keep them warm in freezing temperatures.
Snowy owls can turn their heads almost all the way around to look behind them.
They fly silently through the air so their prey never hears them coming.
In winter, some snowy owls fly south and can be spotted near beaches and open fields.
Baby snowy owls are covered in fluffy gray down when they hatch.
fun_facts.tiny: A snowy owl can hear a tiny mouse moving under the snow.
Their fluffy feathers are so soft they fly without making any sound at all.
Girl snowy owls have dark spots but boy snowy owls are white as fresh snow.
did_you_know.young: They are the heaviest owls in North America.
Their white feathers help them blend into the snowy Arctic landscape.
Male snowy owls are almost pure white, while females have dark spots and bars.
They can see and hear a mouse moving under the snow from far away.
They don't build nests — they lay their eggs right on the ground.
text.size_comparison.young: About as tall as two rulers stacked up — around 2 feet, with snowy white feathers.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bag of sugar — around 6 pounds.
text.map_narration: Snowy owls live in the Arctic tundra of Canada, Alaska, and northern Europe.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep hooting sounds and loud barking calls that echo across the snowy Arctic.

flamingo.name: Flamingo
flamingo.habitat: Shallow lakes and lagoons in warm places

text.summary.young: Flamingos are tall pink birds with long legs and curved beaks that live near shallow lakes in warm places around the world. They are born grey and white, but turn pink from eating tiny shrimp and algae that have special pink colours inside them.
text.summary.tiny: Flamingos are tall pink birds with bendy necks and legs like stilts. They're born grey but turn pink from eating tiny pink shrimps.
fun_facts.young: Flamingos eat with their heads upside down, filtering tiny food from the water with their special beaks.
Their curved beak works like a strainer to catch shrimp and algae.
They make a honking sound when they talk to each other.
They can live in water so salty that most other animals cannot survive there.
They parents make pink milk in their throat to feed their chicks.
Zoo flamingos need to eat special food with the same pink colours or they turn white.
fun_facts.tiny: They eat with their heads upside down in the water.
They stand on one leg to keep the other one warm.
Baby flamingos have straight beaks that slowly curve as they grow.
did_you_know.young: They sleep standing on one leg to keep the other leg warm and save energy.
A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
They can drink boiling hot water from geysers and volcanic lakes.
Baby flamingos are called chicks and they have straight beaks that curve as they grow.
They can fly up to 60 kilometres per hour.
text.size_comparison.young: Standing tall on those skinny legs, they are taller than you — around 4 feet 3 inches!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bag of sugar — around 7 pounds. Those long legs are mostly bone!
text.map_narration: Flamingos live near salty lakes and lagoons in Africa, southern Europe, and the Americas.
text.sound_description.young: They make loud honking and grunting sounds that sound like geese.

peacock.name: Peacock
peacock.habitat: Forests, grasslands, and parks in Asia and around the world

text.summary.young: Peacocks are large, colorful birds originally from Asia that now live in many parts of the world. Their famous tail feathers don't actually contain blue pigment — the shimmering colors come from tiny crystal structures that reflect light like a prism.
text.summary.tiny: Peacocks are birds with tails that shimmer like rainbows. The amazing colours come from tiny crystals in their feathers that bounce light around.
fun_facts.young: When a peacock spreads his tail to show off, it's called a train display.
Peacocks eat insects, seeds, small snakes, and even flowers.
A group of peacocks is called a party — what a perfect name!
They sleep in trees at night to stay safe from predators.
Baby peacocks are called peachicks and can run around just hours after hatching.
They have been kept by humans for over 3,000 years because people love their beauty.
fun_facts.tiny: Only boy peacocks have the big colourful tails — girls are called peahens and they're brown.
A peacock's tail can spread as wide as a grown-up is tall.
Baby peacocks are called peachicks and they can run around just hours after hatching.
did_you_know.young: A peacock's tail can have over 200 feathers and can spread as wide as a grown-up is tall.
Only male peacocks have the big colorful tails — females are called peahens and have brown feathers.
They shake their tail feathers to make a rattling sound that females can feel through the ground.
The eye spots on a peacock's tail feathers are called ocelli, which means 'little eyes'.
They can fly, but they prefer to spend most of their time walking on the ground.
text.size_comparison.young: Their body is about as long as your arm — but with their tail feathers spread out, they are wider than a grown-up's armspan!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a couple bags of sugar — around 11 pounds.
text.map_narration: Peacocks come from the forests of India and Sri Lanka.
text.sound_description.young: They make loud, high-pitched screaming calls that sound like a person shouting 'help!' and they rattle their tail feathers when they dance.

text.summary.young: Emperor penguins are the tallest penguins in the world and live in Antarctica, the coldest place on Earth. Male emperors balance their eggs on their feet for over 100 days in freezing winter without eating anything at all.
text.summary.tiny: Emperor penguins are the tallest penguins and live in Antarctica, the coldest place on Earth. Dads balance their eggs on their feet all winter without eating anything.
fun_facts.young: Emperor penguins toboggan on their bellies across the ice to move faster.
Their black and white coloring helps them hide from predators — white belly from below, black back from above.
Baby emperors can't swim until they lose their fluffy baby feathers and grow waterproof adult feathers.
They have special feathers that trap air to keep them warm in water colder than your freezer.
They can't fly in the air, but they 'fly' underwater using their flippers like wings.
Dad penguins lose almost half their body weight while keeping the egg warm without eating.
fun_facts.tiny: They slide on their bellies across the ice to go faster.
Baby emperors wear fluffy grey feathers like fuzzy pyjamas.
They can't fly in the air, but they fly underwater using their flippers like wings.
did_you_know.young: Dad penguins keep the egg warm on their feet while mom swims far away to catch fish.
They can dive deeper than any other bird — as deep as a 40-story building is tall!
Thousands of penguins huddle together in winter to stay warm, taking turns in the middle where it's warmest.
They chicks have fluffy gray feathers that look like fuzzy pajamas.
They can hold their breath underwater for over 20 minutes while hunting for fish.
text.size_comparison.young: The tallest penguin — they stand almost as tall as you, around 3 feet 11 inches!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a big bag of dog food — around 66 pounds.
text.map_narration: Emperor penguins live only in Antarctica — the coldest place on Earth.
text.sound_description.young: They make loud trumpet calls to find their family in big, noisy crowds.

atlantic_puffin.name: Atlantic Puffin
atlantic_puffin.habitat: Rocky islands and cliffs in the cold North Atlantic Ocean

text.summary.young: Atlantic Puffins are small black and white seabirds with bright orange beaks who live on rocky islands in the cold North Atlantic Ocean. They can carry up to 62 tiny fish in their beak at once by using special spines on their tongue to hold each fish in place.
text.summary.tiny: Puffins are brilliant little birds with bright orange beaks who can hold ten fish at once! They fly through water like tiny penguins and sleep bobbing on waves.
fun_facts.young: Baby puffins are called pufflings and they're covered in fluffy gray feathers.
Puffins spend most of their life at sea and only come to land to have babies.
They can swim underwater using their wings like flippers.
Puffins mate with the same partner year after year.
Their beaks glow under special UV light that humans can't see.
A group of puffins is called a circus or a puffinry.
fun_facts.tiny: Baby puffins are called pufflings and they're covered in fluffy grey feathers.
They can flap their wings faster than you can clap your hands.
Puffins mate with the same partner every year.
did_you_know.young: Puffins can flap their wings up to 400 times per minute to fly fast through the air.
They use their bright orange feet to steer underwater like little paddles when they swim.
Puffins dig burrows in the ground to make cozy nests for their babies.
Their colorful beaks turn brighter orange during mating season to attract a partner.
Puffins can dive as deep as 200 feet underwater to catch fish.
text.size_comparison.young: Only about as long as a ruler — a tiny seabird with a big colourful beak.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as an apple — around 14 ounces.
text.map_narration: Atlantic puffins nest on rocky cliffs along the coasts of the North Atlantic Ocean.
text.sound_description.young: Puffins make low growling and grunting sounds in their burrows and soft chirping calls when they're with their family.

hummingbird.name: Hummingbird
hummingbird.habitat: Gardens, forests, and meadows with lots of flowers

text.summary.young: Hummingbirds are tiny, colorful birds that live in North and South America. They beat their wings so fast — up to 80 times per second — that their wings make a humming sound.
text.summary.tiny: Hummingbirds are the tiniest birds in the whole world, and their wings beat so fast they hum! Some are smaller than your thumb.
fun_facts.young: Hummingbirds are the smallest birds in the world — some are only as big as a bee!
They can fly up to 60 miles per hour when diving.
Their wings move in a figure-eight pattern, not up and down like other birds.
They eat every 10 minutes to keep their energy up.
They drink nectar from flowers using their long tongues, which they can flick 13 times per second.
At night, hummingbirds go into a deep sleep called torpor to save energy — their heart rate drops to just 50 beats per minute.
fun_facts.tiny: They're the only birds that can fly backwards.
Their hearts beat faster than a drum roll when they're flying.
They visit thousands of flowers every single day looking for sweet nectar.
did_you_know.young: They are the only birds that can fly backwards and sideways.
Their hearts beat over 1,000 times per minute when they're flying.
They can hover in one spot like a tiny helicopter.
They remember every flower they've visited and how long it takes each flower to refill with nectar.
They visit up to 2,000 flowers every single day to find food.
text.size_comparison.young: The smallest bird in the world — smaller than your thumb!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh less than a coin — lighter than a single paper clip.
text.map_narration: Hummingbirds live only in the Americas, from Alaska all the way down to Chile.
text.sound_description.young: They make a soft humming sound with their fast-beating wings and chirp or squeak to talk to each other.

blue_jay.name: Blue Jay
blue_jay.habitat: Forests and backyards in North America

text.summary.young: Blue jays are bright blue birds with black necklaces that live in forests across North America. They can copy the sounds of hawks to trick other birds into leaving their food behind.
text.summary.tiny: Blue jays are bright blue birds with black necklaces that can copy hawk sounds to trick other birds. They're so clever they remember where they hid thousands of acorns.
fun_facts.young: Blue jays are very smart and can solve puzzles to get food
They have a special crest of feathers on their head that stands up when they're excited or scared
They love to eat acorns, peanuts, and sunflower seeds
They live in the same area all year and don't fly south for winter
They take baths in water and sometimes even in snow
A group of blue jays is called a party
fun_facts.tiny: They aren't really blue — their feathers just look blue because of how light bounces off them.
They take baths in water and sometimes even in snow.
They plant new oak trees by burying acorns and forgetting where they hid them.
did_you_know.young: They aren't actually blue — their feathers only look blue because of the way light bounces off them
A blue jay can remember where it hid thousands of acorns
They plant new oak trees by burying acorns and forgetting where they put them
They stay with their families all winter long
They can crack open acorns with their strong beaks
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a school ruler — bright blue with a pointy crest on their head.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as an egg — around 3 ounces.
text.map_narration: Blue jays live in the forests and gardens of eastern North America.
text.sound_description.young: They make loud calls that sound like 'jay jay' and can also sing pretty songs.

cardinal.name: Cardinal
cardinal.habitat: Forests, gardens, and backyards across North America

text.summary.young: Cardinals are bright red songbirds that live in North America. Both the male and female cardinals sing beautiful songs to each other, even when the mom is sitting on her eggs.
text.summary.tiny: Cardinals are bright red birds that sing all year long. Mums and dads both sing — even while mum sits on her eggs!
fun_facts.young: Cardinals love to visit bird feeders and eat sunflower seeds
The red color comes from the foods they eat, like berries and fruits
They sing over 20 different songs
They take baths in shallow puddles and splash water all over themselves
Male cardinals sometimes feed seeds to their mates as a gift
They can fly up to 40 miles per hour
fun_facts.tiny: They get their red colour from eating berries and fruits.
They love splashing in puddles and getting soaking wet.
Dad cardinals sometimes bring seeds to mum as a present.
did_you_know.young: Male cardinals are bright red, but females are soft brown with red wings and tail
They don't migrate — they stay in the same place all year, even in winter
Baby cardinals are born with black beaks that turn orange as they grow up
They crack open seeds with their strong, cone-shaped beaks
A cardinal couple will stay together for their whole lives
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a banana — bright red and easy to spot in winter!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as an egg — around 2 ounces.
text.map_narration: Cardinals live in the forests, gardens, and parks of eastern North America and Mexico.
text.sound_description.young: They sing clear, whistling songs that sound like 'cheer-cheer-cheer' or 'birdy-birdy-birdy'.

text.summary.young: Woodpeckers are birds that live in forests all around the world. They hammer on trees up to 20 times per second and never get headaches because their brain floats inside a spongy skull that works like a natural helmet.
text.summary.tiny: Woodpeckers hammer on trees up to 20 times every second and never get headaches. Their brain floats inside a spongy skull that works like a helmet.
fun_facts.young: Woodpeckers have sticky spit on their tongues to catch bugs hiding in tree bark.
They can peck a hole big enough to live in after just two weeks of work.
Baby woodpeckers are born completely bald with no feathers at all.
They store acorns in trees — one bird collected over 50,000 acorns in a single oak tree.
Their beaks are harder than most tree bark and never stop growing.
They close their eyes every time they hit the tree so wood chips don't hurt them.
fun_facts.tiny: They've got sticky spit on their tongues to catch bugs hiding in bark.
They close their eyes every single time they hit the tree so wood chips don't hurt them.
One woodpecker stored over 50,000 acorns in a single oak tree.
did_you_know.young: A woodpecker's tongue is so long it wraps around the back of its skull when not in use.
They have special tail feathers that prop them up like a tripod while they peck.
Their nostrils are covered with tiny feathers to keep wood chips from getting inside.
Some woodpeckers drum on metal pipes and gutters to make louder sounds and attract mates.
They peck about 12,000 times every single day without getting tired.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a ruler — with a strong beak for hammering on trees!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as an egg — around 3 ounces.
text.map_narration: Woodpeckers live in forests all around the world except Australia and Antarctica.
text.sound_description.young: They make a fast tapping sound when they peck on trees and a loud drumming sound to talk to other woodpeckers.

text.summary.young: Swans are large white birds that live on lakes and rivers in Europe, Asia, and North America. They mate for life and stay with the same partner for over 20 years — some swans even grieve when their mate dies.
text.summary.tiny: Swans are huge white birds with necks as long as your arm. They stay with the same partner their whole lives — some even feel sad when their partner dies.
fun_facts.young: Swans eat underwater plants by dipping their long necks deep into the water like a snorkel.
A swan's wingspan can be over 8 feet wide — wider than most adults are tall!
They are very protective parents and will hiss and chase away anyone who gets too close to their babies.
Mute swans aren't actually mute — they grunt, snort, and hiss to communicate.
They sleep floating on the water with one leg tucked up and their head resting on their back.
It takes a swan up to 50 feet of running on water to take off and fly into the sky.
fun_facts.tiny: They dip their long necks underwater to munch on plants growing at the bottom.
A swan's wings spread wider than your dad is tall.
Baby swans are fluffy and grey, then turn white as they grow up.
did_you_know.young: They can fly up to 60 miles per hour — that's as fast as a car on the highway!
A baby swan is called a cygnet and has fluffy gray feathers that turn white as it grows up.
They have over 25,000 feathers to keep them warm and dry in cold water.
When swans fall in love, they bend their necks into a heart shape to show affection.
They can weigh as much as two bowling balls but still glide gracefully across the water.
text.size_comparison.young: With their long neck stretched up, they can be as tall as a grown-up — about 5 feet!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a house cat — around 22 pounds.
text.map_narration: Swans live on lakes, rivers, and ponds across Europe, Asia, and North America.
text.sound_description.young: They honk loudly like a trumpet and hiss when they want to warn others to stay away.

text.summary.young: Parrots are colorful birds with curved beaks that live in warm forests around the world. They can copy human words and sounds because they have two voice boxes instead of one.
text.summary.tiny: Parrots are bright birds with curved beaks that copy sounds and words. They're as clever as a three-year-old child.
fun_facts.young: A parrot's curved beak is so strong it can crack open hard nuts.
Parrots are left-footed or right-footed, just like humans are left-handed or right-handed.
Baby parrots are called chicks and are born without feathers.
They love to dance and bob their heads when they hear music.
Wild parrots sleep in big groups called flocks to stay safe at night.
They can see colors that humans can't see because their eyes are extra special.
fun_facts.tiny: They hold their food with their feet while they eat, just like you hold a biscuit.
Some parrots live longer than your granny — they can reach 80 years old.
Baby parrots are born pink and bald without a single feather.
did_you_know.young: They can live for 80 years — some parrots are older than grandparents!
They are one of the only animals that can talk like humans.
They use their feet like hands to hold food while they eat.
Some parrots can learn over 100 different words.
They mate for life and stay with the same partner forever.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a ruler — colourful, chatty, and always up to something!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a carton of milk — around 3 pounds.
text.map_narration: Parrots live in tropical forests all around the world, from South America to Australia.
text.sound_description.young: They squawk loudly to talk to each other and can copy human words and other sounds perfectly.

cockatoo.name: Cockatoo
cockatoo.habitat: Forests and woodlands in Australia and Asia

text.summary.young: Cockatoos are loud, colorful parrots with big crests on their heads that live in Australia and parts of Asia. They are the only animals besides humans who can hear music and dance to the beat — each cockatoo even makes up its own special dance moves!
text.summary.tiny: Cockatoos are the only animals besides you who can hear music and dance to the beat! Each one makes up its own special moves.
fun_facts.young: Their beaks are so strong they can crack open really hard nuts like almonds and walnuts.
Cockatoos are loud talkers — their calls can be heard over a mile away in the wild!
They love to chew on wood and branches to keep their beaks healthy and sharp.
Some cockatoos have beautiful pink or yellow feathers under their white wings.
They're very social birds and live in big flocks with hundreds of other cockatoos.
They can learn to say words and copy sounds they hear around them.
fun_facts.tiny: Their beaks crack open nuts as hard as stones.
They live as long as your grandparents — some reach 70!
When they're excited, their fancy crest pops straight up.
did_you_know.young: They can live as long as your grandparents — some reach 70 years old!
They use sticks and twigs as tools to reach food they can't get with their beaks.
A cockatoo's crest stands up when they're excited, surprised, or showing off.
They can open complicated locks and latches just by watching and learning.
They mate for life and stay with the same partner for decades.
