text.size_comparison.young: About as tall as a ruler and a half — with a big showy crest they raise when excited!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a loaf of bread — around 2 pounds.
text.map_narration: Cockatoos live in the forests of Australia, Indonesia, and nearby islands.
text.sound_description.young: They make loud squawking and screeching sounds that can be heard from very far away.

canary.name: Canary
canary.habitat: Canary Islands, forests, gardens, homes worldwide

text.summary.young: Canaries are small yellow songbirds originally from the Canary Islands. They were once taken into coal mines to warn miners of dangerous gas — if the canary stopped singing, it meant everyone had to leave quickly.
text.summary.tiny: Canaries are tiny yellow birds with the most beautiful songs. They were once taken deep underground into mines to keep people safe — if the canary stopped singing, everyone knew to rush out fast.
fun_facts.young: Canaries love to take baths and splash in water.
A canary's heart beats over 1,000 times per minute.
Canaries molt their feathers once a year and grow new ones.
Baby canaries can't sing — they learn songs from their fathers.
Canaries eat seeds, fruits, and vegetables.
A canary can live for 10 to 15 years with good care.
fun_facts.tiny: Only daddy canaries sing — mummy canaries make quiet little chirps.
A canary's heart beats faster than you can count.
Baby canaries can't sing at all until they listen to their dads and learn every note.
did_you_know.young: Canaries can sing over 20 different songs!
Only male canaries sing — females chirp quietly.
A canary's song can last up to 30 seconds without stopping.
Canaries can see colors that humans can't see.
Wild canaries are greenish-brown, not bright yellow.
text.size_comparison.young: Tiny enough to sit in the palm of your hand — only about 5 inches long.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh less than a cookie — lighter than two coins.
text.map_narration: Canaries come from the Canary Islands off the coast of Africa — that's how they got their name!
text.sound_description.young: Canaries sing long, beautiful songs with high chirps and rolling trills.

text.summary.young: Robins are small songbirds with bright red-orange chests that live in Europe, Asia, and North Africa. They are surprisingly fierce and will fight other robins — even their own reflection in windows — to protect their territory.
text.summary.tiny: Robins have bright red-orange chests and they're surprisingly fierce. They'll fight other robins to protect their garden.
fun_facts.young: Robins eat worms, insects, berries, and seeds.
A robin can tilt its head to listen for worms moving underground.
They build cup-shaped nests from mud, grass, and moss.
Baby robins don't have red chests — they're spotted brown until they grow up.
They often follow gardeners around to catch worms that get dug up.
A robin's red chest looks brightest in spring when they're trying to impress a mate.
fun_facts.tiny: A robin can tilt its head to listen for worms moving underground.
Baby robins are spotted brown — they don't get their red chest until they grow up.
They follow gardeners around to catch worms that get dug up.
did_you_know.young: They sometimes sing all through the night in cities because streetlights make them think it's daytime.
A robin's red chest isn't just pretty — it's a warning sign to other robins to stay away.
They can remember where they buried hundreds of worms and insects to eat later.
In winter, female robins defend their own territories just as fiercely as males do.
They have been known to attack their own reflection in car mirrors because they think it's another robin invading their space.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a banana — with a bright red breast that's easy to spot.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh less than a cookie — lighter than a handful of coins.
text.map_narration: Robins live in gardens, parks, and forests across Europe.
text.sound_description.young: They sing a cheerful, warbling song with quick notes that go up and down.

text.summary.young: Albatrosses are huge seabirds that live over the cold Southern Ocean and Pacific Ocean. They can fly over 1,000 kilometres in a single day without flapping their wings — they lock their wings open and glide on ocean winds.
text.summary.tiny: Albatrosses are giant seabirds with wings that stretch as wide as a small car. They lock their wings open and glide over the ocean for hours without flapping once.
fun_facts.young: An albatross has the longest wings of any bird — they can stretch as wide as a small aeroplane!
Albatrosses only come to land to lay eggs and raise their babies.
They can smell food from over 20 kilometres away.
They mate for life and find the same partner every year.
They sleep while gliding over the ocean with one eye open.
A young albatross might fly for 5 years without ever touching land.
fun_facts.tiny: An albatross might fly for five years without ever touching land.
They can smell their dinner from further away than you can see.
They sleep while flying with one eye open.
did_you_know.young: An albatross can fly for hours without flapping its wings even once.
They drink salt water and sneeze out the extra salt through special tubes on their beaks.
Some albatrosses live to be 70 years old — that's older than most grandparents!
When albatrosses meet their partner, they dance together by spreading their wings and clacking their beaks.
Baby albatrosses stay in the nest for almost a whole year before they learn to fly.
text.size_comparison.young: With wings spread wide, they are wider than a car — the longest wingspan of any bird, around 11 feet!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a small watermelon — around 18 pounds.
text.map_narration: Albatrosses soar over the Southern Ocean and the North Pacific, spending years at sea.
text.sound_description.young: They make loud honking calls and clack their beaks together when they meet their partners.

text.summary.young: The king cobra is the world's longest venomous snake, living in the forests and swamps of Asia. It's the only snake in the world that builds a nest for its eggs and guards them until they hatch.
text.summary.tiny: The king cobra is the world's longest snake with a bite that can hurt you. It's the only snake that builds a nest and guards its eggs like a mum.
fun_facts.young: They can grow about as long as a small car — that's almost 15 feet from head to tail.
The mother guards her eggs for up to three months without eating a single meal.
With excellent eyesight, they can spot movement from over 300 feet away.
A single bite delivers enough venom to bring down 20 people — or one elephant.
King cobras are excellent swimmers and can climb trees with ease.
The name 'Ophiophagus' means 'snake-eater' in Greek — and they live up to it.
fun_facts.tiny: They can grow longer than a car — that's really, really long for a snake!
They eat other snakes — even the scary ones.
The mum guards her eggs for months without eating anything at all.
did_you_know.young: They can lift their head up to six feet off the ground — tall enough to look a grown-up in the eye.
When threatened, they spread a wide hood to make themselves look bigger and scarier.
They eat other snakes, even venomous ones — that's why they're called 'king'.
Their venom is strong enough to kill an elephant with a single bite.
Baby king cobras are venomous from the moment they hatch.
text.size_comparison.young: They're about as long as a small car — nearly 15 feet stretched out.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a big house cat — around 20 pounds.
text.map_narration: King cobras live in the forests and swamps of South and Southeast Asia.
text.sound_description.young: They make a loud, low hissing sound that sounds almost like a growl.

burmese_python.name: Burmese Python
burmese_python.habitat: Forests, swamps, and grasslands in Southeast Asia

text.summary.young: Burmese pythons are giant snakes that live in forests and swamps across Southeast Asia. They can swallow animals as large as deer whole, then go an entire year without eating again.
text.summary.tiny: Burmese pythons are giant snakes that can swallow animals as big as deer whole. They live in forests and swamps and can go a whole year without eating.
fun_facts.young: Burmese pythons don't chew their food — they swallow it whole.
These snakes can hold their breath underwater for 30 minutes while hunting.
A python's stretchy skin lets its belly grow huge after a big meal.
Baby Burmese pythons are about as long as a ruler when they hatch.
Pythons squeeze their prey tight until it stops breathing, then swallow it headfirst.
These snakes shed their entire skin in one piece as they grow.
fun_facts.tiny: These snakes squeeze their food tight until it stops breathing.
A python's belly stretches huge after a big meal.
They can hold their breath underwater for half an hour.
did_you_know.young: A Burmese python can open its jaws wide enough to swallow a whole deer.
After eating a huge meal, a Burmese python can go a whole year without eating again.
Mother pythons shiver their muscles to keep their eggs warm, just like a living blanket.
They have heat sensors on their lips that help them find warm animals in the dark.
These snakes can grow as long as a car and weigh as much as a grown man.
text.size_comparison.young: One of the longest snakes in the world — about as long as a car, around 16 feet!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a grown-up and a bit more — around 200 pounds.
text.map_narration: Burmese pythons come from the forests of Southeast Asia.
text.sound_description.young: They make a loud hissing sound when they breathe out, especially if they feel threatened.

green_anaconda.name: Green Anaconda
green_anaconda.habitat: Rivers, swamps, and rainforests of South America

text.summary.young: Green anacondas are the world's heaviest snakes and live in rivers and swamps of South America. They hunt by hiding underwater, then wrapping their powerful bodies around animals and squeezing them until they stop breathing.
text.summary.tiny: Green anacondas are the world's heaviest snakes. They hide underwater in rivers and swamps, then wrap around animals and squeeze until they stop breathing.
fun_facts.young: Their eyes and nose are on top of their head so they can see and breathe while the rest of their body hides underwater.
They don't chew their food — they swallow animals whole!
After eating a big meal, they might not need to eat again for weeks or even months.
Their green and brown spotted skin helps them blend in with muddy water and plants.
Baby anacondas are already 2 feet long when they're born and can swim right away.
They shed their skin several times a year as they grow bigger and bigger.
fun_facts.tiny: Their eyes and nose sit on top of their head so they can see and breathe while the rest hides underwater.
They swallow animals whole without chewing!
After a big meal, they might not eat again for weeks.
did_you_know.young: A green anaconda can weigh as much as a baby elephant!
They can hold their breath underwater for up to 10 minutes while waiting for prey.
Female anacondas are much bigger than males — sometimes twice as heavy!
They can open their jaws wide enough to swallow a whole deer.
They give birth to live babies instead of laying eggs — up to 40 babies at once!
text.size_comparison.young: The heaviest snake in the world — about as long as a large car, around 20 feet!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as two grown-ups — around 220 pounds.
text.map_narration: Green anacondas live in the swamps, marshes, and rivers of South America.
text.sound_description.young: They hiss loudly when they feel threatened or want to scare away danger.

text.summary.young: Komodo dragons are the biggest lizards in the world and live on a few small islands in Indonesia. They have venom in their lower jaw that helps them hunt deer, pigs, and even water buffalo.
text.summary.tiny: Komodo dragons are the biggest lizards in the whole world. They live on just a few tiny islands and hunt with a special bite that makes animals sleepy.
fun_facts.young: A Komodo dragon's teeth are so sharp they're like little saws — perfect for cutting meat.
They can smell a dead animal from almost 10 kilometres away using their forked tongue.
Komodo dragons swallow their food in huge chunks — sometimes they even swallow whole goats!
They live on only five small islands in Indonesia and nowhere else in the world.
Their saliva has more than 50 types of bacteria that help break down their food.
They can live for 30 years in the wild.
fun_facts.tiny: They can smell dinner from really, really far away — even further than you can see.
A hungry Komodo dragon can swallow a whole goat.
Baby Komodos climb trees to hide from grown-up Komodos who might eat them.
did_you_know.young: They can eat up to 80% of their body weight in one meal — that's like you eating 160 hamburgers at once!
Female Komodo dragons can have babies without a male — they're one of the only large animals that can do this.
They have a special sense organ in their mouth that helps them taste the air and find food from miles away.
They can run as fast as a dog for short distances — up to 20 kilometres per hour!
Baby Komodo dragons climb trees to stay safe from adult Komodos who might try to eat them.
text.size_comparison.young: The biggest lizard alive — about as long as a small car, around 8 feet from nose to tail!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a grown-up — around 176 pounds.
text.map_narration: Komodo dragons live only on a few small islands in Indonesia.
text.sound_description.young: They hiss loudly when they feel threatened and make low growling sounds.

text.summary.young: Iguanas are large lizards that live in warm forests and jungles of Central and South America. They have a third eye on top of their head that helps them sense danger from above.
text.summary.tiny: Iguanas are big lizards with bumpy spines down their backs. They've got a secret eye on top of their heads that watches the sky.
fun_facts.young: Iguanas eat flowers, leaves, and fruit — no meat at all!
They can drop their tail if grabbed by a predator and grow a new one.
Baby iguanas hatch from eggs buried in warm sand.
They love to sunbathe on tree branches to warm up their bodies.
They can fall 40 feet from a tree and land safely.
Their sharp claws help them climb trees and rocky cliffs.
fun_facts.tiny: They only eat flowers, leaves and fruit — never any meat.
If something grabs their tail, they can drop it off and grow a brand new one.
They love sunbathing on branches to warm up their whole body.
did_you_know.young: They have a third eye on top of their head that can sense light and shadows.
They use their long tail like a whip to defend themselves.
They are excellent swimmers and can hold their breath underwater.
Their spiky back helps protect them from predators.
Some iguanas can grow as long as a bathtub.
text.size_comparison.young: From nose to tail tip, they can be as long as your arm and more — around 5 feet!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bag of sugar — around 9 pounds.
text.map_narration: Green iguanas live in the tropical forests of Central and South America and the Caribbean.
text.sound_description.young: They hiss loudly when they feel threatened and make huffing sounds when they breathe.

text.summary.young: Bearded dragons are friendly lizards from Australia with spiky scales under their chin that look like a beard. When they feel threatened, they puff out their beard and turn it black to look bigger and scarier!
text.summary.tiny: Bearded dragons are friendly lizards from Australia with spiky scales under their chin that look like a beard. They puff out their beard and turn it black when they want to look bigger!
fun_facts.young: Bearded dragons can run on their back legs when they're in a hurry!
They have a third eye on top of their head that senses light and shadows from above.
When they're happy and relaxed, bearded dragons close one eye at a time — like they're winking at you!
Their spiky beard isn't sharp at all — it's made of soft, rubbery scales.
They can live in hot deserts where temperatures reach 40°C (104°F).
They catch insects by shooting out their sticky tongue super fast — faster than you can blink!
fun_facts.tiny: They can run on their back legs when they're in a hurry!
They've got a third eye on top of their head that spots shadows from above.
Their spiky beard isn't sharp at all — it's made of soft, rubbery scales.
did_you_know.young: They wave one arm slowly at other dragons to say hello or show they're friendly.
They bob their heads up and down really fast to show they're in charge.
They can change the color of their beard from yellow to jet black.
They love to bask in the sun on rocks and tree branches to warm up their bodies.
Baby bearded dragons eat mostly insects, but grown-ups also munch on vegetables and flowers.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as your forearm — with a spiky "beard" under their chin!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a can of beans — around 12 ounces.
text.map_narration: Bearded dragons come from the dry deserts and woodlands of Australia.
text.sound_description.young: They hiss softly when they puff out their black beard to warn others to stay away.

gila_monster.name: Gila Monster
gila_monster.habitat: Deserts and rocky hillsides in the southwestern United States and Mexico

text.summary.young: The Gila monster is a venomous lizard that lives in the deserts of the southwestern United States and Mexico. It's one of only two venomous lizards in the entire world, and scientists used a protein from its spit to make medicine that helps people with diabetes.
text.summary.tiny: The Gila monster is a lizard with bumpy skin covered in bright orange and black patterns. It's one of only two lizards in the whole world that can make poison in its mouth.
fun_facts.young: Gila monsters are named after the Gila River in Arizona where they were first discovered
They spend about 95% of their life underground in burrows staying cool
Their colorful beaded skin has patterns of orange, pink, or yellow mixed with black
They don't chase prey — they slowly walk around sniffing for bird eggs and baby animals in nests
When they bite, they hold on tight and chew to work their venom into the wound
Scientists discovered that a protein in Gila monster spit helps control blood sugar, so they made it into diabetes medicine
fun_facts.tiny: They spend almost all their time underground staying cool.
They can eat so much in one meal that they don't need to eat again for months.
Their thick tails store fat like a lunchbox they carry with them.
did_you_know.young: They can eat up to one-third of their body weight in a single meal
They store fat in their thick tails so they can go months without eating
They have black tongues that they flick out to smell the air
Their venom doesn't squirt like a snake's — it drips down grooves in their teeth when they bite
Baby Gila monsters are born with enough venom to protect themselves right away
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as your forearm — chunky, colourful, and one of only a few venomous lizards.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a carton of milk — around 3 pounds.
text.map_narration: Gila monsters live in the deserts of the southwestern United States and Mexico.
text.sound_description.young: They hiss when they feel threatened or want to be left alone.

alligator.name: Alligator
alligator.habitat: freshwater swamps, marshes, rivers, and lakes

text.summary.young: Alligators are large reptiles with powerful jaws that live in swamps and rivers in America and China. Mother alligators carry their tiny babies gently in their mouths to keep them safe from danger.
text.summary.tiny: Alligators are huge swimming giants with the strongest bite in the whole swamp. Mummy alligators carry their tiny babies in their mouths — very, very gently.
fun_facts.young: Alligators can't chew their food — they swallow it whole or tear it into chunks!
An alligator has about 80 teeth, and when one falls out, a new tooth grows back in its place.
They dig underwater dens called 'gator holes' that help other animals survive during droughts.
Mother alligators stay with their babies for up to a year to protect them from predators.
They can run fast on land for short distances — up to 35 kilometres per hour!
In cold weather, alligators stick just their snout out of frozen water to breathe while the rest of their body stays warm below the ice.
fun_facts.tiny: They can't chew — they swallow everything whole or rip it into chunks.
When an alligator loses a tooth, a brand new one grows back.
In freezing weather, alligators poke just their nose through the ice to breathe while they wait for spring.
did_you_know.young: They have been around for 8 million years and look almost exactly the same as their ancient ancestors.
An alligator's bite is one of the strongest in the animal kingdom — stronger than a lion's!
They can hold their breath underwater for up to 2 hours when they're resting.
Baby alligators make squeaking sounds inside their eggs to tell their mother they're ready to hatch.
They have special flaps in their throat that let them open their mouth underwater without drowning.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a car — around 13 feet from snout to tail!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as five or six grown-ups — around 800 pounds.
text.map_narration: American alligators live in the swamps, lakes, and rivers of the southeastern United States.
text.sound_description.young: They hiss when they're warning others to stay away, and they make deep bellowing roars during mating season.

text.summary.young: Crocodiles are large reptiles that live in rivers and swamps across Africa, Asia, Australia, and parts of Central and South America. They have the strongest bite of any animal on Earth — powerful enough to crush bones!
text.summary.tiny: Crocodiles have the strongest bite of any animal on Earth! They live in rivers and swamps and can hold their breath underwater for over an hour.
fun_facts.young: Crocodiles can't stick out their tongues because they're attached to the bottom of their mouths.
Baby crocodiles call to their mother from inside their eggs when they're ready to hatch.
Their mothers gently carry their babies in their mouths to keep them safe.
They can live for 70 to 100 years — longer than most humans!
A crocodile's eyes and nostrils sit on top of its head so it can see and breathe while hiding underwater.
They can swim up to 25 miles per hour by swishing their powerful tails.
fun_facts.tiny: Baby crocodiles call to their mum from inside their eggs when they're ready to hatch.
Their mums gently carry their babies in their mouths to keep them safe.
They swallow stones to help mash up food in their tummies because they can't chew.
did_you_know.young: They swallow stones to help grind up food in their stomachs because they can't chew.
They cry real tears while they eat, but not because they feel sad — it helps keep their eyes clean!
A crocodile can hold its breath underwater for over an hour while waiting for prey.
They have been around for over 200 million years — they lived alongside the dinosaurs!
A crocodile's bite is the strongest of any animal alive today.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a large car — around 16 feet from snout to tail, and some grow even bigger!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a horse — around 1,500 pounds.
text.map_narration: Crocodiles live in tropical rivers, lakes, and coastlines across Africa, Asia, Australia, and the Americas.
text.sound_description.young: They hiss when they're threatened and make deep bellowing roars during mating season.

text.summary.young: Box turtles are small turtles that live in forests and fields across North America. They can close their shell completely like a box — no other turtle can seal themselves up so tightly.
text.summary.tiny: Box turtles can close their shell completely like a treasure chest — no other turtle can seal up so tight. They live in forests and fields, eating berries and bugs.
fun_facts.young: Box turtles can't swim well, so they prefer to live on land instead of in ponds.
Their shell is part of their skeleton — it's made of over 50 bones fused together!
Male box turtles often have bright red eyes, while females usually have brown eyes.
They can remember where they found food and will return to that spot again and again.
They help forests grow by eating berries and spreading seeds in their poop.
When scared, a box turtle pulls its head, legs, and tail inside and shuts the door — predators can't get in!
fun_facts.tiny: Male box turtles often have bright red eyes, while females have brown eyes.
They remember where they found yummy food and go back to that same spot.
Their shell is made of over 50 bones all joined together — it's part of their skeleton!
did_you_know.young: A box turtle can live for 100 years — longer than most people!
They have a special hinge on their bottom shell that lets them close up tight like a treasure chest.
They eat both plants and animals — strawberries, worms, mushrooms, and snails are all on the menu.
They return to the same winter sleeping spot year after year, sometimes for their whole life.
Baby box turtles have flat shells — the dome shape grows as they get older.
text.size_comparison.young: Small enough to hold in both hands — their shell is about as wide as your hand.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as an apple — around 14 ounces.
text.map_narration: Box turtles live in the forests and meadows of eastern North America and Mexico.
text.sound_description.young: They make a quiet hissing sound when they pull their head inside their shell quickly.

text.summary.young: Monitor lizards are large reptiles found in Africa, Asia, and Australia. They can stand up on their back legs like tiny dinosaurs to look around their territory.
text.summary.tiny: Monitor lizards can stand up on their back legs like tiny dinosaurs. They flick their forked tongue to taste the air around them.
fun_facts.young: Monitor lizards flick their tongue in and out to taste smells in the air.
They can eat animals as big as deer.
Baby monitor lizards often live in trees to stay safe from bigger animals.
Their long tail helps them balance when they stand up tall.
They have strong jaws and over 60 sharp teeth.
They are smart reptiles and can remember where they hid food.
fun_facts.tiny: They've got over sixty sharp teeth.
Their long tail helps them balance when they stand tall.
Baby monitor lizards climb trees to stay safe.
did_you_know.young: They have a forked tongue just like snakes to smell the air.
Some monitor lizards can run as fast as a person.
They are excellent swimmers and can hold their breath underwater.
They have sharp claws perfect for climbing trees.
The Komodo dragon is the biggest monitor lizard in the world.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a grown-up lying down — around 6 feet 6 inches from nose to tail.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a big suitcase — around 110 pounds.
text.map_narration: Monitor lizards live in the warm forests and grasslands of Africa, Asia, and Australia.
text.sound_description.young: They hiss loudly when they feel threatened and make low growling sounds.

gecko.name: Gecko
gecko.habitat: Warm forests, deserts, and tropical areas worldwide

text.summary.young: Geckos are small lizards that live in warm places all around the world. They can walk upside down on ceilings because their toes have millions of tiny hairs that stick to almost anything.
text.summary.tiny: Geckos can walk upside down on your ceiling! Their toes have millions of teeny tiny hairs that stick to almost anything.
fun_facts.young: Geckos come in lots of colors—green, brown, orange, spotted, and even bright blue!
Many geckos hunt insects at night using their big eyes to see in the dark.
They shed their skin as they grow, and some eat the old skin for extra nutrients.
Some geckos can change color to blend in with trees or rocks.
The smallest gecko in the world is tiny enough to curl up on your fingertip!
They use their sticky toes to climb trees, rocks, and even your bedroom wall.
fun_facts.tiny: Most geckos don't have eyelids, so they lick their own eyes to keep them clean.
Some geckos can drop their tails if something scary grabs them, then grow a brand new tail later.
The smallest gecko is so tiny it could curl up on your fingertip.
did_you_know.young: A gecko's toes have millions of tiny hairs—so tiny you'd need a microscope to see them!
They can stick to glass, smooth walls, and even walk across ceilings without falling.
Most geckos don't have eyelids—they lick their eyes to keep them clean!
Some geckos can drop their tails if a predator grabs them, then grow a new tail later.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as your finger — tiny, quick, and they can walk up walls!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as an egg — almost nothing at all.
text.map_narration: Geckos live in warm places all around the world, from deserts to rainforests.
text.sound_description.young: They make chirping, clicking, and squeaking sounds to talk to each other.

skink.name: Skink
skink.habitat: Forests, deserts, gardens, and grasslands worldwide

text.summary.young: Skinks are smooth, shiny lizards with short legs that live in forests, deserts, and gardens around the world. Some skinks can drop their tail when scared — it wiggles on the ground to trick predators while the skink runs away!
text.summary.tiny: Skinks are shiny lizards with legs so tiny they wiggle like snakes. They can drop their tail when something scary comes — the tail wiggles all by itself while the skink runs away!
fun_facts.young: Skinks love to sunbathe on warm rocks to heat up their bodies.
Some skinks can live underground and burrow through sand like little diggers.
Blue-tongued skinks stick out their bright blue tongues to scare away enemies.
They eat insects, snails, and fruit — they're not picky eaters!
A skink's scales are so smooth and shiny they look like they're made of glass.
Some skinks can squeeze through tiny cracks to hide from danger.
fun_facts.tiny: Blue-tongued skinks stick out their bright blue tongues to scare away animals that might hurt them.
They love sunbathing on warm rocks because they need sunshine to warm up their bodies.
Some skinks squeeze through cracks as thin as your finger to hide.
did_you_know.young: Some skinks give birth to live babies instead of laying eggs — just like mammals do!
A skink's tail can break off and grow back — it might take months to regrow completely.
They have tiny legs and move by wiggling their body like a snake.
Some skinks have blue tails when they're young to distract predators from their head.
They can blink — they have movable eyelids unlike many other lizards.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a banana — smooth, shiny, and super fast!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as an egg — around 2 ounces.
text.map_narration: Skinks live all over the world in warm places, from forests to gardens to deserts.
text.sound_description.young: They usually stay quiet, but they can hiss softly when they feel scared or threatened.

text.summary.young: Vipers are venomous snakes found on every continent except Antarctica and Australia. They have special heat-sensing pits on their faces that let them hunt warm animals in complete darkness.
text.summary.tiny: Vipers can see heat like magic! They find warm animals in the dark using special spots on their faces.
fun_facts.young: Vipers have the longest fangs of any snake
Their heat-sensing pits work like night-vision goggles
Some vipers can go months without eating
They swallow their prey whole — even if it's bigger than their head
They shed their skin several times a year as they grow
Their pupils are shaped like thin slits instead of circles
fun_facts.tiny: Their fangs fold up like tiny pocket knives when they're not hunting.
They can wait months and months between meals.
They swallow their dinner whole — even if it's bigger than their own head!
did_you_know.young: They can sense heat from a mouse's body even in total darkness
Their fangs fold up like tiny pocket knives when not in use
Some vipers can detect temperature differences as small as three thousandths of a degree
Baby vipers are born with venom and can hunt right away
They shake their tails as a warning before they strike
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as your arm — thick-bodied and dangerously quick.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a loaf of bread — around 1 pound.
text.map_narration: Vipers live on every continent except Australia and Antarctica.
text.sound_description.young: They make a loud hissing sound by pushing air through their mouths as a warning.

text.summary.young: Rattlesnakes are venomous snakes that live in deserts and grasslands across North and South America. They shake the rattle on their tail to warn animals to stay away before they bite.
text.summary.tiny: Rattlesnakes shake the rattle on their tail to say stay away. They live in deserts and grasslands where it's hot and dry.
fun_facts.young: Rattlesnakes can strike faster than you can blink.
Some rattlesnakes can go a whole year without eating.
A rattlesnake shakes its rattle up to 50 times per second.
They swallow their food whole — even mice and rabbits.
The oldest rattlesnakes can live more than 25 years in the wild.
They hibernate in dens with hundreds of other snakes during winter.
fun_facts.tiny: They can strike faster than you can blink.
They swallow mice whole without even chewing.
In winter, hundreds of rattlesnakes snuggle together in one den to keep warm.
did_you_know.young: They add a new segment to their rattle every time they shed their skin.
A rattlesnake's rattle is made of the same stuff as your fingernails.
Baby rattlesnakes are born with just one button on their tail — not a full rattle yet.
They can sense the body heat of other animals with special pits on their face.
A rattlesnake's fangs fold back when its mouth is closed, like pocket knives.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a baseball bat — with a rattle on their tail that warns you to stay away!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a carton of milk — around 3 pounds.
text.map_narration: Rattlesnakes live in the deserts, forests, and grasslands of North and South America.
text.sound_description.young: They hiss and shake their tail rattle to make a buzzing warning sound.

text.summary.young: Sea snakes are venomous snakes that live in warm ocean waters of the Indian and Pacific Oceans. They can breathe through their skin underwater, which lets them stay down for hours without coming up for air.
text.summary.tiny: Sea snakes live in warm oceans and they've got something amazing — they can breathe through their skin! They can stay underwater for hours without coming up for air.
fun_facts.young: Sea snakes have special glands under their tongues that get rid of extra salt from the ocean water.
Their nostrils are on top of their snouts so they can breathe while floating.
They eat fish and eels that they catch with their venomous bite.
They can dive as deep as 100 meters looking for food.
They are more closely related to cobras than to other water snakes.
Their venom is very strong, but they rarely bite people.
fun_facts.tiny: Their noses are right on top of their heads so they can breathe while they float.
Their tails are flat like paddles to help them zoom through the water.
They're cousins of cobras but they live in the sea instead of on land.
did_you_know.young: They can stay underwater for up to 8 hours without breathing air.
Their tails are shaped like paddles to help them swim.
They shed their skin more often than land snakes — sometimes every few weeks.
Most sea snakes can't move well on land because their bellies are too smooth.
Some sea snakes give birth to live babies in the water instead of laying eggs.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a baseball bat — with a flat paddle tail for swimming.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a loaf of bread — around 2 pounds.
text.map_narration: Sea snakes live in the warm tropical waters of the Indian and Pacific Oceans.
text.sound_description.young: They hiss when they come up to breathe air at the surface.

frilled_lizard.name: Frilled Lizard
frilled_lizard.habitat: Forests and woodlands in Australia and Papua New Guinea

text.summary.young: Frilled lizards live in the warm forests and woodlands of Australia and Papua New Guinea. When scared, they open a giant frill around their neck like an umbrella and run away on two legs like a tiny dinosaur.
text.summary.tiny: When a frilled lizard gets scared, it opens a giant frill around its neck like an umbrella. Then it runs away on two legs like a tiny dinosaur!
fun_facts.young: A frilled lizard's frill is made of skin stretched over long pieces of cartilage like an umbrella.
When they open their frill, their mouth opens wide too, making them look even scarier.
They eat insects, spiders, and small lizards.
Frilled lizards can change color slightly to match the trees they're sitting on.
Baby frilled lizards have a frill from the day they hatch.
They're one of the few lizards that regularly run on two legs instead of four.
fun_facts.tiny: Their neck frill stays folded flat until they need it.
When they open their frill, their mouth opens wide too.
They're one of the few lizards that run on two legs.
did_you_know.young: They can run on just their back legs when they're in a hurry.
Their neck frill stays folded flat against their body until they need it.
They spend most of their time high up in trees looking for insects to eat.
The frill can open as wide as 30 centimeters — that's bigger than a dinner plate.
They use their long tail to help them balance when running on two legs.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as your arm — with a huge frill around their neck that pops open like an umbrella!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a loaf of bread — around 1 pound.
text.map_narration: Frilled lizards live in the forests and woodlands of northern Australia and New Guinea.
text.sound_description.young: They make a loud hissing sound when they open their frill to scare away predators.

text.summary.young: Horned lizards are small spiky reptiles that live in the deserts of North America. When a predator gets too close, they can shoot blood from their eyes up to 5 feet away!
text.summary.tiny: Horned lizards have spiky crowns all around their heads. If a hungry fox gets too close, they squirt blood from their eyes!
fun_facts.young: Horned lizards are sometimes called 'horny toads' even though they're lizards, not toads.
They have special grooves on their skin that collect rainwater and channel it straight to their mouth.
When a horned lizard runs, it can stop instantly and freeze like a statue to hide from predators.
The blood they squirt from their eyes tastes bad to predators like coyotes and foxes.
They dig shallow burrows in the sand to sleep in at night and stay cool during hot days.
fun_facts.tiny: They eat hundreds and hundreds of ants every single day.
Their skin has special grooves that catch raindrops and send water right to their mouth.
When they run, they can freeze like a statue to disappear.
did_you_know.young: They can puff up their bodies to look twice as big when they're scared.
They eat mostly ants — sometimes hundreds of ants in a single day!
Their spiky horns are made of the same material as your fingernails.
They can change colour slightly to match the sand and rocks around them.
Baby horned lizards are born with tiny horns already on their heads.
text.size_comparison.young: Only about as long as your finger — a tiny, spiky, flat little dinosaur-lookalike!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as an egg — almost nothing at all.
text.map_narration: Horned lizards live in the deserts and dry grasslands of North America.
text.sound_description.young: They make a quiet hissing sound when they feel threatened or scared.

text.summary.young: Bison are huge, shaggy animals that live on the grasslands of North America. They can run as fast as a horse even though they weigh as much as a small car.
text.summary.tiny: Bison are enormous, shaggy animals with humps on their shoulders. They're as heavy as a car but they can run faster than you can ride your bike!
fun_facts.young: Bison are the largest land animals in North America.
Their thick fur keeps them warm even when it's freezing cold outside.
They roll in the dirt to scratch their backs and keep bugs away.
A bison's hump is made of muscle that helps it push through deep snow.
They can run 55 kilometres per hour — that's faster than most cars in town!
They were almost gone forever, but people worked hard to save them and now there are thousands again.
fun_facts.tiny: They have such thick fur that snow sits right on top without melting.
They roll in dirt patches to scratch their backs and keep bugs away.
A bison's big shoulder hump is actually muscle for pushing through snow.
did_you_know.young: They once roamed in herds of 60 million — the largest animal migration ever!
A bison can jump over a fence that's taller than a grown-up.
Baby bison are called calves and they're born with reddish-orange fur.
They use their massive heads like snowplows to push snow aside and find grass to eat.
They can smell food from three kilometres away.
text.size_comparison.young: Way taller than any grown-up at the shoulder — a massive wall of fur and muscle, around 5 feet 11 inches.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a horse — around 2,000 pounds.
text.map_narration: Bison roam the grasslands and prairies of North America.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep grunting and snorting sounds, and bellow loudly when they're warning others.

text.summary.young: Grizzly bears are huge brown bears that live in forests and mountains across North America and parts of Asia. They can smell food from 30 kilometres away — their nose is seven times stronger than a bloodhound's!
text.summary.tiny: Grizzly bears are enormous brown bears with a huge hump of muscle on their backs. They can smell your picnic from further away than you can see!
fun_facts.young: Grizzly bears love to catch salmon jumping up rivers with their big paws.
Their long claws can be as long as your fingers — perfect for digging up roots!
A grizzly's bite is strong enough to crush a bowling ball.
Baby grizzlies are called cubs and are born while their mother is hibernating.
Grizzlies shake themselves dry just like dogs do after swimming.
They can stand up on their back legs to see and smell better.
fun_facts.tiny: They catch fish by scooping them right out of rivers with their giant paws.
Their claws are as long as your whole hand and perfect for digging.
Baby bears are born tiny while their mum's fast asleep in winter.
did_you_know.young: A grizzly's hump on its back is pure muscle that helps it dig and climb.
Grizzlies can run as fast as a horse — up to 55 kilometres per hour!
They eat both plants and meat, including berries, fish, and even moths.
They can weigh as much as three adult humans put together.
In winter, grizzlies sleep in dens for up to seven months without eating or drinking.
text.size_comparison.young: On all fours, they already reach about your height — around 3 feet 4 inches at the shoulder. Standing up on their hind legs, they're over twice your height!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as three or four grown-ups — around 595 pounds.
text.map_narration: Grizzly bears live in the forests, mountains, and rivers of western North America.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep roars and growls, and huff or grunt when they're curious or annoyed.

text.summary.young: Black bears live in forests across North America. They can be black, brown, cinnamon, or even blonde — not all black bears are actually black!
text.summary.tiny: Black bears aren't always black — they can be brown, cinnamon, or even blonde! They live in forests and love climbing trees.
fun_facts.young: Black bears eat mostly plants, berries, and nuts — meat is only a small part of their diet.
They hibernate in winter, sleeping in dens for up to seven months without eating or drinking.
They have curved claws that work like climbing hooks on trees.
Their sense of smell is seven times better than a bloodhound's!
They sometimes make nests in trees to rest or eat.
Cubs stay with their mother for about a year and a half, learning how to find food and stay safe.
fun_facts.tiny: They sleep through winter in cosy dens without eating or drinking.
They've got curved claws that work like climbing hooks.
They can smell food from farther away than you can walk in a day.
did_you_know.young: They can run as fast as a horse — up to 35 miles per hour!
They can smell food from over a mile away.
They are excellent swimmers and love to play in water.
A mother black bear usually has two or three cubs at a time.
They can climb trees in just seconds, even when they weigh over 300 pounds!
text.size_comparison.young: On all fours, they reach right up to your chin — around 2 feet 11 inches at the shoulder. Standing on their hind legs, they tower over you!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as two grown-ups — around 287 pounds.
text.map_narration: Black bears live in the forests across North America, from Canada to Mexico.
text.sound_description.young: They growl, huff when they're nervous, and grunt softly to their cubs.

text.summary.young: Moose are the biggest deer in the world and live in cold forests across North America, Europe, and Asia. They are excellent swimmers and can dive over 5 metres deep underwater to munch on tasty plants growing at the bottom of lakes.
text.summary.tiny: Moose are the biggest deer in the whole world. They're amazing swimmers and can dive underwater to eat plants from the bottom of lakes.
fun_facts.young: Moose have a flap of skin hanging under their chin called a bell — scientists aren't sure what it's for but it makes them look fancy.
Their long legs help them walk through deep snow that would trap most other animals.
They love to eat plants from the bottom of lakes and can hold their breath underwater for a whole minute.
Male moose crash their antlers together in autumn to see who's the strongest — it sounds like two baseball bats smashing.
They have terrible eyesight but amazing hearing and smell — they can smell you from far away even if they can't see you.
A moose's favourite foods are willow branches, water lilies, and pond weeds.
fun_facts.tiny: They have a flap of skin hanging under their chin called a bell — nobody knows what it's for.
Their long legs let them walk through snow as deep as your waist.
Male moose crash their antlers together in autumn — it sounds like baseball bats smashing.
did_you_know.young: A moose can swim as fast as two Olympic swimmers racing side by side.
Male moose grow enormous antlers that can be as wide as a car — then they fall off every winter and grow back even bigger the next year.
They have special hollow hairs that trap air and help them float like a life jacket when they swim.
A moose can eat up to 30 kilograms of plants in a single day — that's like eating 120 bowls of salad.
Baby moose can outrun a human by the time they're just five days old.
text.size_comparison.young: The tallest animal in North America — way taller than any grown-up, around 6 feet at the shoulder. With antlers, even taller!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a horse — around 1,200 pounds.
text.map_narration: Moose live in the northern forests of North America, Europe, and Asia.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep bellowing calls that sound like a loud groan mixed with a honk — males bellow during autumn to attract females.

text.summary.young: Elk are large deer with brown fur that live in forests and meadows across North America and Asia. Male elk grow huge antlers that can sprout over 2 centimeters every single day — the fastest-growing tissue of any mammal on Earth.
text.summary.tiny: Elk are huge deer with brown fur that grow enormous antlers. Male elk grow their antlers faster than any other bone on Earth — they can sprout as long as your thumb in just one day!
fun_facts.young: Male elk bugle during mating season — their call sounds like a high whistle mixed with a roar and can be heard up to 5 kilometers away.
They eat grass, plants, and tree bark — munching for many hours each day to fill their big bellies.
In summer, elk live high up in cool mountains, but in winter they walk down to valleys where there's less snow.
They have a special stomach with four parts that helps them digest tough plants.
Female elk live in herds with their babies while males often wander alone or in small groups.
They roll in muddy wallows to cool off and protect their skin from biting insects.
fun_facts.tiny: Male elk bugle — it's a high whistle that turns into a roar and travels as far as your eyes can see.
They munch grass and plants for hours every day to fill their big bellies.
Baby elk can stand up and walk just twenty minutes after being born!
did_you_know.young: Male elk shed their antlers every winter and grow brand new ones in spring.
They can run as fast as a car in a neighborhood — up to 45 kilometers per hour!
A male elk's antlers can weigh as much as 18 kilograms — that's like carrying three bowling balls on your head!
They are excellent swimmers and often cross rivers to find food.
Baby elk can stand up and walk just 20 minutes after being born.
text.size_comparison.young: Already taller than you on all fours — about 4 feet 9 inches at the shoulder. Add their huge antlers on top, and they're truly massive!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as three or four grown-ups — around 662 pounds.
text.map_narration: Elk roam the forests and meadows of western North America and eastern Asia.
text.sound_description.young: They make a high-pitched bugle call that starts as a whistle and ends in a deep roar.

text.summary.young: Cougars are big wild cats that live in forests and mountains across North and South America. They can jump farther than any other cat — up to 12 metres in one leap, which is longer than a school bus!
text.summary.tiny: Cougars are big wild cats that can jump longer than a car. They purr and chirp just like your cat at home!
fun_facts.young: Cougars have the longest back legs compared to their front legs of any cat, which helps them jump so far.
A cougar can run as fast as a car in a school zone — up to 80 kilometres per hour for short distances.
They are mostly active at dawn and dusk when their prey is feeding.
Despite being big cats, cougars almost never attack people and usually hide when they see humans.
They mark their territory by scratching trees and leaving scent markers, just like house cats scratch furniture.
A cougar's tail is almost as long as its body and helps it balance when jumping and climbing.
fun_facts.tiny: A cougar's back legs are longer than its front legs — that's why it can jump so far.
They are mostly awake at sunrise and sunset when it's not too bright.
Baby cougars have spots that disappear as they grow up.
did_you_know.young: They can't roar like lions — instead they purr, meow, and chirp just like a pet cat!
They hold the world record for the animal with the most names — over 40 different names in English alone, including puma, mountain lion, and panther.
A cougar can jump 12 metres forward in a single leap — that's as long as a big school bus.
They are excellent climbers and sometimes drag their prey up into trees to keep it safe from other animals.
Baby cougars are born with spots and blue eyes, but the spots disappear as they grow up.
text.size_comparison.young: Sleek and powerful, they reach your shoulders — around 2 feet 6 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a grown-up — around 154 pounds.
text.map_narration: Cougars live across the Americas, from the Canadian Rockies all the way to Patagonia.
text.sound_description.young: They make growling sounds, loud purrs, and high-pitched chirps to communicate.

bobcat.name: Bobcat
bobcat.habitat: Forests, deserts, swamps, and mountains across North America

text.summary.young: Bobcats are wild cats with spotted fur and short tails that live across North America. They can leap 3 metres in a single jump to catch rabbits and birds.
text.summary.tiny: Bobcats are wild cats with spotted coats and stubby tails that look snipped short. They're brilliant jumpers and can leap as far as a small car.
fun_facts.young: Bobcats have tufts of black fur on the tips of their ears that help them hear better.
Their spotted coat works like camouflage to hide them in forests and grasslands.
They are very quiet and secretive — you could live near one and never see it.
They can run up to 50 kilometres per hour in short bursts when chasing prey.
Baby bobcats are called kittens and stay with their mother for almost a year.
They live alone and only meet up with other bobcats to have babies.
fun_facts.tiny: They've got little black brushes on their ear tips that work like nature's hearing aids.
Their spotty coat helps them disappear into forests and meadows like magic.
They are so sneaky and quiet that one might live near you and you'd never know.
did_you_know.young: They get their name from their short, 'bobbed' tail that looks like it's been cut off.
They have excellent hearing and can rotate their ears to pinpoint exactly where a mouse is hiding.
They are mostly active at dawn and dusk when their prey comes out to eat.
A bobcat can take down prey much larger than itself, like deer.
They're amazing climbers and sometimes rest in trees during the day.
text.size_comparison.young: On all fours, they reach your belly — around 2 feet at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a big watermelon — around 22 pounds.
text.map_narration: Bobcats live in the forests, deserts, and swamps of North America.
text.sound_description.young: They growl, hiss when angry, and make loud yowling cries to talk to other bobcats.

text.summary.young: Red foxes live in forests, grasslands, and cities across Europe, Asia, North America, Africa, and Australia. They can sense Earth's magnetic field and use it like a compass to help them pounce on prey hiding under the snow.
text.summary.tiny: Foxes can feel where north is, just like magic. They use this special power to jump through snow and catch dinner hiding underneath.
fun_facts.young: Red foxes can run up to 30 miles per hour when chasing prey or escaping danger.
A red fox's pupils are vertical slits, like a cat's eyes, which helps them see well at night.
They make over 40 different sounds to talk to each other.
They wrap their bushy tails around themselves like a blanket to stay warm in winter.
They are great jumpers and can leap over fences taller than a grown-up.
They live in underground dens called earths that have many tunnels and rooms.
fun_facts.tiny: A fox's eyes have slits like a cat's so they can hunt in the dark.
Foxes talk to each other with more sounds than you can count on your fingers and toes.
Their big fluffy tail wraps around them like your favourite blanket.
did_you_know.young: They can hear a mouse squeaking from 100 feet away.
A red fox's tail is called a brush and helps them balance when running.
They sometimes bury extra food to save it for later, like a secret snack stash.
Baby foxes are called kits and are born with dark brown fur that turns red as they grow.
They have whiskers on their legs that help them find their way in the dark.
text.size_comparison.young: Smaller than most people think — right at above your knees, around 1 foot 4 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bowling ball — around 13 pounds.
text.map_narration: Red foxes live across North America, Europe, Asia, and even parts of Australia.
text.sound_description.young: They make sharp barks and high-pitched screams that sound spooky at night.

coyote.name: Coyote
coyote.habitat: forests, deserts, grasslands, mountains, and cities

text.summary.young: Coyotes are wild dogs that live all across North America, from snowy Canada to hot Mexico. They are so adaptable that they've spread to more places even while humans tried to hunt them — no other large animal has done this!
text.summary.tiny: Coyotes are clever wild dogs that sing to each other at night. They live everywhere from snowy mountains to busy cities — they're brilliant at finding new homes.
fun_facts.young: Coyotes eat almost anything — mice, rabbits, fruit, insects, and even garbage.
A coyote can jump over a 6-foot fence.
They have 42 teeth — that's 10 more than humans!
They use at least 11 different sounds to communicate with each other.
They can swim well and sometimes catch fish.
Their fur changes color with the seasons to help them hide better.
fun_facts.tiny: They eat mice and rabbits and berries and even leftover sandwiches.
They can leap right over a fence as tall as your dad.
A coyote makes at least eleven different sounds to talk to its family.
did_you_know.young: They can run up to 40 miles per hour when chasing prey.
A coyote's howl can be heard up to 3 miles away.
They have been seen living in big cities like Los Angeles and New York.
Baby coyotes are called pups and are born with their eyes closed.
They mate for life and raise their pups together.
text.size_comparison.young: On all fours, they reach your belly — around 1 foot 11 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about the same as you — around 31 pounds.
text.map_narration: Coyotes live across North America, from forests and prairies to city suburbs.
text.sound_description.young: They make a famous howling sound that starts high and gets lower, often joined by yips and barks.

text.summary.young: Raccoons are clever masked animals that live in forests, cities, and parks across North America. Their front paws become five times more sensitive when wet, so they dip food in water to feel it better — that's why it looks like they're washing!
text.summary.tiny: Raccoons wear black masks like little bandits and have the cleverest paws in the forest. They dip their food in water to feel it better — it looks like washing but they're really just using their super-sensitive fingers!
fun_facts.young: Raccoons have super-sensitive fingers with more touch receptors than most animals.
They can run up to 15 miles per hour when they need to escape danger.
They are excellent swimmers and can stay in water for several hours.
Their bushy tails help them balance when climbing high up in trees.
They can eat almost anything — fruits, nuts, insects, fish, and even garbage.
They make their dens in hollow trees, caves, or even attics and chimneys!
fun_facts.tiny: They can open jars and unlatch gates with their clever paws.
Their bushy tails help them balance when they climb high up in trees.
They can eat almost anything — fruits, nuts, insects, fish, and even your rubbish!
did_you_know.young: They can open jars, unlatch gates, and even turn doorknobs with their clever paws.
A raccoon's black mask helps reduce glare from lights at night — like tiny superhero goggles!
They can rotate their back feet 180 degrees to climb down trees headfirst.
Baby raccoons are called kits, and they stay with their mom for about a year.
They remember solutions to problems for up to three years — they never forget a good trick!
text.size_comparison.young: Standing on all fours, they only come up to your knees — around 1 foot at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a bowling ball — around 18 pounds.
text.map_narration: Raccoons live across North America, from forests to cities.
text.sound_description.young: They make chittering and purring sounds when they're happy, and growl when they're scared or angry.

beaver.name: Beaver
beaver.habitat: Rivers, lakes, and streams with trees nearby

text.summary.young: Beavers are large rodents that live near rivers and lakes in North America and Europe. They use their strong teeth to cut down trees and build dams that create ponds — changing entire landscapes like nature's engineers.
text.summary.tiny: Beavers chew down trees with their orange teeth and build dams that turn rivers into ponds. They're nature's builders, making homes from sticks and changing whole forests.
fun_facts.young: Beavers are the second-largest rodents in the world — only capybaras are bigger!
A beaver can cut down a small tree in just five minutes using only its teeth.
Their teeth are orange because they have special iron in them that makes them extra strong.
They build underwater tunnels so they can swim into their lodge without being seen.
A beaver family works together — parents, babies, and older siblings all help build and repair the dam.
They eat bark, leaves, and water plants — they especially love willow and aspen trees.
fun_facts.tiny: A beaver can chop down a thin tree in five minutes using just its teeth.
They have orange teeth because they've got iron inside them to make them super strong.
Baby beavers stay with their family for two years, helping fix the dam and learning to build.
did_you_know.young: A beaver's teeth never stop growing, so they must keep chewing to wear them down.
Their dams can be over 800 meters long — longer than eight football fields!
They can hold their breath underwater for 15 minutes while they work.
A beaver's tail is flat like a paddle and helps them steer when swimming.
They slap their tail on the water to warn their family of danger.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as a big pillow — with a wide, flat tail like a paddle.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a big bag of dog food — around 55 pounds.
text.map_narration: Beavers live near rivers, streams, and ponds across North America and Europe.
text.sound_description.young: They make soft chattering sounds with their teeth and slap their flat tails loudly on the water to warn others.

text.summary.young: Mountain goats live high in the rocky mountains of North America. They can balance on tiny ledges just 5 cm wide — narrower than your hand!
text.summary.tiny: Mountain goats live high in the rocky mountains where hardly any other animals can go. They can balance on ledges narrower than your hand!
fun_facts.young: Mountain goats have two toes on each hoof that can spread apart to help them grip rocky surfaces.
They live higher up mountains than almost any other animal in North America.
Their thick white coat has two layers — woolly fur underneath and long guard hairs on top.
They can climb slopes so steep that predators like bears and wolves can't follow them.
They lick rocks and soil to get salt and minerals their bodies need.
Males grow beards and have horns that curve backward like little daggers.
fun_facts.tiny: Their hooves spread apart like fingers to grip the rocks.
Baby mountain goats can climb steep cliffs when they're just one day old.
They're not really goats — they're more like antelopes!
did_you_know.young: Their hooves work like climbing shoes — hard edges grip the rock and soft pads inside stick to smooth surfaces.
They can jump up to 3.5 meters in a single leap to reach the next ledge.
They aren't actually goats — they're more closely related to antelopes!
Their white fur is so thick that they can survive in freezing mountain winds and snow.
Baby mountain goats, called kids, can climb steep cliffs when they're just one day old.
text.size_comparison.young: On all fours, they reach right up to your chin — around 2 feet 11 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a grown-up — around 154 pounds.
text.map_narration: Mountain goats live high up in the Rocky Mountains of North America.
text.sound_description.young: They make bleating sounds like a sheep and snort when they're alarmed.

text.summary.young: Arctic foxes live in the coldest places on Earth — the snowy Arctic. Their fur changes color with the seasons: white in winter to hide in snow, and brown in summer to blend with the rocky ground.
text.summary.tiny: Arctic foxes live in the coldest, snowiest places on Earth. Their fur is white in winter and brown in summer.
fun_facts.young: An Arctic fox's paws are covered in thick fur to keep them warm on ice.
They build dens with tunnels that can be over 100 years old.
Arctic foxes are only about the size of a house cat.
They can run up to 50 kilometres per hour.
They eat lemmings, birds, fish, and even berries.
Their ears are small and round to keep heat from escaping.
fun_facts.tiny: They're about as big as your family cat.
Their fluffy tail works like a cozy blanket when they curl up to sleep.
They can hear tiny animals moving under the snow.
did_you_know.young: They have the warmest fur of any mammal on Earth.
Their thick, fluffy tail works like a blanket when they sleep.
They can hear lemmings moving under the snow.
They can survive temperatures as cold as -70°C.
They sometimes follow polar bears to eat leftover food.
text.size_comparison.young: Small and fluffy, they only stand your knees — around 11 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a house cat — around 8 pounds.
text.map_narration: Arctic foxes live in the frozen tundra around the Arctic, including Canada, Alaska, and Scandinavia.
text.sound_description.young: They make high-pitched barks and howls to talk to each other.

text.summary.young: Wolverines are fierce, stocky animals that live in cold forests and mountains across North America, Europe, and Asia. They can take down prey ten times their size and have even been known to scare grizzly bears away from food.
text.summary.tiny: Wolverines are brave, strong animals with thick brown fur and huge paws. They're so fierce they can scare bears away from dinner!
fun_facts.young: Wolverines are part of the weasel family, like otters and badgers.
They mark their territory with a strong scent that tells other wolverines to stay away.
They cache their food by burying it in snow to eat later.
Their scientific name Gulo gulo means glutton glutton because they eat so much when they find food.
Baby wolverines are called kits and stay with their mother for about two years.
They have thick fur on the bottom of their paws to keep their feet warm in the snow.
fun_facts.tiny: They have special fur that ice and snow slide right off.
Their enormous paws work like snowshoes so they don't sink in deep snow.
They can smell food buried deeper than you are tall!
did_you_know.young: They have special teeth that can crunch through frozen meat and bones in winter.
A wolverine's fur is so special that frost and ice won't stick to it.
They can smell food buried under six feet of snow.
They have huge paws that work like snowshoes to help them walk on deep snow.
They can travel over 15 miles in a single day searching for food.
text.size_comparison.young: Compact and powerful — right at your hips, around 1 foot 6 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about the same as you — around 31 pounds.
text.map_narration: Wolverines live in the remote forests and tundra of northern North America, Europe, and Asia.
text.sound_description.young: They make deep growls, fierce snarls, and loud hisses when they feel threatened.

text.summary.young: Prairie dogs are small, chatty rodents that live in underground towns across the grasslands of North America. They have the most complex animal language ever discovered — their alarm calls can describe the exact colour, size, and speed of danger heading their way.
text.summary.tiny: Prairie dogs are chatty little diggers that live in underground towns across the grasslands. They've got the cleverest animal language ever — their barks can describe exactly what danger looks like.
fun_facts.young: Prairie dogs are named after their dog-like barking sounds
Their tunnels can be as long as a school bus
They eat grass, seeds, roots, and flowers
They stand up on their back legs to see over the tall grass
They flick their tails to signal different warnings to their family
Baby prairie dogs are called pups and stay underground for six weeks after they're born
fun_facts.tiny: They're named after their dog-like barking sounds.
Their tunnels can be as long as a school bus.
They stand on their back legs to peek over tall grass.
did_you_know.young: They kiss and hug each other to say hello
A prairie dog town can have thousands of animals living together
They build separate rooms underground for sleeping, eating, and going to the bathroom
They can describe a tall person in a blue shirt differently than a short person in a yellow shirt — just by changing their call
They post guards at tunnel entrances to watch for danger while others eat
text.size_comparison.young: About as tall as a school ruler when they stand up on their hind legs!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a carton of milk — around 2 pounds.
text.map_narration: Prairie dogs live in the grasslands and prairies of central North America.
text.sound_description.young: They make sharp barking sounds to warn their friends about danger.

alligator_snapping_turtle.name: Alligator Snapping Turtle
alligator_snapping_turtle.habitat: Rivers and swamps in North America

text.summary.young: Alligator snapping turtles are huge turtles that live in rivers and swamps in North America. They wiggle their pink tongue like a worm to trick fish into swimming right into their mouth!
text.summary.tiny: Alligator snapping turtles wiggle their pink tongue like a worm to trick fish into swimming right into their mouth! They're huge turtles that live in rivers and swamps.
fun_facts.young: They barely move when hunting — they just sit still and wiggle their tongue
Their tongue looks exactly like a juicy pink worm
They spend most of their life underwater
They have three big ridges on their shell that look like mountain ranges
Baby alligator snapping turtles are only as big as a ping pong ball
They eat fish, snails, frogs, and even other turtles
fun_facts.tiny: Their tongue looks exactly like a juicy pink worm.
They have three big ridges on their shell that look like mountains.
Baby alligator snapping turtles are only as big as a ping pong ball.
did_you_know.young: Their bite is strong enough to snap through bone
They can hold their breath underwater for up to 50 minutes
They're one of the heaviest freshwater turtles in the world
Their spiky shell looks like an alligator's back
They can live longer than most humans
text.size_comparison.young: Their shell is about as wide as a big pillow — and they have a jaw strong enough to snap a broomstick!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a grown-up — around 176 pounds.
text.map_narration: Alligator snapping turtles live in the rivers, lakes, and swamps of the southeastern United States.
text.sound_description.young: They make a loud snapping sound with their powerful jaws and can hiss when threatened.

roadrunner.name: Roadrunner
roadrunner.habitat: Deserts and scrublands of southwestern North America

text.summary.young: Roadrunners are swift ground birds that live in the deserts and scrublands of North America. They're fast enough to catch and kill rattlesnakes by grabbing them and slamming them against rocks.
text.summary.tiny: Roadrunners are desert birds that run faster than you can ride your bike. They're brave enough to catch rattlesnakes and bash them on rocks.
fun_facts.young: A roadrunner will grab a rattlesnake by the tail, whip it around, and smash its head on a rock.
They eat scorpions, tarantulas, and lizards without getting hurt by stings or bites.
Roadrunners make a cooing sound that gets lower and slower, not a 'beep beep' like in cartoons.
They have a patch of bare blue and orange skin behind each eye that they can puff up when excited.
They build stick nests in cacti or thorny bushes to keep eggs safe from predators.
They can jump straight up in the air to snatch dragonflies and butterflies.
fun_facts.tiny: They eat scorpions and tarantulas without getting hurt.
They jump straight up to catch butterflies in the air.
They have bright blue and orange skin behind their eyes that puffs up when they're excited.
did_you_know.young: They can run up to 26 miles per hour — faster than most people can sprint!
They rarely fly because running uses less energy in the hot desert.
They have two toes pointing forward and two pointing backward to help them run on sand.
They cool down by panting like a dog and fluttering their throat.
They can lower their body temperature at night to save energy, then warm up in the morning sun.
text.size_comparison.young: About as long as your arm — they zip along the ground faster than most people can run!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as an apple — around 14 ounces.
text.map_narration: Roadrunners live in the deserts and scrublands of the southwestern United States and Mexico.
text.sound_description.young: They make a cooing sound that starts high and slides down lower and slower, plus they clack their beaks together.

text.summary.young: Ocelots are small wild cats with beautiful spotted coats that live in the rainforests and grasslands of Central and South America. Their fur lies flat in either direction, which helps them squeeze silently through thick jungle plants without making a sound.
text.summary.tiny: Ocelots are wild cats covered in spots and swirls that look like tiny paintings. Their fur lies flat in any direction, so they slip through the jungle without a whisper.
fun_facts.young: Ocelots can jump up to 6 feet straight up in the air to catch birds.
An ocelot will sometimes drag its prey up into a tree to eat in peace.
Baby ocelots are born with their eyes closed and don't open them for about two weeks.
They mark their territory by scratching trees and rubbing their cheeks on branches.
These spotted cats can eat porcupines by carefully avoiding the sharp quills.
They are sometimes called 'painted leopards' because their coats look like tiny works of art.
fun_facts.tiny: They can leap as high as your bedroom ceiling to snatch birds from the air.
They turn their ankles backwards to climb down trees headfirst, just like squirrels do.
No two ocelots have the same pattern — each one's coat is as special as your fingerprints.
did_you_know.young: They are excellent swimmers and often hunt for fish in rivers and streams.
An ocelot's spotted coat is like a fingerprint — no two ocelots have exactly the same pattern.
They can turn their ankles backwards to climb down trees headfirst, just like squirrels.
These cats spend most of their time alone and only meet other ocelots to have babies.
They have much larger eyes than house cats, which help them see clearly at night when they hunt.
text.size_comparison.young: On all fours, they stand your hips — around 1 foot 8 inches at the shoulder.
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as a big watermelon — around 26 pounds.
text.map_narration: Ocelots live in the forests and scrublands of Central and South America and the southern United States.
text.sound_description.young: They meow and purr like house cats, but they also make louder growling and hissing sounds when they want to scare away other animals.

polar_bear.name: Polar Bear
polar_bear.habitat: Arctic sea ice and frozen coasts

text.summary.young: Polar bears are huge white bears that live in the freezing Arctic where sea ice covers the ocean. Their fur looks white, but each hair is actually hollow and see-through like a tiny straw, helping trap warmth from the sun against their black skin underneath.
text.summary.tiny: Polar bears are huge white bears that live where the freezing ocean is covered in ice. Their fur looks white, but it's actually see-through like tiny straws that trap sunshine against their black skin.
fun_facts.young: Polar bears are amazing swimmers and can paddle for days without stopping.
Baby polar bears are born tiny — about the size of a guinea pig!
They don't drink water — they get all the water they need from the seals they eat.
Their scientific name means 'sea bear' because they spend so much time swimming in the ocean.
They clean themselves by rolling in the snow like it's a giant bathtub.
When a polar bear gets too hot, it goes for a swim in the icy water to cool down!
fun_facts.tiny: They can swim for days without stopping.
Baby polar bears are born tiny — about as big as a guinea pig!
They clean themselves by rolling in the snow like it's a giant bath.
did_you_know.young: Their fur isn't really white — each hair is clear and hollow like a tiny tube!
Under all that fur, polar bears have jet-black skin that soaks up heat from the sun.
They are the biggest meat-eating land animals on Earth.
A polar bear's paws are as wide as dinner plates to help them walk on thin ice without breaking through.
They can smell a seal from 20 miles away — even when it's hiding under thick ice!
text.size_comparison.young: On all fours, they're already way taller than you at the shoulder — about 4 feet 4 inches. Standing on their hind legs, they're taller than a door!
text.weight_comparison.young: They weigh about as much as five or six grown-ups — around 1100 pounds.
text.map_narration: Polar bears live on the sea ice and coastlines of the Arctic.
text.sound_description.young: They roar and growl loudly, and make soft chuffing sounds when they're happy or talking to their cubs.

arctic_wolf.name: Arctic Wolf
arctic_wolf.habitat: frozen Arctic tundra and ice fields

text.summary.young: Arctic Wolves live in the coldest, most frozen places on Earth — the High Arctic of Canada and Greenland. They are the only wolves in the world that are not threatened by humans because almost no people live where they do.
text.summary.tiny: Arctic Wolves live in the coldest, snowiest places on Earth where almost no people go. Their thick white fur keeps them warm in blizzards and helps them hide in the snow.
fun_facts.young: Arctic Wolves have fur on the bottom of their paws to keep their feet warm on ice.
A pack of Arctic Wolves can travel 30 miles in a single day looking for food.
They work together as a team to hunt animals much bigger than themselves, like musk oxen.
Arctic Wolves howl to talk to each other across the snowy wilderness.
In the High Arctic, the sun doesn't set for months in summer — Arctic Wolves hunt in 24-hour daylight!
Their thick double coat is so warm they can sleep outside in blizzards.
fun_facts.tiny: They've got fur on the bottoms of their paws to keep their feet warm on ice.
A pack can travel as far as your town to the next town in just one day looking for food.
In summer up in the High Arctic, the sun never sets — they hunt in daylight all day and all night!
did_you_know.young: Arctic Wolves can survive in temperatures colder than your freezer — down to minus 70 degrees!
Their white fur helps them hide in the snow when they hunt.
Arctic Wolves can go days without eating, then eat 20 pounds of meat in one meal.
They have small ears and short noses to keep warm in the freezing cold.
